name: Passu Peak
name_ur: پسو سر‬
short_description: Mountain
description: Passu Sar is a mountain peak in the Batura Muztagh, a sub-range of the Karakoram mountain range, in the Hunza District of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. It is the high point of the Passu massif, which also includes Passu Diar. The peak lies on the main ridge of the Batura Muztagh, about 7 km (4.3 mi) east of Batura Sar.

name: Kunyang Chhish
name_ur: کنیانگ چھش
short_description: Notable nature site located in Nagar District.
description: Kunyang Chhish is the second-highest mountain in the Hispar Muztagh, a subrange in the Karakoram mountains in Pakistan. Alternative variations of the name are Kunyang Kish and Khinyang Chhish. Its height, also sometimes given as 7,823 metres (25,666 ft), is ranked 21st in the world.

name: Yutmaru Glacier
name_ur: یتمارو گلیشیر
short_description: Notable nature site located in Nagar District.
description: Glacier in Pakistan

name: Passu Cones Viewpoint
name_ur: پسو کونز
short_description: Cathedral-like spires of Tupopdan peak above the KKH.
description: The jagged Passu Cones are one of the most photographed views in Pakistan, rising above the Karakoram Highway.
history: Tupopdan peak is part of the Karakoram range.
significance: Iconic Karakoram scenery.
culture: Wakhi culture predominates in Gojal.
local_customs: Do not stop on dangerous road bends.
food: Simple cafes in Passu.
shopping: None.
tips: Sunrise and sunset light are best.

name: Abruzzi Glacier
name_ur: آبروزي گلیشیر
short_description: Notable nature site located in Shigar District.
description: The Abruzzi Glacier is located north of the Baltoro Kangri in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. The glacier flows northwest before turning westwards and eventually merges with the Baltoro Glacier, one of the largest glaciers outside of the polar regions. From its upper reaches, the glacier offers striking views of K2, the second-highest mountain in the world and the highest in Pakistan.

derivative work: Rupert Pupkin (talk)

name: Biarchedi
name_ur: بیارچیڈی
short_description: Notable nature site located in Shigar District.
description: Biarchedi Peak is a mountain peak on the south of the Baltoro Glacier in Pakistan.

name: Gasherbrum III
name_ur: گاشر برم سوم
short_description: Mountain
description: Gasherbrum III, surveyed as K3a, is a summit in the Gasherbrum massif of the Baltoro Muztagh, a subrange of the Karakoram on the border between Xinjiang, China and Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. It is situated between Gasherbrum II and IV.

name: Gasherbrum IV
name_ur: گاشر برم چہارم
short_description: Mountain
description: Gasherbrum IV, originally surveyed as K3, is the 17th highest mountain on Earth and the 6th highest in Pakistan, as well as the highest independent mountain under eight thousand metres in Pakistan.

name: Mubarak Haveli (Bhati Gate)
name_ur: مبارک حویلی اندرون بھاٹی گیٹ لاہور
short_description: Grand 18th-century Mughal haveli where the Koh-i-Noor diamond was surrendered to Maharaja Ranjit Singh.
description: Constructed during the reign of Muhammad Shah, this sprawling courtyard haveli witnessed pivotal historical events, including the surrender of the Koh-i-Noor diamond in 1813.

name: Gasherbrum V
name_ur: گاشر برم پنجم
short_description: Mountain in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan
description: Gasherbrum V is a mountain in the Gasherbrum massif, located in the Karakoram range in Gilgit–Baltistan, Pakistan.
image_credit: Florian Ederer released the original version into public domain.

name: Trango Monk
name_ur: ٹرانگو مونک
short_description: Natural landmark in Shigar District
description: Natural landmark in Shigar District

name: Trango Tower
name_ur: ٹرانگو ٹاور
short_description: Natural landmark in Shigar District
description: Natural landmark in Shigar District

name: Rakaposhi
name_ur: راکاپوشی‬‎
short_description: Notable nature site located in Sikandarabad.
description: Rakaposhi also known as Dumani is a mountain within the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan. It is situated in the middle of the Nagar and Bagrote valleys. The mountain is extremely broad, measuring almost 20 kilometres (12 mi) from east to west. It is the only peak on earth that descends directly and without interruption for almost 6,000 metres from its summit to its base.

name: K2 Italian expeditions museum
name_ur: کے ٹو اطالوی مہمات عجائب گھر
short_description: Museum in Skardu
description: Museum in Skardu

name: Kharphocho Fort
name_ur: قلعہ سکردو
short_description: Historic site in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan
description: Skardu Fort or Kharpocho is a fort in Skardu in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan. It mainly served as a military stronghold and strategic lookout. It is situated above the junction of Indus and Shigar rivers, overlooking the Rock of Skardu.

name: Shangrila Resort (Lower Kachura Lake)
name_ur: شنگریلا ریزورٹ
short_description: Lakeside resort known as Heaven on Earth near Skardu.
description: Lower Kachura Lake, home to the Shangrila Resort, is a calm lake ringed by orchards and mountains.
history: The resort was developed in the 1980s and gained fame for its pagoda-style buildings.
significance: Gateway to the high peaks of the Karakoram.
culture: Balti culture predominates in Skardu.
local_customs: Respect private resort areas.
food: Trout and apricot dishes.
shopping: Dry fruit and gemstones in Skardu bazaar.
tips: Combine with Upper Kachura Lake.
entry_fee: Small entry fee to the resort.

name: Deosai National Park
name_ur: دیوسائی قومی پارک
short_description: Notable nature site located in Skardu District.
description: Deosai National Park is a high-elevation national park located on an alpine plain between the Skardu District and Astore District in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. Lying to the east of Nanga Parbat in the western Himalayas close to the central Karakoram Range and surrounded by Deosai Mountains, the national park is in the tentative list under World Heritage Site of Pakistan.

name: Kutiah Lungma Glacier
name_ur: کوتیا لنگما گلیشیئر
short_description: Notable nature site located in Skardu District.
description: Kutiah Lungma Glacier is a glacier that stretches for approximately 12 km in length and has a width of about 3 km. It is situated within the Karakoram mountain range in the Stak Valley of District Skardu, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. This glacier is located in the Stak Valley, which is sometimes referred to as Staq, and it falls within the subdivision of Roundu in district Skardu, Gilgit-Baltistan.

name: Karun Koh
name_ur: قارون کوہ
short_description: Mountain peak
description: Karun Kuh is a mountain located in the area of Shimshal Valley, a valley in the Karakoram range of Asia. Located in the area of Shimshal, Gilgit–Baltistan, Pakistan, it has a summit elevation of 6,977 m above sea level.

name: Tupopdan
name_ur: توپوپدان
short_description: Notable nature site located in Sost.
description: Tupopdan, also known as Passu Cathedral or Passu Cones, is a mountain in northern Pakistan.

name: Islamabad Museum
name_ur: اسلام آباد میوزیم
short_description: Museum in Blue Area
description: Museum in Blue Area

name: Islamabad Zoo
name_ur: اسلام آباد چڑیا گھر
short_description: Zoo in Islamabad, Pakistan
description: Islamabad Zoo, previously Marghazar Zoo, was a 33-hectare (82-acre) zoo in Islamabad Capital Territory. It was opened in 1978, and was under the administration of Capital Development Authority of Pakistan before its closure in December 2020 due to its mistreatment of animals.

name: Margalla Hills National Park
name_ur: مارگلہ ہل قومی پارک
short_description: Notable nature site located in Blue Area.
description: Margalla Hills National Park is a national park in Pakistan located in Islamabad Capital Territory, near its northern boundary with Haripur District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The park includes the Margalla Hills, which form the foothills of the Himalayas, along with Shakarparian Park and Rawal Lake.

name: Golra Sharif Railway Museum
name_ur: گولڑہ شریف ریلوے عجائب گھر
short_description: Notable museum site located in Golra Sharif.
description: Golra Sharif Railway Museum, also known as Pakistan Railways Heritage Museum, is a railway museum located near Sector F-13 of Islamabad, Pakistan. It is located at the Golra Sharif railway station, a junction station in the Rawalpindi Division of Pakistan Railways, located at 1,994 feet above sea level, in the southeast of the Margalla Hills and east of the cradle of Gandhara civilization, the ancient city of Taxila.

name: Daman-e-Koh Viewpoint
name_ur: دامنِ کوہ
short_description: Hilltop garden with panoramic views over Islamabad.
description: A terraced viewpoint in the Margalla Hills offering sweeping views of Islamabad, Faisal Mosque and Rawal Lake.
history: Developed as a public viewpoint as Islamabad was planned in the 1960s.
significance: The best panoramic view of the planned capital.
culture: A favourite family spot, with monkeys in the trees.
local_customs: Do not feed the monkeys.
food: Snack kiosks and a cafe on site.
shopping: Few shops.
tips: Clear days after rain give the best views.

name: Lok Virsa Heritage Museum
name_ur: لوک ورثہ میوزیم
short_description: Folk heritage museum of Pakistan's crafts, costumes and music.
description: Lok Virsa showcases the living folk traditions of Pakistan's regions with dioramas, embroidery, musical instruments and woodwork.
history: Established as the National Institute of Folk and Traditional Heritage in 1974.
significance: The best single overview of Pakistan's regional cultures.
culture: Regular craft festivals bring artisans from across the country.
local_customs: Photography may be restricted in some halls.
food: Food stalls during festivals.
shopping: Handicrafts shop with authentic regional crafts.
tips: Check for the annual Lok Mela festival.
opening_hours: About 10 AM to 6 PM, closed Mondays.

name: Margalla Hills Trail 3
name_ur: مارگلہ ٹریل 3
short_description: Popular hiking trail climbing to viewpoints in Margalla Hills National Park.
description: A steep, well-used trail starting in F-6 that climbs through forest to viewpoints and continues towards Pir Sohawa.
history: Part of Margalla Hills National Park, established in 1980.
significance: Shows the biodiversity of the Himalayan foothills.
culture: Early morning hikes are a local tradition.
local_customs: Stay on the trail; carry water and avoid hiking alone at dusk.
food: Bring your own snacks.
shopping: None.
tips: Start early in summer to avoid heat.
opening_hours: Open from dawn; avoid after dark.

name: Chughtai Museum (National Artist Heritage)
name_ur: چغتائی میوزیم گارڈن ٹاؤن لاہور
short_description: Dedicated art museum showcasing the masterworks, etchings, and miniature paintings of Abdur Rahman Chughtai.
description: Preserving over a thousand original watercolor paintings, prints, and pencil sketches, this serene museum celebrates the visionary who melded Mughal miniature traditions with Art Nouveau.

name: Shakir Ali Museum (Tipu Block Garden Town)
name_ur: شاکر علی میوزیم ٹیپو بلاک گارڈن ٹاؤن لاہور
short_description: Artistic red-brick home of pioneer modernist painter Shakir Ali, preserved as a public gallery and research center.
description: Designed and constructed with exposed burnt bricks and terracotta arches by the artist himself, this sanctuary displays his iconic cubist paintings, personal easel, and collection of folk sculptures.

name: Tollington Market Heritage Arts Complex
name_ur: ٹولنٹن مارکیٹ تاریخی آرٹس کمپلیکس مال روڈ لاہور
short_description: 1864 timber-and-brick exhibition pavilion on Mall Road restored as a cultural handicraft and art hall.
description: Originally constructed for the Punjab Exhibition of 1864, its exposed wooden trusses and classical colonnades now house fine arts exhibitions, antique book sales, and heritage displays.

name: Pakistan Monument
name_ur: پاکستان یادگار
short_description: Flower-shaped national monument on Shakarparian hill with a museum.
description: The Pakistan Monument has four large petals representing the provinces and three smaller ones for the territories, with murals of national history on the inner walls.
history: Completed in 2007 and designed by architect Arif Masoud.
significance: It symbolises national unity.
culture: Murals depict the Pakistan Movement and figures such as Jinnah and Iqbal.
local_customs: Respect the monument; no climbing.
food: Cafes on site and at nearby Lok Virsa.
shopping: The museum shop sells books and souvenirs.
tips: Combine with Lok Virsa Museum next door (overlapping radius).

name: Lahore Museum
name_ur: لاہور عجائب گھر
short_description: Pakistan's oldest major museum with Gandhara art, miniatures and coins.
description: Housed in a red-brick Indo-Gothic building on The Mall, the museum holds Gandhara Buddhist sculpture, Mughal and Sikh artefacts, miniature paintings and the famous Fasting Buddha.
history: Founded in 1865 and moved to its current building in 1894; Rudyard Kipling's father John Lockwood Kipling was an early curator.
significance: It is the best single place to understand the deep history of Punjab and Gandhara.
culture: The collection traces the cultural history of the region from the Indus Valley to the modern era.
local_customs: Photography rules vary by gallery; bags may be checked.
food: Cafes on The Mall and Anarkali nearby.
shopping: Zamzama gun is outside; Anarkali Bazaar is a short walk away.
tips: Allow two hours; the Gandhara gallery is the highlight.
opening_hours: Typically 9 AM to 5 PM, closed on some public holidays.

name: Empress Market
name_ur: ایمپریس مارکیٹ
short_description: Colonial clock-tower market for spices, dry fruit and produce.
description: A Victorian market building with a tall clock tower in Saddar, selling spices, dry fruit, meat, fabric and household goods.
history: Built in the 1880s and named after Queen Victoria, Empress of India.
significance: One of Karachi's best-known colonial landmarks.
culture: Bargaining is expected.
local_customs: Keep valuables secure.
food: Street food around Saddar.
shopping: Spices, dry fruit and tea.
tips: Morning is the best time to see the market active.

name: Mohenjo-daro
name_ur: موہنجو داڑو
short_description: UNESCO ruins of one of the world's earliest planned cities.
description: The ruins of a Bronze Age Indus Valley city with grid streets, drainage, the Great Bath and a Buddhist stupa.
history: Built around 2500 BCE and rediscovered in the 1920s; a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980.
significance: A cornerstone of world archaeology.
culture: The Indus civilisation had advanced urban planning and trade.
local_customs: Do not climb on fragile walls.
food: Limited food; carry water.
shopping: Replica seals at the museum shop.
tips: Visit in winter; summers are extremely hot.
image_credit: The original uploader was M.Imran at English Wikipedia.

name: Faisal Mosque
name_ur: فیصل مسجد
short_description: Iconic tent-shaped national mosque at the foot of the Margalla Hills.
description: With its tent-like concrete shell and four pencil-thin minarets, Faisal Mosque is the national mosque of Pakistan and one of the largest mosques in the world.
history: Designed by Turkish architect Vedat Dalokay and completed in 1986, funded largely by a gift from King Faisal of Saudi Arabia.
significance: It is the defining landmark of Islamabad and a centre of national religious life.
culture: Its modern design breaks from traditional domes and is inspired by a Bedouin tent.
local_customs: Dress modestly: cover shoulders and knees; women should carry a scarf. Remove shoes before entering prayer areas and keep voices low, especially during prayer times.
food: Food kiosks near the parking area; F-7 Jinnah Super has restaurants.
shopping: Islamic books and prayer items at stalls near the entrance.
tips: Visit at sunset for views against the Margalla Hills.
opening_hours: Daily; tourist access outside prayer times.

name: Rawal Lake
name_ur: راول جھیل
short_description: Reservoir with lakeside gardens, boating and sunset views.
description: An artificial reservoir that supplies water to Rawalpindi, surrounded by terraced gardens, picnic spots and boating points.
history: Formed by a dam on the Korang river completed in 1962.
significance: A calm natural escape close to the city.
culture: Families come for picnics and boat rides.
local_customs: Swimming is not allowed.
food: Snack stalls at the view point.
shopping: None.
tips: Sunset from the lake view park is beautiful.
entry_fee: Small entry fee to the lake view park.

name: Azadi Museum
name_ur: آزادی میوزیم
short_description: Museum in Batapur
description: Museum in Batapur

name: Model Town Central Park
name_ur: ماڈل ٹاؤن پارک
short_description: Family park and also a golf course located in Model Town, Lahore, Pakistan
description: The Model Town Park is located in Model Town, Pakistan. It was developed in 1985 by then Governor of Punjab, Ghulam Jilani Khan. It has 2.0 km jogging tracks.

name: Ubauro Historic Jamia Mosque & Talpur Fort
name_ur: اوباڑو تاریخی جامع مسجد و تالپور قلعہ گھوٹکی
short_description: 18th-century brick fort and historic mosque marking the ancient northern frontier boundary of Sindh.
description: Strategically positioned near the Punjab border, Ubauro preserves decorated Islamic tombs, multi-domed mosques, and defensive bastions that repelled northern invasions.

name: Daharki Baba Nanak Darbar & Mariam Temple
name_ur: ڈہرکی بابا نانک دربار و مریم مندر گھوٹکی
short_description: Prominent interfaith pilgrimage complex in Daharki celebrated for communal harmony and Udasi Sikh heritage.
description: Holding holy scriptures and sacred Guru Darbars, this expansive spiritual haven hosts annual Melas where Hindu, Sikh, and Muslim devotees celebrate shared humanitarian ethics.

name: Lakhidar Historic Gateway & Clock Tower (Shikarpur)
name_ur: لکھی در تاریخی گیٹ وے و کلاک ٹاور شکارپور
short_description: The principal historic entry gate of walled Shikarpur featuring an illuminated public clock tower.
description: One of the original eight fortified gates of Shikarpur, Lakhidar led the primary trade route to Lakhi and Sukkur, surrounded by celebrated sweetmeat shops and traditional falooda parlors.

name: Cawasjee Parsi Heritage Hospital Building
name_ur: کاؤس جی پارسی ہیرٹیج ہسپتال شکارپور
short_description: 1930s colonial Parsi philanthropic hospital built from red brick and carved timber balconies.
description: Endowed by Parsi merchant Seth Cawasjee Dinshaw, this colonial building stands as a testament to the generous inter-communal philanthropy that enriched historic Shikarpur.

name: Sir Shahnawaz Bhutto Memorial Library Larkana
name_ur: سر شاہنواز بھٹو میموریل لائبریری لاڑکانہ
short_description: Grand 1980s public research library in Larkana holding over 100,000 rare books and historical manuscripts.
description: Named after the visionary statesman Sir Shahnawaz Bhutto, this modern Islamic-arched library serves students, scholars, and historians across northern Sindh with digital archives and quiet study halls.

name: Ancient Bazira
name_ur: بریکوٹ
short_description: Town in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
description:
Barikot is a city located in the middle course of the Swat River in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. It is located about 20 km (12 mi) away from Mingora and the Butkara Stupa. It is the entrance town to the central Swat Valley with a population of approximately 115,045 people.
Barikot is the location of an ancient citadel captured by Alexander the Great, with Chalcolithic remains dating back to c. 1700 BC, and an early-historic period town dating back to c. 600 BC. 
The Italian Archaeological Mission founded by Giuseppe Tucci has been excavating ruins of the ancient town of Bazira under Barikot since 1984.

name: Lulusar Lake
name_ur: لالو سر
short_description: Lake in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
description: The Kaghan Valley is an alpine river valley traversed by Kunhar River in Mansehra District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The valley stretches 155 kilometres (96 mi) in northern Pakistan, rising from its lowest elevation of 650 m (2,134 ft) to the Babusar Pass around 4,170 m (13,690 ft). The highest mountain peak in the valley, known as Malika Parbat, stands at a height of around 5,290 metres (17,360 ft).

name: Lulusar-Dudipatsar National Park
name_ur: لولوسر-دودی پت سر نیشنل پارک
short_description: National park of Pakistan
description: Lulusar-Dodipat National Park is located in the Kaghan Valley in Mansehra District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The park was created in 2003. The scenic Dudipatsar Lake and Lulusar Lake and peaks are in the park.

name: Khyber Pass
name_ur: درۂ خیبر
short_description: Mountain pass connecting Afghanistan and Pakistan
description: The Khyber Pass is a mountain pass in the Khyber District of the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, along the international border with Afghanistan. It connects the town of Landi Kotal to the Valley of Peshawar at Jamrud by traversing part of the White Mountains. Since it was part of the ancient Silk Road, it has been a vital trade route between Central Asia and the Indian subcontinent and a strategic military choke point for various states that controlled it. The Khyber Pass is considered one of the most famous mountain passes in the world.

name: Mahabat Khan Mosque
name_ur: مسجد مہابت خان
short_description: 17th-century Mughal mosque with painted interiors in old Peshawar.
description: A white Mughal mosque with tall minarets and finely painted floral interiors in the heart of the Walled City.
history: Built in the 1670s during the governorship of Mahabat Khan.
significance: Peshawar's finest Mughal monument.
culture: An active community mosque.
local_customs: Dress modestly: cover shoulders and knees; women should carry a scarf. Remove shoes before entering prayer areas and keep voices low, especially during prayer times.
food: Street food around Qissa Khwani.
shopping: Spice and cloth markets nearby.
tips: Visit outside prayer times.

name: Sethi Havelis
name_ur: سیٹھی حویلیاں پشاور
short_description: Museum in Peshawar
description: Museum in Peshawar

name: Sikaram Sar
name_ur: سیکرم
short_description: Notable nature site located in Shalozan.
description: Mount Sikaram is a mountain on the Afghanistan–Pakistan border, south of the Kabul River and Khyber Pass. At 4,755 m (15,600 ft), it is the highest peak of the Spīn Ghar, or Safēd Kōh, mountain range.

name: Shahbaz Garhi
name_ur: شہباز گڑھی
short_description: Archaeological site
description: Shahbaz Garhi, or Shahbazgarhi, is a village and historic site located in Mardan District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. It is at an altitude of 293 metres.

name: Paiju Peak
name_ur: پائیجو چوٹی
short_description: Notable nature site located in Shigar District.
description: Paiju Peak, also known as Payu, is a mountain in northern Pakistan.

name: Broghil National Park
name_ur: بروغل نیشنل پارک
short_description: Notable nature site located in Upper Chitral District.
description: Broghil Valley National Park is located in the extreme northern reaches of the Upper Chitral District in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, close to the Pak–Afghan border. It lies around the Mountains of Central Asia biodiversity hotspot.
image_credit: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (Broghil Valley National Park)

name: Tirich Mir
name_ur: ترچ میر
short_description: Highest mountain of the Hindu Kush range
description: Terich Mir, 7,708 meters (25,289 ft), is the highest mountain of the Hindu Kush range, the 33rd highest peak in the world and the highest mountain outside of the Himalayas–Karakoram range. It is located in the Chitral District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

name: Udren Zom
name_ur: ادرین زوم
short_description: Notable nature site located in Upper Chitral District.
description: Udren Zom is a mountain in the Hindu Kush mountain range in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan. Its summit has an elevation of 7,140 metres (23,425 ft) and a topographic prominence of 1,620 metres (5,315 ft). It is one of the highest peaks in the world located outside of the Himalayan and Karakoram ranges.

name: Jungle Kingdom
name_ur: جنگل ورلڈ ایوب پارک، راولپنڈی
short_description: Zoo and animal theme park in Rawalpindi, Pakistan
description: Jungle World is an animal theme park and zoological garden located in Ayub National Park, Rawalpindi District, Pakistan. The visitor spot is spread over about 200,000 square metres.

name: Tomb of Dai Anga
name_ur: مقبرہ دائی انگہ
short_description: Mughal Monument in Lahore
description: The Tomb of Dai Anga, also known as the Gulabi Bagh, is a 17th-century Mughal tomb complex located in the Mughal-era suburb of Begampura, outside the Walled City of Lahore, Pakistan.

name: Jinnah Bagh Central Public Park (Larkana)
name_ur: جناح باغ مرکزی عوامی پارک لاڑکانہ
short_description: Lush shaded municipal garden in the center of Larkana featuring century-old trees, rose beds, and walking tracks.
description: The principal green lung of Larkana, Jinnah Bagh provides a tranquil haven for evening strollers, family picnics, and public cultural gatherings under majestic banyan canopies.

name: Hamal Lake Wetland Wildlife Reserve (Qambar)
name_ur: حمل جھیل قدرتی آبی ذخیرہ و پرندوں کی پناہ گاہ قمبر
short_description: Vast 25-kilometer natural freshwater lake at the foot of Kirthar hills hosting tens of thousands of migratory birds.
description: Surrounded by reed marshes and tamarisk scrub, Hamal Lake is a vital freshwater ecosystem where indigenous boatmen fish for carps and wintering ducks roost in absolute natural tranquility.

name: Drigh Lake Protected Bird Sanctuary
name_ur: ڈریگھ جھیل محفوظ قدرتی پناہ گاہ قمبر لاڑکانہ
short_description: Designated Ramsar wetland and wildlife sanctuary renowned as a winter haven for night herons and mallards.
description: Covering 164 hectares of tranquil waters and dense lotus beds, Drigh Lake features observation towers where birdwatchers observe rare whistling teals, spoonbills, and marsh harriers.

name: Johi Historic Desert Gateway & Water Wells
name_ur: جوہی تاریخی صحرائی گیٹ وے و قدیم کنویں دادو
short_description: Historic outpost town on the border of the Kirthar range known for deep stone stepwells and Shiva temples.
description: Serving as the gateway for treks into the Gorakh Hills and Kirthar National Park, Johi preserves ancient caravan routes, desert handicraft markets, and centuries-old brick tombs.

name: Muztagh Tower
name_ur: مز تاغ ٹاور
short_description: Mountain
description: Muztagh Tower, also Mustagh Tower; Muztagh: icy mountain), is a mountain situated in Baltoro Muztagh, which is a segment of the Karakoram range. It straddles the border of the Gilgit–Baltistan region of Pakistan and the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of China. Muztagh Tower is located between the basins of the Baltoro and Sarpo Laggo glaciers.

name: Jamia Masjid Mehtab
name_ur: مسجد مہتاب
short_description: Mosque in Jaranwala, Punjab, Pakistan
description: Mosque in Jaranwala, Punjab, Pakistan

name: Rohtas Fort
name_ur: قلعہ روہتاس
short_description: Massive 16th-century garrison fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
description: Rohtas Fort's huge stone walls and gates stretch for kilometres across the hills near Jhelum.
history: Built by Sher Shah Suri in the 1540s to block the return of the Mughal emperor Humayun.
significance: An outstanding example of early Muslim military architecture.
culture: A fusion of Afghan and Persian military architecture.
local_customs: Wear sturdy shoes.
food: Few options; bring snacks.
shopping: None.
tips: Allow a half day.

name: Kalar Kahar Lake
name_ur: کلر کہار جھیل
short_description: Lake in Punjab, Pakistan
description: Lake in Punjab, Pakistan

name: Anarkali Bazaar
name_ur: انارکلی بازار
short_description: One of South Asia's oldest markets for fabrics, jewellery and street food.
description: A bustling bazaar of narrow lanes selling clothes, bangles, shoes, fabric and street snacks, named after the legendary Anarkali.
history: The bazaar has existed for at least two centuries and grew alongside colonial Lahore's Mall Road.
significance: It offers a lively snapshot of everyday Lahori life.
culture: Bargaining is expected and the market is busiest in the evening and before Eid.
local_customs: Bargain politely; keep valuables secure in crowds.
food: Try dahi bhallay, gol gappay and fresh falooda.
shopping: Embroidered fabric, khussa shoes, glass bangles and jewellery.
tips: Go in the evening; avoid peak Eid rush if you dislike crowds.
opening_hours: Shops open roughly noon to 10 PM; many close on Sundays.

name: Badshahi Mosque
name_ur: بادشاہی مسجد
short_description: A grand Mughal-era mosque of red sandstone facing the Lahore Fort.
description: Built of red sandstone with white marble domes, the Badshahi Mosque is one of the largest mosques in the world and the crown of Lahore's Walled City skyline. Its vast courtyard can hold tens of thousands of worshippers.
history: Commissioned by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb and completed in 1673, the mosque was the largest in the world for over three centuries. It was used as a garrison during Sikh rule and later restored under British and Pakistani administration.
significance: It is a symbol of Mughal architectural ambition and of Lahore's identity, and remains an active place of worship.
culture: The mosque sits within the Hazuri Bagh complex alongside the Lahore Fort, the Roshnai Gate and the tomb of the poet Allama Iqbal.
local_customs: Dress modestly: cover shoulders and knees; women should carry a scarf. Remove shoes before entering prayer areas and keep voices low, especially during prayer times.
food: Fort Road Food Street next door serves karahi, tikka and lassi with views of the minarets at night.
shopping: Look for embroidered shawls and miniature-painting souvenirs in the Walled City lanes nearby.
tips: Visit late afternoon for golden light on the sandstone, then stay for the illuminated view after sunset.
opening_hours: Open daily, roughly sunrise to after Isha prayer; tourist access is limited during Friday prayers.
entry_fee: Free entry; shoe-keeping attendants expect a small tip.

name: City Museum
name_ur: شکارپور سٹی میوزیم
short_description: Museum in Shikarpur
description: Museum in Shikarpur

name: Mehar Historic Trading Chowk & Rice Mandi
name_ur: میہر تاریخی تجارتی چوک و چاول منڈی دادو
short_description: Bustling agricultural market town in northern Dadu district renowned for premium basmati and irri rice milling.
description: Intersected by historic canal regulators, Mehar handles extensive wholesale produce trade, offering vibrant street bazaars filled with local sweets, pottery, and traditional fabric.

name: Khunjerab Pass
name_ur: خنجراب پاس
short_description: High-altitude border crossing on the Karakoram Highway.
description: At about 4,700 metres, Khunjerab is one of the highest paved border crossings in the world, on the Pakistan-China border.
history: The Karakoram Highway over the pass opened in the 1980s.
significance: A landmark of engineering and the old Silk Road.
culture: Part of Khunjerab National Park.
local_customs: Altitude sickness is possible; move slowly.
food: Carry snacks; options are very limited.
shopping: None.
tips: Go early; weather changes fast.

name: Ilford Peak
name_ur: الفورڈ چوٹی
short_description: Notable nature site located in Machulo.
description: Ilford Peak is a peak located on the watershed of the Nangmah, Khane and Lachit valleys, Pakistan. The mountain, located in the Karakoram mountain range, is 6080 meters high. It was first climbed on July 23, 2019 by a group of Russian climbers Markevich Konstantin, Sushko Denis and Anton Ivanov.

name: Shaji-ki-Dheri Remains (Kaniska Stupa)
name_ur: کنشک اسٹوپا
short_description: Stupa on the outskirts of Peshawar, Pakistan
description: The Kanishka Stupa was a monumental stupa established by King Kanishka of Kushan during the 2nd century CE in today's Shaji-ki-Dheri on the outskirts of Peshawar, Pakistan.

name: Data Darbar
name_ur: داتا دربار
short_description: Shrine of the 11th-century Sufi saint Ali Hujwiri, Lahore's spiritual heart.
description: Data Darbar is the shrine of Ali Hujwiri, known as Data Ganj Bakhsh, and one of the most visited Sufi shrines in South Asia.
history: Ali Hujwiri authored the Kashf al-Mahjub, a classic Persian treatise on Sufism, and died in Lahore in the 11th century.
significance: It is central to Lahore's Sufi heritage and draws visitors of all backgrounds.
culture: Devotees offer prayers, distribute food (langar) and listen to qawwali.
local_customs: Dress modestly: cover shoulders and knees; women should carry a scarf. Remove shoes before entering prayer areas and keep voices low, especially during prayer times. Separate entrances may exist for men and women.
food: Free langar is distributed; street food around Bhati Gate.
shopping: Prayer beads, rose petals and religious books.
tips: Thursday evenings feature qawwali; expect crowds.

name: Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park
name_ur: گلشن اقبال پارک
short_description: Notable park site located in Lahore.
description: The Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park is a large park and recreational space in Lahore, Pakistan. With an area of over 67 acres (0.27 km2), the park is one of the largest in the city. It is situated in the suburban locality of Allama Iqbal Town. The name Gulshan-e-Iqbal is literally translated as "the garden of Iqbal," referring to Iqbal, the national poet of Pakistan. It has many recreational rides for children and adults making it a popular venue for families, especially on weekends and other holidays. It also features a vast artificial lake and a mini-zoo.

name: Haleji Lake Pelican Watchtowers & Sanctuary
name_ur: ہالیجی جھیل پیلیکن واچ ٹاورز و پناہ گاہ ٹھٹھہ
short_description: Famous artificial lake sanctuary once dubbed 'the bird watcher's paradise of Asia', sheltering 200 bird species.
description: Surrounded by a 17-kilometer motorable bund, Haleji features elevated wildlife viewing hides, freshwater marsh crocodiles sunbathing on sandbanks, and thousands of pelicans diving in unison.

name: Mirpur Bathoro Historic Rice & Canal Town
name_ur: میرپور بٹھورو تاریخی دھان و نہری قصبہ سجاول
short_description: Historic agricultural township in Sujawal district holding centuries-old Sufi shrines and rice mills.
description: Situated near ancient branches of the Indus delta, Mirpur Bathoro features lively weekly cattle fairs, traditional Sindhi quilt (rilli) makers, and lush irrigated paddy fields.

name: Jati Coastal Outpost & Camel Sanctuary
name_ur: جاتی ساحلی قصبہ و اونٹوں کا نخلستان سجاول
short_description: Southern coastal delta town famous for coastal saltwater-swimming Kharai camels and mangrove honey.
description: The jumping-off point for exploring the Shah Bandar ruins, Jati is celebrated for its unique herds of indigenous camels that swim through deep seawater channels to graze on offshore mangrove leaves.

name: Matli Historic Grain & Rice Mills Bazaar
name_ur: ماتلی تاریخی غلہ و چاول فیکٹریز بازار بدین
short_description: Northern commercial hub of Badin district operating dozens of modern and heritage rice husking mills.
description: Flanked by the Phuleli canal command, Matli's vast grain trading markets distribute fragrant non-basmati and basmati varieties across Pakistan, accompanied by traditional sweet shops.

name: Tando Bago Cultural Square & Mirs Legacy
name_ur: ٹنڈو باگو کلچرل چوک و تالپور ورثہ بدین
short_description: Historic Talpur foundation in Badin district celebrated for educational institutions and folk poetry.
description: Established by Mir Bago Khan Talpur, this tranquil town holds historic high schools, brick havelis, and shaded mango orchards that nurtured generations of Sindhi intellectuals.

name: Golarchi (Shaheed Fazil Rahu) Wetlands
name_ur: گولارچی (شہید فاضل راہو) قدرتی جھیلیں بدین
short_description: Vibrant coastal township surrounded by natural gas energy fields and freshwater fishing lakes.
description: Located near coastal creeks, Golarchi blends modern oil and gas energy infrastructure with tranquil rural wetlands that support local waterbird populations and freshwater aquaculture.

name: Chelhar Sand Dune Village & Rilli Weavers
name_ur: چیلھار ریتلے ٹیلے کا گاؤں و رلی کاریگر تھرپارکر
short_description: Famous desert village nestled among towering sand dunes, renowned as the global capital of hand-stitched Rilli quilts.
description: In Chelhar, master Thari women stitch thousands of geometric patchwork quilts from recycled cotton fabrics, creating museum-quality textile art recognized in international ethnographic collections.

name: Diplo Historic Desert Town & Camel Fair
name_ur: ڈپلو تاریخی صحرائی قصبہ و اونٹ منڈی تھرپارکر
short_description: Ancient southern Thar Desert town known for camel trading caravans and salt lake extraction.
description: Situated near the edge of the great salt pans of the Rann of Kutch, Diplo features peaceful whitewashed desert homes, camel-drawn carts, and a vibrant local bazaar selling wool rugs and desert leatherwork.

name: Chachro High Desert Dunes & Wilderness
name_ur: چھاچھرو اونچے ریتلے ٹیلے و صحرائی حسن تھرپارکر
short_description: Remote eastern desert capital surrounded by undulating sand dunes, roaming peacocks, and acacia woodlands.
description: The cultural heartland of eastern Tharparkar, Chachro offers authentic encounters with rural desert life, star-studded unpolluted night skies, and traditional circular thatched mud huts known as Chaunras.

name: Mirpur Khas Mango & Fruit Research Station
name_ur: میرپور خاص مینگو و فروٹ ریسرچ اسٹیشن
short_description: Pakistan's oldest agricultural fruit research station established in 1904, fathering modern mango varieties.
description: Spanning lush experimental orchards, this historic station developed and standardized famous Pakistani mangoes including Sindhri and Siroli, hosting the prestigious annual National Mango Festival.

name: Lake Saiful Muluk
name_ur: جھیل سیف الملوک
short_description: Alpine lake below Malika Parbat, wrapped in folklore.
description: A turquoise high-altitude lake in the Kaghan Valley reached by jeep from Naran, surrounded by snow-capped peaks.
history: The lake is linked to the legend of Prince Saif-ul-Malook and the fairy princess Badri-ul-Jamala.
significance: One of Pakistan's most famous natural sights.
culture: Storytellers recount the fairy tale by the shore.
local_customs: Weather changes quickly; carry warm clothing.
food: Tea and pakoras at shore-side stalls.
shopping: Few shops.
tips: Large radius (3 km) suits mountain areas with weak GPS.

name: Fort Road Food Street
name_ur: فورٹ روڈ فوڈ اسٹریٹ
short_description: Restored havelis turned rooftop restaurants with views of the Badshahi Mosque.
description: A pedestrian street of restored old buildings whose rooftops overlook the Badshahi Mosque. It is one of the most atmospheric places to try traditional Lahori cuisine at night.
history: The street was restored as a heritage food destination, reviving colonial and Mughal-era facades of the Walled City.
significance: It combines heritage, food culture and one of the best night views in the city.
culture: Lahoris are famous for their love of food; dinner here is a social event that runs late into the night.
local_customs: Dinner is usually late (9 PM onwards). Ask for rooftop seating early.
food: Mutton karahi, chicken tikka, seekh kebab, paye, and sweet lassi.
shopping: Cushion covers and lamps decorated with truck art are sold nearby.
tips: Busiest on weekends; the radius overlaps the Badshahi Mosque, ideal for testing overlapping geofences.
opening_hours: Most restaurants open from late afternoon to after midnight.
entry_fee: No entry fee; meals are mid-range.
image_credit: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (Fort Road Food Street)

name: Tomb of Jahangir
name_ur: مقبرہ جہانگیر
short_description: Mughal emperor's mausoleum in a walled garden across the Ravi river.
description: The mausoleum of Emperor Jahangir stands in a large garden in Shahdara, decorated with marble inlay, frescoes and four tall minarets.
history: Built in the 1630s by his son Shah Jahan. The nearby tombs of Nur Jahan and Asif Khan form a wider Mughal complex.
significance: It is one of the finest Mughal tombs outside India.
culture: The tomb blends Persian garden design with Mughal decoration.
local_customs: Remove shoes where requested inside the tomb chamber.
food: Limited food nearby; eat in central Lahore.
shopping: Few shops; bring water.
tips: Its large radius (1.5 km) is useful for testing early-warning geofences while driving.

name: Chittori Talpur Historic Royal Graveyard
name_ur: چٹوری تالپور شاہی تاریخی قبرستان میرپور خاص
short_description: 18th-century yellow sandstone necropolis of the Mankani Talpur rulers adorned with intricate relief carvings.
description: Featuring ornate domed pavilions constructed from carved stone without mortar, Chittori preserves the tombs of Mir Sher Muhammad Talpur's ancestors with beautiful stone jaali windows and jharokas.

name: Kahu-jo-Daro Ancient Buddhist Stupa Mound
name_ur: کاہو جو دڑو قدیم بدھ اسٹوپا و آثار میرپور خاص
short_description: 4th-century CE Buddhist archaeological stupa mound that yielded the famous terracotta Buddha sculptures of Sindh.
description: Excavated by Henry Cousens, this ancient site demonstrated the vibrant Buddhist heritage of pre-Islamic Sindh, holding carved terracotta plaques depicting Lord Buddha in meditation, now preserved in museums.

name: Khipro Desert Livestock & Camel Fairgrounds
name_ur: کھپرو صحرائی مویشی و اونٹ منڈی سانگھڑ
short_description: Major transit market between irrigated Sindh and the Thar Desert trading thoroughbred camels and cattle.
description: Every week, thousands of Thari pastoralists gather in Khipro to trade prized red Sindhi cattle, racing camels, and desert ghee, creating a bustling spectacle of authentic nomadic commerce.

name: Shahdadpur Historic Sufi Shrines & Market
name_ur: شہداد پور تاریخی صوفی درگاہیں و تجارتی بازار سانگھڑ
short_description: Historic township founded by Mir Shahdad Khan Talpur in the 18th century, famous for cloth markets.
description: Home to centuries-old Talpur tombs and revered Sufi shrines, Shahdadpur is an active commercial town serving the fertile cotton belts of the Rohri Canal commands.

name: Sakrand Agricultural Research Experimental Groves
name_ur: سکرنڈ زرعی تحقیقاتی ادارے کے باغات شہید بینظیر آباد
short_description: Pioneering 1920s agricultural research center that developed high-yield cotton and wheat strains for Sindh.
description: Established to support irrigation from the Sukkur Barrage, Sakrand features experimental date palm groves, cotton trial fields, and citrus orchards that have educated agriculturalists for a century.

name: Baltit Fort
name_ur: بلتت قلعہ
short_description: Centuries-old fort overlooking the Hunza valley.
description: Perched above Karimabad, Baltit Fort is a restored mountain fort and museum with views of Rakaposhi and Ultar peaks.
history: Its foundations date back around 700 years; it was the seat of the Mirs of Hunza and was restored in the 1990s.
significance: A symbol of Hunza's heritage.
culture: Tibetan-influenced architecture reflects ties across the Karakoram.
local_customs: Guided tours are mandatory inside.
food: Try apricot cake and walnut bread in Karimabad.
shopping: Gemstones, handwoven rugs and dry apricots.
tips: Combine with Altit Fort.

name: Saidpur Village
name_ur: سید پور گاؤں
short_description: Restored centuries-old village at the foot of the Margalla Hills.
description: A historic village with restored stone houses, a Hindu temple, a gurdwara and restaurants set against the hills.
history: Named after Sultan Said Khan of the Gakhar tribe in the 16th century; the village was a site of religious diversity.
significance: A good place to understand the pre-Islamabad history.
culture: Shows the shared Hindu, Sikh and Muslim heritage of the area.
local_customs: Respect places of worship.
food: Traditional restaurants serving desi food.
shopping: Small craft shops.
tips: Pleasant in the evening; combine with Trail 3.

name: Katas Raj Temples
name_ur: کٹاس راج مندر
short_description: Ancient Hindu temple complex around a sacred pond.
description: A complex of temples built around a pond considered sacred in Hindu tradition, in the Salt Range.
history: Temples date from the 7th century onwards; the site is linked to legends of the Mahabharata.
significance: A key site of Pakistan's religious diversity.
culture: Pilgrims visit during festivals.
local_customs: Respect worship areas.
food: Limited food nearby.
shopping: None.
tips: Combine with the Salt Range drive.

name: Liberty Market
name_ur: لبرٹی مارکیٹ
short_description: Popular Gulberg market for clothes, fabrics and street snacks.
description: A modern shopping hub in Gulberg known for women's clothing, designer lawn, jewellery and food stalls around a central roundabout.
history: Developed in the 1960s as Gulberg grew into a planned residential area.
significance: A good contrast to the old city bazaars.
culture: Evening shopping and snacks are a family outing for many Lahoris.
local_customs: Fixed prices in branded stores; bargaining at stalls.
food: Fresh juice, chaat and fast food.
shopping: Lawn fabric, shoes, jewellery and accessories.
tips: Parking is tight in the evening; use ride-hailing.

name: Raja Bazaar
name_ur: راجہ بازار
short_description: Rawalpindi's busiest traditional market for everything from spices to fabric.
description: A dense, historic market district of narrow lanes selling spices, cloth, utensils, dry fruit and street food.
history: One of the oldest markets of Rawalpindi, dating back to the 19th century.
significance: A lively look at old Rawalpindi.
culture: Bargaining is the norm.
local_customs: Keep valuables secure; traffic is chaotic.
food: Chana chaat and fresh jalebi.
shopping: Spices, dry fruit, fabrics and household goods.
tips: Visit before noon to avoid the worst crowds.

name: Mohatta Palace
name_ur: موہٹہ پیلس
short_description: Pink sandstone palace turned museum in Clifton.
description: An elegant palace of pink Jodhpur stone with domes and balconies, now a museum hosting art and heritage exhibitions.
history: Built in 1927 as the summer home of businessman Shivratan Mohatta.
significance: A rare surviving example of pre-partition grandeur.
culture: Rajput-style architecture in Karachi.
local_customs: Photography rules vary by exhibition.
food: Cafes in Clifton nearby.
shopping: Museum shop with books and crafts.
tips: Check current exhibitions before visiting.
opening_hours: About 11 AM to 6 PM, closed Mondays.

name: Qazi Ahmed Historic Grand Trunk Road Stop
name_ur: قاضی احمد تاریخی شاہراہ پڑاؤ شہید بینظیر آباد
short_description: Historic roadside caravanserai town on the National Highway famed for fresh buffalo curd and mutton karahi.
description: A bustling transit stop connecting Upper and Lower Sindh, travelers pull over day and night at Qazi Ahmed for authentic clay pot yogurt (dahi), sweet tea, and sizzling highway dhaba dishes.

name: Jungshahi Stone Carving Ateliers
name_ur: جنگشاہی پتھر تراشی کارخانے ٹھٹھہ
short_description: Historic stone carving studios in Thatta famous for quarrying pink and yellow sandstone for monuments.
description: Jungshahi sandstone has built the great architectural monuments of Sindh including Makli, Frere Hall, and Mohatta Palace, celebrated for its durability and warm golden hue.

name: Gharo Creek Mangrove Tidal Haven
name_ur: گھارو کریک مینگروو پناہ گاہ ٹھٹھہ
short_description: Serene tidal creek along the National Highway offering dense mangrove channels and crab fishing.
description: Connecting the Indus delta network to the Arabian Sea, Gharo Creek is a vital spawning habitat for tiger prawns, mudskippers, and coastal herons in lower Sindh.

name: Tomb of Shah Rukn-e-Alam
name_ur: مزار شاہ رکنِ عالم
short_description: Massive octagonal brick tomb, a masterpiece of Multani tilework.
description: This 14th-century octagonal mausoleum of the Sufi saint Shah Rukn-e-Alam dominates Multan's skyline with its blue-tiled brick walls.
history: Built in the early 14th century during the Tughlaq period.
significance: One of the earliest examples of Tughlaq architecture.
culture: Multan is called the City of Saints for its many shrines.
local_customs: Dress modestly: cover shoulders and knees; women should carry a scarf. Remove shoes before entering prayer areas and keep voices low, especially during prayer times.
food: Sohan halwa is the famous local sweet.
shopping: Blue pottery and camel-skin lamps.
tips: Avoid the midday summer heat.

name: Taxila Museum
name_ur: ٹیکسلا میوزیم
short_description: Gandhara civilisation treasures near the UNESCO ruins of Taxila.
description: The museum displays Buddhist sculpture, coins, jewellery and pottery excavated from the ancient city of Taxila.
history: Taxila was a major centre of learning and trade on the Silk Road; the ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980.
significance: Key to understanding Buddhist heritage in Pakistan.
culture: Gandhara art blends Greek, Persian and Indian styles.
local_customs: Photography may be restricted inside.
food: Small cafes on the road outside.
shopping: Replica Gandhara sculptures sold nearby.
tips: Combine with the Dharmarajika and Sirkap ruins.

name: Fairy Meadows
name_ur: فیری میڈوز
short_description: Alpine meadow with a direct view of Nanga Parbat.
description: A grassy plateau reached by jeep and trek from Raikot Bridge, offering views of the 8,126 m Nanga Parbat.
history: Named by German climbers; the base camp of Nanga Parbat's Rakhiot face is nearby.
significance: One of the most dramatic mountain views on Earth.
culture: Cabins and camping run by locals.
local_customs: The jeep road is dangerous; use local drivers.
food: Simple meals in camps.
shopping: None.
tips: Bring warm layers even in summer.

name: Burns Road Food Street
name_ur: برنس روڈ فوڈ اسٹریٹ
short_description: Karachi's legendary street of nihari, biryani and rabri.
description: A historic street lined with decades-old eateries serving Karachi favourites, from nihari and haleem to biryani and kulfi.
history: Many restaurants trace their roots to families who migrated in 1947.
significance: The heart of Karachi's street food culture.
culture: Food is shared and eaten late at night.
local_customs: Expect crowds and simple seating.
food: Nihari, biryani, haleem, fried fish, rabri and kulfi.
shopping: Few souvenirs; it is all about food.
tips: Go hungry and try several shops.
opening_hours: Most stalls open evening to late night.

name: Mirpur Sakro Historic Shrine & Farms
name_ur: میرپور ساکرو تاریخی درگاہ و باغات ٹھٹھہ
short_description: Tranquil agricultural town in lower Thatta surrounded by banana plantations and Sufi shrines.
description: Known for its rich alluvial delta soil, Mirpur Sakro produces high-grade Cavendish bananas, betel leaves (paan), and fresh coconuts supplied to Karachi markets.

name: Jhimpir Yellow Sandstone Quarries
name_ur: جھمپیر زرد ریتلے پتھر کی تاریخی کانیں ٹھٹھہ
short_description: Century-old stone quarries supplying warm limestone blocks for historical architecture across Pakistan.
description: Geologically part of the Laki limestone formation, these historic quarries have provided the distinctive building blocks for Sindh's colonial courthouses, churches, and palaces.

name: Var Ancient Indus Delta Outpost
name_ur: وار قدیم انڈس ڈیلٹا چوکی سجاول
short_description: Remote coastal delta outpost town on the historic salt trading trails of lower Sujawal.
description: A peaceful rural fishing haven along the delta channels where traditional boat builders construct wooden fishing dhows using ancient local techniques.

name: Talhar Historic Rice Belt & Mandi
name_ur: تلہار تاریخی دھان بیلٹ و منڈی بدین
short_description: Historic railway junction in Badin surrounded by emerald paddy fields and aromatic rice mills.
description: A primary procurement center for Sugdasi and Irri varieties of rice, Talhar has anchored southern Sindh's agricultural grain trading since the early 20th century.

name: Kario Ghanwar Ancient Archaeological Mound
name_ur: کڑیئو گھنوار قدیم آثار و ٹیلے بدین
short_description: Historical pre-Islamic settlement mound in western Badin yielding ancient terracotta pottery.
description: Guarding the ancient delta trade trails, Kario Ghanwar preserves the multi-layered historical heritage of early settlements that flourished along abandoned branches of the Indus.

name: Qissa Khwani Bazaar
name_ur: قصہ خوانی بازار
short_description: The storytellers' bazaar at the heart of old Peshawar.
description: Historic market where travellers and traders once gathered to hear stories over tea, now full of tea houses and dry fruit shops.
history: Peshawar is one of the oldest living cities in South Asia and a historic caravan stop near the Khyber Pass.
significance: A living piece of Silk Road history.
culture: Green tea (kahwa) and hospitality are central to Pashtun culture.
local_customs: Dress conservatively; ask before photographing people.
food: Chapli kebab and kahwa.
shopping: Dry fruit, Peshawari chappals and copperware.
tips: Combine with Mahabat Khan Mosque.

name: Lahore Fort (Shahi Qila)
name_ur: شاہی قلعہ لاہور
short_description: UNESCO World Heritage citadel with Mughal palaces, halls and the Sheesh Mahal.
description: The Lahore Fort is a sprawling citadel of palaces, audience halls, gardens and gateways spanning several Mughal reigns. Highlights include the mirror-mosaic Sheesh Mahal, the Picture Wall and the Alamgiri Gate.
history: Rebuilt in its current form by Emperor Akbar in the 16th century and expanded by Jahangir, Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site together with the Shalimar Gardens in 1981.
significance: It is among the most complete records of Mughal court life in South Asia.
culture: The fort showcases Mughal tile mosaics, fresco work and pietra dura inlay, with Persian, Hindu and Central Asian influences.
local_customs: Some halls require separate tickets; photography with a tripod may need permission.
food: Try the street food of Fort Road and Gawalmandi after your visit.
shopping: Handicraft stalls near the fort entrance sell khussa shoes and replica tiles.
tips: Allow at least two hours; wear comfortable shoes for the ramps and stone paths.
opening_hours: Daily, about 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM (seasonal variation).
entry_fee: Ticketed; foreign visitors pay a higher rate.

name: Minar-e-Pakistan
name_ur: مینارِ پاکستان
short_description: National monument marking the 1940 Lahore Resolution, set in Greater Iqbal Park.
description: A tall tower of concrete and marble rising above Greater Iqbal Park, Minar-e-Pakistan commemorates the resolution that called for a separate homeland for the Muslims of South Asia.
history: Built between 1960 and 1968 on the spot where the All-India Muslim League passed the Lahore Resolution on 23 March 1940.
significance: It is a central symbol of the founding of Pakistan and a gathering place on national days.
culture: The base is shaped like a flower and carries inscriptions of the resolution text and national verses in Urdu, Bengali and English.
local_customs: Families picnic in the park in the evening; respect the monument area.
food: Stalls around Iqbal Park sell roasted corn, chaat and fresh juices.
shopping: Small vendors sell flags and national souvenirs around Pakistan Day.
tips: The surrounding park has fountains and walking tracks; it gets busy on public holidays.
opening_hours: Park open daily from morning to late evening.

name: Shalimar Gardens
name_ur: شالامار باغ
short_description: Terraced Mughal pleasure gardens with fountains and marble pavilions.
description: A Persian-style garden laid out on three descending terraces with hundreds of fountains, water channels and pavilions, designed as a paradise on earth.
history: Laid out by Emperor Shah Jahan in 1641-42. Together with the Lahore Fort, the gardens are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
significance: It is one of the finest surviving examples of Mughal garden design.
culture: The design follows the charbagh concept of four-part gardens symbolising paradise in Islamic tradition.
local_customs: Picnicking is common; avoid walking on restricted lawns.
food: Snack vendors near the gate sell samosas and seasonal fruit.
shopping: Limited shopping; bring water.
tips: Visit in spring when fountains run and flowers bloom.

name: Wagah Border Ceremony
name_ur: واہگہ بارڈر
short_description: Energetic daily flag-lowering ceremony at the Pakistan-India border.
description: Every evening, border guards perform a high-energy flag-lowering ceremony with synchronised marching while crowds cheer from the stands.
history: The ceremony has been held at the Wagah-Attari crossing since 1959.
significance: It is a unique blend of patriotism and spectacle.
culture: Spectators wave flags and chant patriotic slogans; the atmosphere is festive.
local_customs: Arrive early; bags and cameras may be checked by security.
food: Bring snacks and water; facilities are basic.
shopping: Flag and souvenir sellers near the parking area.
tips: Arrive an hour before sunset. Carry your ID.

name: Nindo Shahar Historic Heritage Bazaar
name_ur: نندو شہر تاریخی ورثہ بازار بدین
short_description: Quaint desert-fringe market town in southern Badin known for traditional leatherwork and ajraks.
description: Serving pastoral desert communities near the Rann of Kutch, Nindo Shahar features vibrant weekly bazaars where nomadic herders trade hand-embroidered textiles and livestock.

name: Khoski Agro-Industrial Waterfront
name_ur: کھوسکی زرعی و شکر صنعتی مرکز بدین
short_description: Lush sugarcane plantation town in eastern Badin commanding extensive irrigation canal networks.
description: Fed by perennial irrigation waters, Khoski features sprawling emerald fields of towering sugarcane and sugar refining plants that power southern Sindh's industrial economy.

name: Wazir Khan Mosque
name_ur: مسجد وزیر خان
short_description: Exquisite 17th-century mosque covered in Mughal tile mosaics and frescoes.
description: Tucked into the Walled City near Delhi Gate, the Wazir Khan Mosque is renowned for the most ornate Mughal-era faience tile work in Pakistan, with floral frescoes covering almost every surface.
history: Built in the 1630s during the reign of Shah Jahan by Ilm-ud-din Ansari, known as Wazir Khan, the governor of Lahore.
significance: It is considered a masterpiece of Mughal decorative art and has been carefully restored.
culture: Its forecourt once hosted a bazaar of calligraphers and bookbinders, a tradition reflected in the shops around it.
local_customs: Dress modestly: cover shoulders and knees; women should carry a scarf. Remove shoes before entering prayer areas and keep voices low, especially during prayer times.
food: Try the traditional sweets and halwa puri in the lanes around Delhi Gate.
shopping: The Shahi Guzargah (Royal Trail) has spice markets and copper-ware shops.
tips: The small radius (300 m) is useful for testing precise geofences in dense streets.
opening_hours: Daily, outside prayer times for tourists.

name: Sakesar
name_ur: سكيسر
short_description: Notable nature site located in Lawa.
description: Sakesar is the highest mountain in the Salt Range in Punjab, Pakistan. Its height is 1,525 metres (5,003 ft). It lies on the outer fringes of the Soon Valley in Khushab District in the Punjab province. The small village of Sakesar is named after the mountain and Uchhali Lake is just below it.

name: Murree Mall Road
name_ur: مری مال روڈ
short_description: Hill station promenade with pine forests and mountain views.
description: The pedestrian Mall Road is the centre of Murree hill station, lined with shops, cafes and colonial buildings.
history: Murree was founded as a British sanatorium in the 1850s.
significance: Pakistan's most visited hill station.
culture: A favourite summer escape from the plains.
local_customs: Roads can close in heavy snow; check alerts before travelling.
food: Chapli kebab, corn and hot tea.
shopping: Shawls, woollens and wooden crafts.
tips: Avoid peak snowfall weekends unless roads are confirmed open.

name: Gurdwara Janam Asthan
name_ur: گوردوارہ جنم استھان‎
short_description: Sikh gurdwara near Lahore, Pakistan
description: Gurdwara Janam Asthan, also known as Gurdwara Nankana Sahib, is a gurdwara, and one of the holiest sites of Sikhism, located in Nankana Sahib, Punjab, Pakistan. It is situated at the site where Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, was born. It is officially listed as a 'Protected Heritage Monument' by the Government of Punjab, Pakistan; and is managed by the Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee under the federal government of Pakistan.

name: Kartarpur Corridor
name_ur: کرتارپور راہداری‎
short_description: Border corridor between the neighbouring nations of India and Pakistan
description: The Kartarpur Corridor is a visa-free border crossing and religious corridor, connecting two gurdwaras, Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, near Narowal in Pakistan and Gurudwara Dera Baba Nanak, Gurdaspur district, Punjab, India. The crossing allows devotees from India to visit the gurdwara in Kartarpur, Pakistan, 4.7 kilometres from the India–Pakistan border on the Pakistani side without a visa. Pakistani Sikhs are unable to use the border crossing, and cannot access Dera Baba Nanak on the Indian side without first obtaining an Indian visa or unless they work there.

name: Khabeki Lake
name_ur: کھبیکی جھیل
short_description: Lake in Punjab, Pakistan
description: Khabikki Lake is a saltwater lake in the Soan Sakaser Valley in the southern Salt Range in Khushab District, Punjab, Pakistan.. It is a part of the Uchhali Wetlands Complex. In 1976, it was designated a Ramsar site, the first such site in Pakistan.

name: Uchhali Lake
name_ur: اوچھالی
short_description: Saltwater lake in Soan Sakaser Valley in the southern Salt Range area in Pakistan
description: Uchhali is a saltwater lake in Soan Sakaser Valley in the southern Salt Range area in the province of Punjab, Pakistan. This lake is formed due to the absence of drainage in the range.

name: Shrine of Baba Farid
name_ur: درگاہ بابا فرید
short_description: Notable religious site located in Pakpattan.
description:
The Shrine of Baba Farid is a 13th-century Sufi dargah shrine located in Pakpattan, Punjab, Pakistan dedicated to the Punjabi Sufi mystic and poet Baba Farid. The shrine is one of the most important in Pakistan,
and was among the first Islamic holy sites in South Asia – providing the region's Muslims a local focus for devotion. The shrine is also revered by Sikhs, who include Baba Farid's poetry into the Guru Granth Sahib – regarded by Sikhs to be the eternal Guru.

name: The Memorial Mosque
name_ur: بیتِ یادگار
short_description: One of the earliest mosques in Rabwah
description: The Memorial Mosque or Yādgār Masjid, commonly known as Bait-e-Yādgār, is one of the oldest mosques of Rabwah, in Punjab, Pakistan. It is located in the Fazl-e-Omar Hospital, and built in 1958, on the site where Zuhr prayer was offered in September 1948, on the occasion of the inauguration of the new centre.

name: Jinnah Park
name_ur: جناح پارک
short_description: Park in Rawalpindi, Pakistan
description: Jinnah Park is an amusement and public park located on Airport Road in the high-security Chaklala Cantonment suburb of Rawalpindi, Pakistan. It is the town's primary amusement park and covers an area of approximately 17 hectares. Initial plans for its development began as early as 1995 and it was opened in 2006. It was named after Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the founder and first Governor-General of Pakistan. Sculptures of Jinnah and his family name are placed at the park's main entrance.

name: Azeem Masjid
name_ur: عظیم مسجد
short_description: Village in Dera Ghazi Khan district of Punjab, Pakistan
description: Basti Azeem is a village in Dera Ghazi Khan district of Punjab, Pakistan, which is named by Haji Muhammad Azeem Khan Gurchani (Waliyani). This village is located near Indus Highway, 45 km from Dera Ghazi Khan. Hiltorent Sori is located in southern side of this village. The main occupation of the people of this village is agriculture. Wheat, cotton and vegetables are important crops of this area. The Saraiki and Urdu languages are used in this village.

name: Hiran Minar complex
name_ur: ہرن مینار
short_description: Complex in Sheikhupura, Pakistan
description: Hiran Minar is an early 17th-century Mughal-era complex in Sheikhupura, in the Pakistani province of Punjab. It was built at the site of a game reserve in memory of Mughal Emperor Jahangir's beloved pet antelope, Mansraj. The emperor is remembered for his fondness of nature, and the complex embodies the Mughal relationship between humans, pets and hunting.

name: Sheikhupura Fort
name_ur: شیخوپورہ قلعہ
short_description: Mughal-Era Fort
description: Sheikhupura Fort is a 17th-century Mughal-era fort near the city of Sheikhupura in Punjab, Pakistan.

name: Pakistan Air Force Museum
name_ur: پاکستان ایئر فورس میوزیم
short_description: Museum in Karachi, Pakistan
description: Pakistan Air Force Museum Faisal is the main museum of the Pakistan Air Force located on the south-western edge of PAF Base Faisal near Karsaz Flyover on Shahrah-e-Faisal at Karachi.
image_credit: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (Pakistan Air Force Museum)

name: Pangrio Desert Gateway & Shrines
name_ur: پنگریو صحرائی گیٹ وے و صوفی مزارات بدین
short_description: Gateway town where irrigated Badin farmland transitions into the vast sand dunes of the Thar Desert.
description: Famed for its peaceful Sufi shrines and annual folk fairs, Pangrio offers stunning visual contrasts between emerald green rice fields and the golden sands of the Thar Desert.

name: Luari Sharif Historic Sufi Seminary
name_ur: لواری شریف تاریخی صوفی درسگاہ بدین
short_description: Celebrated 18th-century Naqshbandi theological school preserving Islamic manuscripts and calligraphy.
description: Operating alongside the grand Dargah of Khwaja Muhammad Zaman, this historic madrasa has educated generations of scholars in Persian mysticism, Quranic exegesis, and humanitarian ethics.

name: Sindh Agriculture University Campus (Tando Jam)
name_ur: سندھ زرعی یونیورسٹی کیمپس ٹنڈو جام حیدرآباد
short_description: Pakistan's premier agricultural university campus and botanical research groves established in 1940.
description: Spanning hundreds of acres of experimental fields, research laboratories, and shaded mango orchards, Tando Jam educates the nation's agronomists, horticulturists, and veterinarians.

name: Bojohaghur I
name_ur: بوجوہاغور اول
short_description: Notable nature site located in Karimabad.
description: Bojohagur or Bojohaghur Duanasir is a summit in the Batura Muztagh, a subrange of the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. It is the west summit of a short ridge whose high point is Ultar Sar, also known as Bojohaghur Duanasir II. It lies about 10 km (6.2 mi) northeast of the Karimabad, a town on the Karakoram Highway in the Hunza Valley, part of the Hunza District of Gilgit-Baltistan.

name: Choricho
name_ur: چوریچو
short_description: Notable nature site located in Shigar District.
description: Mountain in Pakistan

name: Amluk-Dara stupa
name_ur: املوک دارا اسٹوپا
short_description: Amluk-Dara stupa is located in Swat valley of Pakistan.
description: Amluk-Dara stupa is located in Swat valley of Pakistan. It is a part of Gandhara civilization at Amluk-Dara. The stupa is believed to have been built in the third century. The stupa was first discovered by a Hungarian-British archaeologist Sir Aurel Stein in 1926. It was later studied by Domenico Faccena in the 60s and 70s.

name: Balochistan Sphinx
name_ur: ابوالہول بلوچستان
short_description: Natural rock formation in Balochistan, Pakistan
description: Hingol National Park or Hungol National Park is the largest national park in Pakistan, located in the Makran coastal region of Balochistan along the Arabian Sea. The park covers an area of about 6,100 square kilometres (2,400 sq mi) and is located 200 km northwest of Karachi in the three districts of Gwadar, Lasbela and Awaran in Balochistan. Hingol was declared a national park in 1988.
image_credit: Bilal Mirza from Kuala Lumpur/ Hong Kong / Dubai

name: Bashigram Lake
name_ur: بشیگرام جھیل
short_description: Notable nature site located in Bilkanai.
description: Bashigram Lake also known as Bashigram Danda in Pashto is an alpine glacial lake located to the eastern side of Madyan in Swat District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan.

name: Sirkap
name_ur: سرکپ
short_description: Archaeological site near Taxila, Punjab, Pakistan
description: Sirkap is the name of an archaeological site on the bank opposite to the city of Taxila, Punjab, Pakistan.

name: Haveli of Nau Nihal Singh
name_ur: حویلی نحویلی نو نہال سنگھو نہال سنگھ
short_description: Monument
description: The Haveli of Nau Nihal Singh, officially known as Government Victoria Girls' High School, is a haveli (mansion) that houses a government school located in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan.

name: Neevin Mosque
name_ur: جامعہ کریمیہ نیویں مسجد
short_description: Notable religious site located in Walled City.
description: Jamia Karimia Mosque, also known as the Neevin Mosque, or Neevin Masjid, is a 15th-century mosque built during the Lodi dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. It is located in the ancient Walled City of Lahore, in Pakistan's Punjab province. It is notable for its foundation 25 feet below street level. The mosque is further noted for being one of Lahore's few remaining pre-Mughal monuments.
image_credit: The Walled City of Lahore Authority

name: Roshnai Gate
name_ur: روشنائی دروازہ
short_description: One of the historic gates of the Walled City of Lahore, Pakistan
description: Roshnai Gate is one of the thirteen gates within the Walled City of Lahore in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan. It was the main entry into Lahore for emperors and nobles during the Mughal, and later Sikh period.
image_credit: Pale blue dot at English Wikipedia

name: Gasherbrum VI
name_ur: گیشربرم ششم
short_description: Mountain
description: Gasherbrum VI, also known as Chochordin Peak, is a 6979m mountain in the Gasherbrum massif, located in the Karakoram range of Gilgit–Baltistan, Pakistan. Gasherbrum VI lies on a ridge south of the main crest. This ridge leads west to Gasherbrum V and then north to Gasherbrum IV. The mountain is considered unclimbed.

name: Gasherbrum VII
name_ur: گیشربرم ہفتم
short_description: Mountain
description: Mountain

name: Farid Gate
name_ur: فرید گیٹ
short_description: One of the historic gates of the Old City of Bahawalpur, Pakistan
description: One of the historic gates of the Old City of Bahawalpur, Pakistan

name: Damas Lake
name_ur: دماس جھیل
short_description: Lake in Punjab, Pakistan
description: Lake in Punjab, Pakistan

name: Hachindar Chhish
name_ur: ہچندر چھش
short_description: Notable nature site located in Aliabad.
description: Mountain in Pakistan
