short_description: Modern cultural and learning hub in Clifton hosting digital archives, book clubs, and cultural exhibitions.
description: A premier international library space featuring extensive English literature collections, public lectures, creative writing workshops, and educational resources.

name: Liaquat Memorial National Library
name_ur: لیاقت میموریل نیشنل لائبریری کراچی
short_description: National legal depository library on Stadium Road preserving hundreds of thousands of rare manuscripts and newspapers.
description: Established in 1950, this massive public repository holds complete historical newspaper runs, United Nations depository documents, and Oriental manuscripts in Persian, Arabic, and Sindhi.

name: DHA Golf & Country Club Waterfront
name_ur: ڈی ایچ اے گالف و کنٹری کلب کراچی
short_description: Championship 18-hole coastal golf course set along the scenic mangrove waters of Gizri Creek.
description: Spread across 140 acres of lush seaside fairways, the club offers illuminated night golfing, international tournaments, and scenic dining terraces overlooking the tidal creek.

name: Karachi Marina Club (Gizri Creek)
name_ur: کراچی مرینا کلب (گیزری کریک)
short_description: Premier yachting, sailing, and marine boating marina on the protected saltwater creeks of DHA.
description: A nautical sanctuary where sailboats, luxury catamarans, and speedboats dock. Offering private boat cruises into the Arabian Sea and water sports along the Indus delta channels.

name: Karachi YMCA Ground & Heritage Hall
name_ur: کراچی وائی ایم سی اے گراؤنڈ و تاریخی ہال
short_description: Historic 1913 sports and community hub in Civil Lines that nurtured Pakistan's early badminton and hockey legends.
description: Founded in 1913, the Young Men's Christian Association campus hosted early national sporting championships, debate societies, and community theater, anchoring central Karachi's secular civic traditions for over a century.

name: Karachi Gymkhana Club
name_ur: کراچی جمخانہ کلب
short_description: 1886 colonial gentlemen's club in Civil Lines renowned for lush cricket grounds, squash courts, and colonial verandas.
description: Established in 1886, Karachi Gymkhana is one of the oldest social and sporting clubs in South Asia. Its manicured turf cricket pitch hosted first-class matches and touring international teams throughout the 20th century.

name: Karachi Club Heritage Enclave
name_ur: کراچی کلب تاریخی عمارت
short_description: 1907 elite social and cultural club on Dr. Ziauddin Ahmed Road founded as an inclusive alternative to colonial-only clubs.
description: Established in 1907 by leading Indian merchants, judges, and philanthropists, Karachi Club became the social salon where Pakistan's founding leaders gathered, surrounded by tranquil lawns and classical banquet halls.

name: Metropole Square & Heritage Corner
name_ur: میٹروپول چوک و تاریخی ورثہ کراچی
short_description: Iconic mid-century crossroads in Civil Lines connecting Saddar, Clifton, and the Cantonment.
description: Anchored by the historic 1950s Hotel Metropole, this intersection was the center of Karachi's golden post-independence cosmopolitan era, hosting visiting dignitaries, jazz musicians, and airline travelers.

name: Boat Basin Open-Air Food Street
name_ur: بوٹ بیسن اوپن ایئر فوڈ اسٹریٹ کلفٹن
short_description: Karachi's 24-hour food street in Clifton famous for cheese parathas, Balochi tikka, and sunrise breakfasts.
description: Running along Khayaban-e-Roomi, Boat Basin never sleeps. It is the premier destination for late-night foodies seeking tandoori chai, sizzling Bihari kababs, and crackling laccha parathas well past midnight.

name: Do Darya Coastal Dining Promenade
name_ur: دو دریا ساحلی فوڈ پرومیناڈ ڈی ایچ اے کراچی
short_description: Awe-inspiring seaside dining boulevard in DHA Phase 8 where restaurants extend directly on wooden decks over the Arabian Sea.
description: Stretching along the open ocean at the southeastern tip of Karachi, Do Darya features open-air restaurant decks perched above crashing ocean waves, serving fresh seafood, Peshawari karahi, and charcoal grills.

name: Guru Mandir Falooda & Chaat Street
name_ur: گرو مندر فالودہ و چاٹ اسٹریٹ کراچی
short_description: Historic crossroads renowned for century-old crushed-ice Falooda parlors, Bun Kababs, and spiced fruit chaat.
description: Located near the historic Gurumandir roundabout, this street has delighted sweet tooths for decades with towering glasses of rose syrup falooda, dense kulfa slices, and Karachi's iconic street bun kababs.

name: Zahid Nihari (Tariq Road)
name_ur: زاہد نہاری طارق روڈ کراچی
short_description: Famous Tariq Road culinary institution renowned for fragrant brown onion gravy and prime beef shank stew.
description: A staple of PECHS and Tariq Road shopping expeditions, Zahid Nihari serves robust, aromatic beef stews accompanied by piping hot sesame tandoori nans straight from clay ovens.

name: Meerath Famous Kabab House
name_ur: میرٹھ فیمس کباب ہاؤس کراچی
short_description: Historic barbecue house near Guru Mandir celebrated for tender Bihari Tikka and handmade parathas since 1954.
description: Founded by master kebabiers from Meerut, India, this legendary restaurant introduced thinly sliced marinated beef strips grilled on open wood embers, wrapped in piping hot flaky parathas.

name: Hanifia Hunter Beef (Saddar)
name_ur: حنیفیہ ہنٹر بیف صدر کراچی
short_description: Originator of Karachi's legendary cured hunter beef slices served with signature spicy green mustard sauce.
description: Invented by the Hanifia family, their cured, spiced, and slowly roasted beef brisket served in crusty burger buns with sour mustard sauce has been an iconic Karachi delicacy for over half a century.

name: Karachi Haleem (Burns Road)
name_ur: کراچی حلیم برنز روڈ
short_description: Benchmark Haleem house on Burns Road simmering seven pulses, broken wheat, and shredded beef for twelve hours.
description: Serving true artisanal Shahi Haleem garnished with golden fried onions, fresh mint, ginger juliennes, and chaat masala, Karachi Haleem defines the authentic taste of the city's festive stew.

name: Zainab Market Garment & Leather Bazaar
name_ur: زینب مارکیٹ صدر کراچی
short_description: World-famous export garment, leather jacket, denim, and brass handicraft bargain bazaar in Saddar.
description: Spanning multi-level underground basements and street shops, Zainab Market is legendary for brand-name export overruns, hand-stitched leather goods, lapis lazuli jewelry, and embroidered Kashmiri shawls.

name: Abdullah Haroon Road Electronics Market
name_ur: عبداللہ ہارون روڈ الیکٹرانکس و موبائل مارکیٹ صدر
short_description: Pakistan's largest hub for mobile phones, digital gadgets, computers, and telecommunications equipment.
description: Centering on Star City Mall and surrounding arcades, this bustling commercial zone handles thousands of daily wholesale transactions for smartphones, spare parts, and consumer tech.

name: Bolton Market Historic Wholesale Center
name_ur: بولٹن مارکیٹ تاریخی ہول سیل سینٹر کراچی
short_description: Colonial-era wholesale trade marketplace established in 1883 along historic Bunder (M.A. Jinnah) Road.
description: Originally constructed in 1883 and expanded in 1886, Bolton Market remains the mega wholesale junction connecting sea imports from Karachi Port to retail distributors across Pakistan.

name: Jodia Bazaar Historic Spice & Commodity Market
name_ur: جوڑیا بازار تاریخی مصالحہ منڈی کراچی
short_description: South Asia's bustling historical spice, grain, dry fruit, and bulk commodity trading exchange.
description: The fragrant labyrinth of Jodia Bazaar has traded cardamoms, cloves, Iranian saffron, and Afghan dry fruits since the mid-19th century, setting wholesale food prices for the entire country.

name: Timber Market (Old City Karachi)
name_ur: ٹمبر مارکیٹ اولڈ سٹی کراچی
short_description: Centuries-old timber and hardwood lumber import market serving Pakistan's shipbuilding and furniture crafts.
description: Situated near the Layari River basin, this market has supplied Burma teak, deodar pine, and African hardwoods to Karachi boat builders and master carpenters since the 1800s.

name: Hassan Ali Effendi Road Paper Market
name_ur: حسن علی آفندی روڈ پیپر مارکیٹ کراچی
short_description: Historical center of printing paper, imported cardstock, wedding invitation craft, and bookbinding.
description: The beating heart of Pakistan's printing and publishing trade, where publishers, stationery designers, and wedding planners source fine papers from mills across the world.

name: Sunday Bachat Bazaar Clifton
name_ur: اتوار بچت بازار کلفٹن کراچی
short_description: Massive weekend open-air flea and discount bazaar hosting over 1,000 canopy stalls.
description: Drawing tens of thousands of bargain hunters every Sunday, this organized canvas-tent bazaar features farm-fresh agricultural produce, export surplus apparel, crockery, and household goods at subsidized rates.

name: Jama Cloth Market (M.A. Jinnah Road)
name_ur: جامع کلاتھ مارکیٹ ایم اے جناح روڈ کراچی
short_description: Karachi's oldest and most extensive retail bridal and unstitched fabric bazaar established in 1950.
description: An essential stop for family wedding preparations, featuring hundreds of shops offering Banarsi brocades, chiffon, lawn prints, velvet, and intricate hand-embroidery work.

name: Lighthouse Flea & Thrift Bazaar
name_ur: لائٹ ہاؤس لنڈا و سیکنڈ ہینڈ مارکیٹ کراچی
short_description: Legendary thrift, vintage fashion, sports gear, and imported second-hand clothing market near Lighthouse Cinema.
description: A goldmine for vintage denim, imported hiking boots, leather luggage, and sporting goods arriving through container shipping, attracting fashion students and thrifty shoppers alike.

name: Bhanoth Historic Indus River Ferry Ghat
name_ur: بھانوٹھ تاریخی دریائے سندھ کشتی گھاٹ مٹیاری
short_description: Ancient river crossing point where wooden dhows ferry passengers and camels across the Indus to Jamshoro.
description: Commanding breathtaking views of the wide Indus river channel, Bhanoth preserves the timeless spectacle of boatmen navigating seasonal floods and sandy river islands.

name: Khyber Village Sweet Citrus & Mango Orchards
name_ur: خیبر گاؤں میٹھے مالٹے و آم کے باغات مٹیاری
short_description: Picturesque agricultural village renowned for lush citrus groves and mango estates along the canals.
description: Fed by rich irrigation distributaries, Khyber is famous across Sindh for sweet early-season mandarins, guava groves, and traditional village hospitality.

name: Mehar Historic Grain Silos & Mills
name_ur: میہر تاریخی فلور ملز و غلہ ڈپو دادو
short_description: Major wheat and rice grinding complex powering grain distribution across north-central Sindh.
description: Anchoring the northern borders of Dadu, Mehar's mill district operates around the clock during wheat harvest, surrounded by bustling grain markets and sweet shops.

name: Radhan Historic Railway Junction & Canal
name_ur: رادھن تاریخی ریلوے اسٹیشن و کینال دادو
short_description: Colonial railway hub connecting agricultural towns of western Sindh to Sukkur and Karachi.
description: Preserving red-brick colonial staff quarters and iron footbridges, Radhan remains a vital transport lifeline for passenger trains crossing through Dadu district.

name: Khairpur Nathan Shah Historic Canal Spine
name_ur: خیرپور ناتھن شاہ تاریخی نہری اسٹریٹ دادو
short_description: Lush agricultural township intersected by major drainage canals and rice paddies.
description: Serving as a major commercial center for western Dadu, this bustling town features vibrant grain markets, traditional Sindhi sweet stalls, and historic canal bridges.

name: Phulji Station Historic Grain Bazaar
name_ur: پھلجی اسٹیشن تاریخی غلہ بازار دادو
short_description: Historic railhead town renowned for wholesale onion, wheat, and oilseed auctions.
description: Lined with brick godowns and merchant offices dating to the early 20th century, Phulji is a vital trading nexus between the Kirthar foothills and the Indus plains.

name: Cadet College Petaro Heritage Grounds
name_ur: کیڈٹ کالج پٹارو تاریخی کیمپس جامشورو
short_description: Pakistan's premier residential military college campus founded in 1957 on the banks of the Indus.
description: Covering hundreds of acres of manicured parade grounds, sports complexes, and historic brick halls, Petaro has educated generations of military leaders, doctors, and statesmen.

name: Manjhand Historical Talpur Tombs & Necropolis
name_ur: مانجھند تاریخی تالپور مقابر و قبرستان جامشورو
short_description: 18th-century painted tombs featuring exquisite frescoes of royal processions, peacocks, and battles.
description: Overlooking the Indus highway, these neglected architectural jewels hold rare folk murals illustrating traditional Sindhi weaponry, horsemen, and floral patterns in vivid natural pigments.

name: Laila Peak
name_ur: لیلیٰ چوٹی
short_description: Notable nature site located in Shigar District.
description: Laila Peak in the Arundu Valley of Baltistan region, is 6,985 metres (22,917 ft) high. It was first climbed by the Hekiryou Alpine Club of Japan on 9 August 1975. The peak is one of the most beautiful peak in the range with difficult access to the summit. An important aspect of its climbing route is that, it is only accessible from ChogoLungma glacier via Arundu Valley of Shiger. The base camp is at a 3 days trek from the village. It is one of the three Laila Peaks situated in the Karakoram. The other two are in Hushe Valley and Astore Valley.

name: Peshawar Museum
name_ur: پشاور میوزیم
short_description: Museum in Peshawar
description: Museum in Peshawar

name: Jamia Masjid Gulzar-e Madina
name_ur: جامع مسجد گلزار مدینہ
short_description: Mosque in Bhagwal, Kharian tehsil, Gujrat district, Punjab, Pakistan
description: Mosque in Bhagwal, Kharian tehsil, Gujrat district, Punjab, Pakistan

name: Hawke's Bay Beach & Coastal Huts
name_ur: ہاکس بے ساحل و ہٹس کراچی
short_description: Sweeping golden sand beach on the Arabian Sea famous for rental vacation huts, camel rides, and beach buggies.
description: Named after Bladen Wilmer Hawke, this wide sandy bay provides the archetypal Karachi seaside outing with crashing surf, shaded stone cabanas, and fresh roasted corn on the cob.

name: Turtle Beach Coastal Sanctuary
name_ur: ٹرٹل بیچ ساحلی مسکن کراچی
short_description: Pristine coastal cove between Sandspit and Hawke's Bay featuring rocky tide pools and soft sunbathing dunes.
description: Famous for its shallow, swimmable tides during winter months, colorful crabs scurrying along rock outcrops, and tranquil evening coastal sunsets over the Arabian Sea horizon.

name: Paradise Point Rocky Headland
name_ur: پیراڈائز پوائنٹ چٹانی ساحل کراچی
short_description: Dramatic sandstone headland on the Arabian Sea formerly featuring a famous natural stone archway carved by waves.
description: Known for its rugged coastal cliffs, deep ocean spray, and horseback riding along the shoreline, Paradise Point offers magnificent elevated vantage points over the turbulent sea.

name: Bariokhal Shish
name_ur: باریوخال شش
short_description: Notable nature site located in Bunji.
description: Peak in Pakistan

name: Shigar Fort
name_ur: قلعہ شگر
short_description: Fort in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan
description: The Shigar Palace, also known as Fong Khar, is an old palace located in the town of Shigar, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. Situated at a distance of around 30 kilometres (19 mi) from Skardu, it lies on the way which further leads to Baltoro Glacier and K2, the latter being the second highest mountain on the Earth.

name: Bahawalpur Museum
name_ur: بہاولپور میوزیم
short_description: Museum in Bahawalpur
description: Museum in Bahawalpur

name: Prahladpuri Temple
name_ur: پرھلاد پوری مندر
short_description: Destroyed Hindu temple in Multan, Pakistan
description: Prahladpuri Temple was a Hindu temple located in Multan city of Punjab province in Pakistan. The temple was located on top of a raised platform (mandapa) at the southern tip of the Multan Fort, adjacent to the Shrine of Bahauddin Zakariya. Named after Prahlada, it was dedicated to the Hindu deity Narasimha. The temple faced neglect after the formation of Pakistan, and faced destruction and land grabbing by miscreants.

name: Umarkot Fort
name_ur: عمرکوٹ قلعہ
short_description: Fort in Umerkot
description: Umarkot Fort, also called Amarkot, is a fort in Umerkot, Sindh, Pakistan, built in the Rajput style of architecture.

name: Sunera Beach Coastal Bay
name_ur: سنیرا بیچ ساحلی خلیج کراچی
short_description: Hidden coastal cove near Cape Monze with turquoise waters, sea cliffs, and peaceful camping shorelines.
description: Accessible via scenic winding tracks along the cliff tops, Sunera Beach offers pristine, uncrowded sands and dramatic rock formations ideal for stargazing and coastal bonfires.

name: Mubarak Village & Churna Island Gateway
name_ur: مبارک ولیج و چرنا آئی لینڈ گیٹ وے کراچی
short_description: Karachi's second largest traditional fishing village and the primary launching boat point for Churna Island scuba diving.
description: Set beneath jagged arid hills on the coast, Mubarak Village is inhabited by hospitable Baloch fishermen. Its harbor of colorful wooden launches ferries adventurers to Churna Island for coral reef exploration.

name: Khosar Gang
name_ur: خوسر گینگ
short_description: Khosar Gang is a mountain located in Shigar valley of Baltistan.
description:
Khosar Gang is a mountain located in Shigar valley of Baltistan. It is the tallest mountain in the Shigar Valley. The mountain is also referred to as Koser Gunge, which is how it is labeled in Google and other maps
There is controversy over the actual height of the mountain. The official height is 6400 meters, however all who have climbed the mountain claim that its actual height is 6040 meters. The highest contour curve on Google Maps is 5980 meters. The most popular and safest time to climb is July.

name: Gondogoro Pass
name_ur: گوندوگورو لا
short_description: Pakistani mountain pass
description: Gondogoro Pass is a mountain pass that stands at an elevation of 5585 meters. It is located in the Baltistan region of Pakistan, approximately 25 km south of the world's second-highest peak, K2. This pass serves as a connection between the Gondogoro Glacier to the southwest and the Vigne Glacier to the northeast.

name: Rose & Jasmine garden
name_ur: روز اور جیسمین گارڈن، اسلام آباد
short_description: Garden in Islamabad, Pakistan
description: Rose and Jasmine Garden is a public garden located within the recreational area of Shakarparian near Sports Complex Aabpara, on Kashmir Highway in Islamabad, Capital Territory, Pakistan. The garden spans 20,360 square meters and is known for its extensive collection of roses, featuring approximately 250 distinct varieties. In addition to roses, it also hosts about 150 species of jasmine.

name: Gorkhatri Tehsil
name_ur: گور کھٹری
short_description: Archaeological site in Peshawar, Pakistan
description: Gor Khatri is an archeological site located in Peshawar, Pakistan. It was built in the Mughal-era by Jehan Ara Begum, daughter of Shah Jahan, as a caravanserai.

name: Shri Varun Dev Mandir (Manora Island)
name_ur: شری ورن دیو مندر منوڑا جزیرہ کراچی
short_description: Ancient seaside Hindu temple on Manora Island dedicated to Varuna, the Vedic lord of the oceans and water.
description: Featuring ornate carved sandstone shikhara architecture dating back to the 16th century and reconstructed in 1917, this seaside sanctum preserves rare nautical religious heritage in Pakistan.

name: China Port (South Asia Terminal Breakwater)
name_ur: چائنا پورٹ بریک واٹر کلفٹن کراچی
short_description: Massive engineered sea breakwater wall of interlocking tetrapods extending deep into the Arabian Sea.
description: Constructed to shield the South Asia Pakistan Deep Water Terminal from monsoon tidal swells, this sweeping promenade became a viral sensation for sea gazing and breeze catching.

name: Clifton Sea View Beach & Promenade
name_ur: کلفٹن سی ویو ساحل و واک وے کراچی
short_description: Karachi's most iconic public urban beach, bustling with dune buggies, camel rides, and sea breeze walkers.
description: The democratic living room of Karachi where families of all backgrounds gather in the hundreds of thousands every weekend to wet their feet in the Arabian Sea waves and watch the setting sun.

name: National Academy of Performing Arts (Hindu Gymkhana)
name_ur: نیشنل اکیڈمی آف پرفارمنگ آرٹس (ہندو جمخانہ) کراچی
short_description: 1925 Rajasthani Rajput-Mughal heritage palace hosting Pakistan's premier national theater and music academy.
description: Designed by Agha Ahmed Hussain in 1925 with scalloped stone jharokas, chattris, and cupolas. Now home to NAPA, where Zia Mohyeddin spearheaded the revival of classical Pakistani drama.

name: Laila Peak (Rupal Valley)
name_ur: لیلی چوٹی (وادی روپل)
short_description: Notable nature site located in Neelam Valley District.
description: Laila Peak is a major prominence at the southwestern terminus of the Rupal Valley in Pakistan. The peak soars 6,132 metres (20,118 ft) above sea level and some 7,500 feet (2,290 m) above the Rupal Valley floor. To its north lies the Rupal Glacier and to its east lies 5,642-metre (18,510 ft) Rupal Peak. To the north of the Rupal Glacier stands the Nanga Parbat massif, one of largest in the world. Nanga Parbat itself soars 8,126 m (26,660 ft) above sea level. About its flanks stand numerous notable peaks including Rakhiot Peak, Chongra Peak, Shaigiri and Mazeno Peak.

name: Rakhiot
name_ur: رائے کوٹ
short_description: Mountain in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, subpeak of Nanga Parbat
description: Rakhiot Peak is a peak in the Himalayas range of the Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. It is one of the many subsidiary summits of the Nanga Parbat massif.

name: Turpin Peak
name_ur: ترپن چوٹی
short_description: Notable nature site located in Astore District.
description: Peak of the Nanga Parbat group in Pakistan

name: Baltoro Kangri
name_ur: بلتورو کنگری
short_description: Notable nature site located in Shigar District.
description: Baltoro Kangri is a mountain of the Karakoram mountain range in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. Baltoro Kangri is the 82nd highest mountain in the world with an elevation of 7,312 metres (23,990 ft). It lies to the south of the Gasherbrums and east of Chogolisa Peak. The huge Baltoro Glacier rises from the foot of Baltoro Kangri. On the northern side of Baltoro Kangri lies the Abruzzi Glacier.

name: Pakistan Museum of Natural History
name_ur: پاکستان میوزیم آف نیچرل ہسٹری
short_description: Natural history museum in Capital Territory, Pakistan
description: Pakistan Museum of Natural History (PMNH), (Urdu: عجائب خانہ جاتِ پاکستان برائے طبعی تواریخ) established in 1976, is a public natural history museum situated in Islamabad, the federal capital of Pakistan.

name: Ashoka Rocks
name_ur: مانسہرہ سنگی فرمان
short_description: Notable attraction site located in Mansehra.
description: Mansehra Rock Edicts are fourteen edicts of the Mauryan emperor Ashoka, inscribed on rocks in Mansehra in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The edicts are cut into three boulders and date back to 3rd century BC and they are written in the ancient Indic script of Gandhara culture, Kharosthi. The edicts mention aspects of Ashoka’s dharma. The site was submitted for inclusion in the World Heritage Sites and is currently in the tentative list.

name: Noshaq
name_ur: نوشاخ
short_description: Mountain in Afghanistan/Pakistan
description: Noshaq is a 7,492 m (24,580 ft) high peak in the Hindu Kush lying on the border of Afghanistan and Pakistan. It is the highest mountain in Afghanistan, the second highest in the Hindu Kush after Terich Mir, and the 52nd highest in the world. It is also the westernmost 7,000 m (22,966 ft) peak in the world.

name: T2F (The Second Floor) Cultural Space
name_ur: دی سیکنڈ فلور (ٹی ٹو ایف) ثقافتی کیفے کراچی
short_description: Pioneering independent community cafe, art space, and open-mic sanctuary founded by Sabeen Mahmud in DHA.
description: Established in 2007, T2F sparked a cultural movement in Karachi by providing an uncurated public space for critical dialogue, indie acoustic music, poetry slams, and contemporary art debates.

name: Pakistan Air Force (PAF) Museum Karsaz
name_ur: پاکستان ایئر فورس (پی اے ایف) میوزیم کارساز کراچی
short_description: Vast aviation museum and landscaped aircraft park on Shahrah-e-Faisal featuring historic fighter jets and bombers.
description: Preserving Pakistan's aerial combat history, the museum displays the Vickers Viking aircraft used by Quaid-e-Azam Jinnah, legendary 1965 Sabre jets, Mirage interceptors, and scale aviation galleries.

name: Karachi Planetarium & Aerospace Park
name_ur: کراچی پلانیٹیریم و ہوابازی پارک
short_description: Astronomical education center on University Road housing an authentic retired Boeing 720 passenger jetliner.
description: Featuring a sky projection dome that screens cosmic journeys through constellations and planets, alongside an actual cockpit walk-through of Pakistan International Airlines' historic passenger aircraft.

name: Distaghil Sar
name_ur: دستاغل سر
short_description: Mountain in Karakoram mountain range
description: Disteghil Sar or Distaghil Sar is the highest mountain in the Baltin Bar Nallah Shishkat, Hunza. It is part of the Karakoram mountain range in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. It is the 19th-highest mountain on Earth, the 7th-highest in Pakistan, and the first of the high peaks after Shishapangma to be the tallest independent summit of its own subrange. The mountain has a 3-kilometre-long (1.9 mi) top ridge above 7,400 meters elevation, with three distinct summits: Northwest, 7,885 m; Central, 7,760 m; and Southeast, 7,696m or 7,535m.

name: Chogolisa
name_ur: چھوغو لیسا
short_description: Notable nature site located in Shigar District.
description: Chogolisa is a trapezoidal mountain located in the Karakoram range within the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan. It is situated near the Baltoro Glacier in the Concordia region, which is renowned for hosting some of the world's tallest peaks.

name: Istor-o-Nal
name_ur: استور و نل
short_description: Notable nature site located in Upper Chitral District.
description: Istor-o-Nal is the third highest mountain in the Hindu Kush range, in the Chitral District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province in Pakistan. It is the 68th highest independent peak in the world. It crowns a massif with eleven peaks of elevation more than 7,000 m (22,966 ft).

name: Harappa
name_ur: ہڑپہ
short_description: Archaeological site in Punjab, Pakistan
description: Harappa was a settlement in Punjab, Pakistan, about 24 kilometres west of Sahiwal, that takes its name from a modern village near the former course of the Ravi River. The Ravi now runs eight kilometres to the north.

name: The Dawood Foundation MagnifiScience Centre
name_ur: دی داؤد فاؤنڈیشن میگنیفی سائنس سینٹر کراچی
short_description: Pakistan's premier interactive contemporary science and technology discovery center in the Old Railway Quarter.
description: Spanning four storeys of hands-on physical exhibits, living mangrove biomes, sound resonance chambers, and renewable energy simulators designed to inspire generations of young scientists.

name: Citizens Archive of Pakistan Heritage Center
name_ur: سٹیزنز آرکائیو آف پاکستان ورثہ سینٹر کراچی
short_description: Dedicated oral history archive and partition memory museum preserving thousands of eyewitness testimonies.
description: Pioneered by Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy to safeguard the personal stories of the 1947 partition generation through interactive audiovisual booths, historical letters, and vintage passport exhibits.

name: VM Art Gallery (Rangoonwala Community Centre)
name_ur: وی ایم آرٹ گیلری رنگون والا سینٹر کراچی
short_description: Prominent contemporary art institution in Dhoraji nurturing emerging Pakistani painters, sculptors, and printmakers.
description: Operating since 1987 under Zubeida Mustafa's stewardship, VM Art Gallery runs extensive non-profit residency programs, printmaking workshops, and provocative contemporary art showcases.

name: Chawkandi Art Gallery Clifton
name_ur: چوکنڈی آرٹ گیلری کلفٹن کراچی
short_description: Pioneering private contemporary art gallery founded by Zohra Hussain in 1984 representing masters like Jamil Naqsh.
description: A cornerstone of the South Asian modern art movement, Chawkandi has nurtured four decades of Pakistani contemporary visual arts, ceramics, miniature painting, and sculpture.

name: Masherbrum
name_ur: ماشربرم
short_description: Mountain in Pakistan, the highest peak of Masherbrum Mountains
description: Masherbrum is a mountain located in the Ghanche District in the Gilgit Baltistan region of Pakistan. With an elevation of 7,821 metres, it ranks as the 22nd highest mountain globally and the 9th highest in Pakistan.

name: Masjid Tooba
name_ur: مسجد طوبیٰ‎
short_description: Mosque in Karachi, Pakistan
description: Masjid-e-Tooba also known as Gol Masjid, is a mosque located in the city of Karachi in Sindh province of Pakistan. It is situated near the main Korangi Road in Phase II of the Defence Housing Authority, Karachi.

name: Falak Sher
name_ur: فلک سر
short_description: Mountain in Hindu Kush Mountains, Pakistan
description: Falak Sar is a 5,918 metres (19,416 ft) high mountain peak located in the Hindu Kush Range at the junction of Swat Valley and Kandia Valley in Pakistan. It is the highest mountain peak in Swat Valley, followed by Mankial Sar.

name: Clock Tower
name_ur: گھنٹہ گھر، سیالکوٹ
short_description: Clock tower in Punjab, Pakistan
description: The Clock Tower, Sialkot, commonly called Ghanta Ghar, is a five-storey brick clock tower that dominates Iqbal Square in Sialkot Cantonment, Punjab, Pakistan. Completed late in the period of British India, the tower remains the city's most recognisable civic landmark and a fixed point around which commercial life in the adjoining Saddar Bazaar revolves.

name: Malir Valley Green Orchards & Farms
name_ur: ملیر وادی سرسبز باغات و فارم ہاؤسز کراچی
short_description: Karachi's traditional green agricultural oasis along the Malir River bed renowned for guava, papaya, and vegetable crops.
description: Historically supplying fresh produce to the colonial port city, Malir's lush farms, shaded date groves, and weekend agro-retreats offer a cool countryside sanctuary within the metropolis.

name: Damloti Historic Wells Waterworks Malir
name_ur: ڈملوٹی تاریخی کنویں و واٹر ورکس ملیر کراچی
short_description: 1880s colonial stone-engineered gravity well system that provided Karachi's first filtered piped municipal drinking water.
description: Engineered by British municipal hydrologist James Strachan, these massive stone conduit wells tapped underground subterranean aquifers along the Malir River, pumping millions of gallons of sweet water to the city.

name: Hub Dam Lake & Wildlife Sanctuary
name_ur: حب ڈیم جھیل و جنگلی حیات کی پناہ گاہ کراچی
short_description: Vast 24,000-acre freshwater reservoir on the Sindh-Balochistan border providing boating, fishing, and migratory bird watching.
description: Constructed in 1981 across the Hub River, this sprawling blue lake surrounded by jagged rocky hills is a designated Ramsar wetland site hosting thousands of pelicans, ducks, and cranes every winter.

name: Gadap Valley Agro-Farms & Hills
name_ur: گڈاپ وادی فروٹ باغات و پہاڑیاں کراچی
short_description: Sprawling hilly agricultural region of northern Karachi renowned for organic vegetable cultivation and desert hills.
description: Nestled against the southern foothills of the Kirthar range, Gadap is home to indigenous Sindhi and Baloch rural villages, historic water check-dams, and expansive farm resort estates.

name: Kathore Archaeological Mounds & Riverbed
name_ur: کتھور قدیم آثار و ندی کراچی
short_description: Ancient prehistoric settlement mounds and historic caravanserai crossroads on the old trade route to Sehwan.
description: Located along the Super Highway corridor, Kathore holds ancient burial mounds, petroglyphs, and medieval staging posts where camel trains rested on journeys from Thatta to central Sindh.

name: Chawkandi Tombs UNESCO Tentative Necropolis
name_ur: چوکنڈی قبرستان تاریخی مقابر کراچی
short_description: 15th to 18th century intricately carved yellow sandstone funerary necropolis built by Baloch and Jokhio tribes.
description: Renowned worldwide for pyramidal sandstone tombs adorned with exquisite relief carvings of horsemen, swords, jewelry, and geometric filigree without using mortar, representing unmatched folk Islamic sepulchral art.

name: Chaqchan Mosque
name_ur: خانقاہِ چقچن
short_description: Mosque in Khaplu, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan
description: The Chaqchan Mosque is a Sufi Noorbakshia mosque, located in the city of Khaplu, in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of northern Pakistan. Dating from 1370, the mosque is one of the oldest in the region, from the time when the area's populace converted en masse from Tibetan Buddhism to Islam. The mosque has architecture similar to that of mosques built in the Kashmir Valley. It features a blend of Tibetan, Mughal and Persian styles of architecture.

name: Buni Zom
name_ur: بونی زوم
short_description: Mountain in Hindu Raj Mountains
description: The Buni Zom group is a prominent mountain area of Chitral, in the Hindu Raj range of Pakistan. Buni Zom (main) is the highest peak of the group with an elevation of 6,542 m (21,463 ft). It is located about 50 km (30 mi) northeast of the town of Chitral, and about 50 km (30 mi) east of Tirich Mir, the highest peak in the Hindu Kush.

name: Peucelaotis
name_ur: پشکلاوتی
short_description: Archaeological site in Pakistan, former capital of the Gandhara kingdom
description: Pushkalavati was the capital of the ancient region of Gandhāra in modern-day northwestern Pakistan. Its ruins are located on the outskirts of the modern city of Charsadda in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 35–42 kilometres northeast of Peshawar, at the banks of Jindi River, near the junction of Swat River with Kabul River. The earliest archaeological remains in Bala Hisar mound are from 1400 to 800 BCE. Pushkalavati may have been incorporated as an Achaemenid regional settlement around 520 BCE, and it remained an important city through to the beginning of the 3rd century CE.

name: Chitral Museum
name_ur: چترال میوزیم
short_description: Museum in Chitral
description: Museum in Chitral

name: Shrine of Khawaja Gulam Freed
name_ur: جواجہ غلام فرید کا دربار
short_description: 19th-century sufi Punjabi poet of the punjab , polyglot, scholar and writer
description: Khawaja Ghulam Farid was a 19th-century Sufi poet and mystic from Bahawalpur, Punjab, belonging to the Chishti Order. Most of his work is in his mother tongue Multani, or what is now known as Saraiki. However, he also contributed to the Standard Punjabi, Urdu, Pashto, Sindhi, Hindi and Persian literature. His writing style is characterized by the integration of themes such as death, passionate worldly and spiritual love, and the grief associated with love.

name: Hub River Gorge & Camel Crossings
name_ur: حب ندی گھاٹی و روایتی اونٹ کراسنگ
short_description: Scenic natural rocky defile along the Hub River marking the provincial boundary between Sindh and Balochistan.
description: Carving through barren limestone ridges, the Hub riverbed features seasonal freshwater pools, desert acacia groves, and rugged hiking terrain popular for off-road expeditions.

name: Karachi Safari Park & Swan Lake
name_ur: کراچی سفاری پارک و ہنس جھیل گلشن اقبال
short_description: Massive 148-acre public wildlife safari park in Gulshan-e-Iqbal featuring drive-through animal enclosures and chairlifts.
description: Opened in 1970, Safari Park features a natural hill terrain holding a large swan boating lake, aviary, children's amusement zones, and drive-through viewing of nilgai, deer, and exotic waterfowls.

name: Sann Heritage Town & G.M. Syed Memorial
name_ur: سان تاریخی قصبہ و جی ایم سید یادگار جامشورو
short_description: Historic riverfront town in Jamshoro district and resting place of Sindhi philosopher G.M. Syed.
description: The gateway to the Great Wall of Sindh (Ranikot Fort), Sann has been a political and literary pilgrimage destination for Sindhi scholars, poets, and students for over half a century.

name: K6 Peak
name_ur: بلتستانی چوٹی
short_description: Mountain
description: Surveyed as K6, but also known as Baltistan Peak, it is a notable peak of the Masherbrum Mountains, a subrange of the Karakoram mountain range in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan. Despite being much lower than the adjoining Eight-thousanders and high 7000m peaks such as Masherbrum, K6 has huge, steep faces, and great relief above the nearby valleys.

name: Kohe Shakawr
name_ur: کوہِ شاکاور
short_description: Mountain in Afghanistan/Pakistan
description: Mountain in Afghanistan/Pakistan

name: Shuhada
name_ur: شہداء
short_description: Place of worship in Lahore
description: Place of worship in Lahore

name: Shams Pir Island
name_ur: جزیرہ شمس پیر
short_description: Notable viewpoint site located in Mauripur.
description: Shamspir is a populated island off the coast of Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan. The village on the island, administratively part of Keamari District, is home to approximately 5,000 residents.

name: Bagh Ibn-e-Qasim Seaside Mega Park
name_ur: باغ ابنِ قاسم ساحلی میگا پارک کلفٹن کراچی
short_description: South Asia's largest urban seaside park spanning 130 manicured acres between Clifton Beach and Jahangir Kothari Parade.
description: Featuring sweeping stone canopies, illuminated promenades, undulating rose lawns, and stone obelisks overlooking the sea, connecting seamlessly with the shrine of Abdullah Shah Ghazi.

name: Aziz Bhatti Park & Boating Lake
name_ur: عزیز بھٹی پارک و بوٹنگ جھیل گلشن اقبال کراچی
short_description: Sprawling family park named after Major Raja Aziz Bhatti NH featuring an expansive freshwater boating lake.
description: A beloved family sanctuary in District East, Aziz Bhatti Park features mature eucalyptus and banyan groves, scenic paddle boating around a central fountain, and children's amusement areas.

name: Polo Ground (Bagh-e-Jinnah Baradari)
name_ur: پولو گراؤنڈ (باغِ جناح بارہ دری) سول لائنز کراچی
short_description: Historic colonial polo field and lush public park featuring an authentic carved marble Mughal Baradari pavilion.
description: Host to historic military parades, civic receptions for visiting world leaders, and premier flower shows, this tranquil park features manicured hedges and a historic marble-pillared pavilion.

name: Diran
name_ur: دیرن
short_description: Notable nature site located in Aliabad.
description: Diran is a mountain in the Karakoram range in Bagrot Valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. This 7,266-metre (23,839 ft), pyramid-shaped mountain lies to the east of Rakaposhi (7,788m).

name: Laila Peak
name_ur: لیلی چوٹی
short_description: Notable nature site located in Ghanche District.
description: Laila Peak is a mountain located in the Hushe Valley, near the Gondogoro Glacier within the Karakoram. Situated in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan, Laila Peak has an elevation of 6,096 metres (20,000 ft). Its distinctive feature is its spear-like shape, and its northwest face presents a challenging slope of 45 degrees, spanning over 1,500 vertical meters. The height of Laila Peak in the Hushe Valley has been a subject of controversy and discrepancy. Various sources and maps have mentioned different elevations for the peak. Some believe it to be around 6,200 meters, while others suggest it as 6,614 metres (21,699 ft). However, according to a Japanese mountaineering map by Tsuneo Miyamori published in 2003, the height of Laila Peak is listed as 6,096 meters.

name: Kargah Buddha
name_ur: کارگاہ بدھا
short_description: Kargah Buddha is an archaeological site located about 6 miles (9.7 km) outside of Gilgit, Gilgit−Baltistan, Pakistan.
description: Kargah Buddha is an archaeological site located about 6 miles (9.7 km) outside of Gilgit, Gilgit−Baltistan, Pakistan. It is a carved image of a large standing Buddha, some 50 ft (15 m) high, in the cliff-face in Kargah Nala. The carving, which is in a style also found in Baltistan, is estimated to date back to the 7th century.

name: Sakar Sar
name_ur: ساکر سر
short_description: Mountain in Afghanistan/Pakistan
description: Sakar Sar is a mountain peak located at 6,272 metres above sea level. It lies in the Hindu Kush-Karakoram, in part in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan and in part in Afghanistan's Wakhan Corridor.

name: Hunza Peak
name_ur: ہنزہ چوٹی
short_description: Mountain in Gilgit-Baltistan (Pakistan)
description: Hunza Peak lies in the westernmost subrange of the Karakoram range in Pakistan, along with the Ladyfinger Peak (Bublimating). It lies on the southwest ridge of the Ultar Sar massif, the most southeasterly of the major groups of the Batura Muztagh. The whole massif rises precipitously above the Hunza Valley to the southeast.

name: Ladyfinger Peak
name_ur: لیڈی فنگر
short_description: Notable nature site located in Karimabad.
description: The Bublimotin, Bubli Motin, Bublimating or Ladyfinger Peak, is a distinctive rock spire in the Batura Muztagh, the westernmost subrange of the Karakoram range in Pakistan. It lies on the southwest ridge of the Ultar Sar massif, the most southeasterly of the major groups of the Batura Muztagh. The whole massif rises precipitously above the Hunza Valley to the southeast.

name: Amb temples
name_ur: انب شریف مندر
short_description: Notable religious site located in Quaidabad.
description: The Amb Temples, are part of an abandoned Hindu temple complex located at the western edge of the Salt Range in Punjab, Pakistan. The temple complex was built in Gandhara Nagara style in the 9th to 10th centuries CE by the Odi Shahi dynasty.

name: Karachi Boat Club & Chinna Creek
name_ur: کراچی بوٹ کلب و چنا کریک
short_description: 1881 colonial rowing and sculling club nestled on Chinna Creek that has produced international regatta champions.
description: Established in 1881, the Karachi Boat Club is one of the oldest rowing clubs in Asia. Its timber boathouse holds fine wooden sculls, hosting annual regattas on the tidal saltwater channels.

name: Sandspit Mangrove Forest Creeks & Kayaking
name_ur: سینڈز پٹ مینگروو کریکس و کیاکنگ کراچی
short_description: Dense saltwater mangrove wetlands along Karachi harbour offering guided kayaking, crabbing, and birding.
description: Serving as coastal green lungs and natural fish nurseries, these tidal creeks are teeming with mudskippers, flamingos, and herons, drawing ecotourists for peaceful canoe paddles through narrow green water tunnels.

name: Korangi Creek Coastal Strip & Mudflats
name_ur: کورنگی کریک ساحلی پٹی و مڈ فلیٹس کراچی
short_description: Tidal saltwater creek system bordering Ibrahim Hyderi, famous for fishing dhows and coastal bird sanctuaries.
description: A bustling maritime ecosystem where hundreds of wooden motorized fishing boats dock alongside intertidal mudflats that support migratory waders and rich artisanal crab fishing.

name: Banaras Silk Weavers Colony (Orangi)
name_ur: بنارس سلک ویورز کالونی اورنگی کراچی
short_description: Historic artisan settlement of master Muslim weavers from Varanasi practicing hereditary pure silk jacquard weaving.
description: Settled in the 1950s, this neighborhood houses thousands of traditional wooden handlooms and jacquard powerlooms crafting opulent Banarsi saris, gold-thread zari brocades, and bridal silk dupattas.

name: Baldia Town Gateway & RCD Highway
name_ur: بلدیہ ٹاؤن گیٹ وے و آر سی ڈی شاہراہ کراچی
short_description: Historic overland commercial transit gateway linking Karachi to Balochistan, Iran, and Turkey along the RCD Highway.
description: Lined with ornate truck art workshops, Balochi tea hotels, and wholesale tire and transport logistics centers that have powered Pakistan's trans-regional overland freight for decades.

name: Hispar Sar
name_ur: ہسپر سر
short_description: Mountain in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan
description: Mountain in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan

name: Kanjut Sar II
name_ur: کنجوت سر دوم
short_description: Notable nature site located in Nagar District.
description: Summit in Pakistan

name: Swat Museum
name_ur: سوات میوزیم
short_description: Museum in Mingora, Pakistan
description: Swat Museum is a museum located in Saidu Sharif, on the road connecting Mingora and Saidu Sharif in the Swat District of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan.

name: Saraghrar I
name_ur: سراغرار
short_description: Fourth highest independent peak in the Hindu Kush, Pakistan
description: Saraghrar is the fourth-highest independent peak in the Hindu Kush and located in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The entire Saraghrar massif is a huge, irregularly stretched plateau at elevation around 7,000 m (22,966 ft), lying above vertical granite and ice faces, which protects it all around. Its distinct summits are poorly identified, and information gathered from expeditions that have visited the area is often misleading. The main summits are: NE summit, northwest summit, southwest summit, south summit, and southeast summit.

name: Landhi Historic Dairy & Cattle Colony
name_ur: لانڈھی تاریخی ڈیری و کیٹل کالونی کراچی
short_description: One of the world's largest concentrated dairy settlements supplying fresh milk and cream to Karachi.
description: Established in 1958, this immense livestock township houses nearly half a million dairy buffaloes and cows, showcasing the colossal logistics that feed milk tea (chai) to a mega city of 20 million people.

name: Liaquatabad (Lalu Khet) Super Market
name_ur: لیاقت آباد (لالو کھیت) سپر مارکیٹ کراچی
short_description: Legendary working-class shopping nexus renowned for gold jewelry, unstitched cottons, and bird bazaars.
description: Dating back to the establishment of Liaquatabad in the early 1950s, Lalu Khet Super Market is celebrated for affordable bridal sets, fabric bargaining, and its famous Sunday exotic bird and pigeon exchange.

name: Tomb of Jam Nizamuddin II (Makli)
name_ur: مقبرہ جام نظام الدین ثانی مکلی ٹھٹھہ
short_description: 1509 masterpiece sandstone mausoleum of the Samma dynasty Sultan at UNESCO Makli Hill.
description: Built in 1509, this square sandstone mausoleum features exquisite stone-carved jharoka balconies, Quranic calligraphy bands, and Hindu-Islamic syncretic motifs carved directly into yellow stone without mortar.

name: Tomb of Isa Khan Tarkhan II (Makli)
name_ur: مقبرہ عیسیٰ خان ترخان ثانی مکلی ٹھٹھہ
short_description: Two-storey stone-pillared palatial mausoleum built in 1644 surrounded by pillared stone verandas.
description: Constructed in 1644 during Mughal rule, this monumental two-storey stone mausoleum features multi-tiered pillared loggias, delicate honeycomb jaali screens, and stone cenotaphs commemorating the Tarkhan governor.

name: Peak 11
name_ur: پمری چھیش
short_description: Notable nature site located in Nagar District.
description: Pumari Chhish, is a group of peaks in the Shimshal Valley, in the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. The central peak, rises to 7,492m. It lies about 4 km east of Khunyang Chhish, in the heart of the Hispar, north of the Hispar Glacier.

name: Ogre II
name_ur: اوگر دوم
short_description: Natural landmark in Shigar District
description: Natural landmark in Shigar District

name: Butkara Stupa
name_ur: بتکرا اسٹوپا
short_description: Buddhist stupa site in Mingora, Swat
description: Butkara Stupa is an ancient Buddhist stupa site in Mingora, Swat, close to the Swat Museum.

name: Tomb of Jan Baba (Makli)
name_ur: مقبرہ جان بابا مکلی ٹھٹھہ
short_description: 1608 intricately carved sandstone tomb featuring delicate mihrabs and Quranic stone calligraphy.
description: Erected in 1608 by Isa Khan Tarkhan II for his father Jan Baba, this tomb is famous for its intricate surface relief carving that resembles woodwork carved into solid living limestone.

name: Tomb of Diwan Shurfa Khan (Makli)
name_ur: مقبرہ دیوان شرفا خان مکلی ٹھٹھہ
short_description: 1638 Persian-style blue-glazed tile and red brick mausoleum crowned by a turquoise glazed dome.
description: A rare example of Persian brick architecture at Makli, featuring vibrant cobalt-blue and turquoise glazed tiles, four round corner towers, and the subterranean burial crypt of the Arghun royal minister.

name: Sonda Historic Graveyard
name_ur: سونڈا تاریخی قبرستان ٹھٹھہ
short_description: Ancient 16th-century terraced sandstone necropolis perched on a limestone ridge near Keenjhar Lake.
description: Located along the National Highway near Sonda village, this necropolis contains richly carved Chawkandi-style tombs featuring motifs of turbans, swords, and female jewelry indicating the gender of the departed.

name: Kalan Kot (Tughlaqabad) Fort Ruins
name_ur: کلان کوٹ (تغلق آباد) قلعہ کے کھنڈرات ٹھٹھہ
short_description: 14th-century medieval fortified garrison citadel overlooking the Makli ridge, built by Samma and Arghun kings.
description: Built on an ancient Hindu citadel and fortified with heavy stone ramparts and brick bastions, Kalan Kot served as a defensive military refuge during enemy sieges of the capital city of Thatta.

name: Momhil Sar
name_ur: مومہل سر
short_description: Mountain
description: Momhil Sar is, at 7,414 metres (24,324 ft) above sea level, the 64th highest mountain peak in the world. It is situated in Shimshal Valley, the Hispar Muztagh subrange of the Karakoram range, a few kilometres to the north-west of its parent peak Trivor in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan.

name: Trivor
name_ur: ترِیور
short_description: Mountain
description: Trivor is one of the high mountain peaks of the Hispar Muztagh, a subrange of the Karakoram range in the Shimshal Valley, Gilgit-Baltistan of Pakistan. Its height is often given as 7,728 metres (25,354 ft), but this elevation is not consistent with photographic evidence. The height given here is from a Russian 1:100,000 topographic map.

name: Phuparash Peak
name_ur: پھوپراش چوٹی
short_description: Notable nature site located in Nagar District.
description: Phuparash Peak is a mountain in Hispar Valley in the Gilgit District, Gilgit–Baltistan, Pakistan. It lies east of Miar Peak. The Phuparash and Miar glaciers are nearby. the peak is visible while trekking to Rush Lake.

name: Spantik
name_ur: سپانٹک
short_description: Mountain
description: Spantik, also known as Golden Peak, is a mountain situated in the Spantik-Sosbun subrange within the Karakoram range. It is located in Shigar District, of the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan. The northwest face of Spantik is dominated by a pronounced pillar of creamy yellow marble which reaches up its north face to 300 m below the summit. Its distinctive appearance has given the peak its Buruskaski name, "Ganesh Chish" or Golden Peak. This outcropping is renowned for its exceptionally challenging climbing route, famously referred to as the "Golden Pillar".

Golden_Peak.JPG: Hypernsnyper

name: Pir Patho Hilltop Shrine & Minaret
name_ur: پیر پٹھو درگاہ و تاریخی مینار ٹھٹھہ
short_description: Ancient 12th-century Sufi pilgrimage shrine and ruined brick watchtower commanding sweeping views of the Indus delta.
description: Perched on a solitary limestone outcrop in the lower delta, Pir Patho marks an ancient cultural transition point from Buddhist to early Islamic Sindh, crowned by an 800-year-old circular beacon tower.

name: Jhimpir Wind Corridor & Natural Springs
name_ur: جھمپیر ونڈ کوریڈور و قدرتی چشمے ٹھٹھہ
short_description: Pakistan's premier green energy wind farm plateau featuring cold mineral freshwater springs and rocky valleys.
description: Home to hundreds of towering modern wind turbines turning in the coastal Arabian Sea gales, Jhimpir also holds historic natural freshwater springs and the revered shrine of Sheikh Jhimpir.

name: Chilya Fish Point (Keenjhar Lake)
name_ur: چلیہ فش پوائنٹ کینجھر جھیل ٹھٹھہ
short_description: Legendary lakeside culinary hub famous for freshly caught Indus catfish and Kuriro fried in spicy Sindhi masala.
description: The ultimate roadside food stop on the National Highway, where travelers feast on hot crispy fish steaks, fresh clay oven rotis, and chilled sugarcane juice overlooking the azure waters of Keenjhar.

name: Karka
name_ur: کارکا
short_description: Notable nature site located in Ghizer District.
description: Karka is a summit in the Hindu Raj range in Northern Pakistan and has a peak elevation of 6,222 m (20,413 ft).

name: Malubiting
name_ur: مالونیتنگ
short_description: Mountain in the Rakaposhi-Haramosh Mountains in Pakistan
description: Malubiting, also known as Malubiting West, ranks as the second highest peak between the Haramosh and Hispar valleys in the Karakoram range in Pakistan. It is situated between Bilchar Dobani and Haramosh Peak, in the Gilgit-Baltistan region.

name: Sangemarmur
name_ur: سنگ مرمر سر
short_description: Pyramidal peak in the Batura Muztagh, Pakistan
description: Sangemarmar Sar, or Sangemar Mar and Sang-e-Marmar, is a pyramidal peak in the Batura Muztagh, at the end of a spur ridge running southwest from Passu Sar in Pakistan. It lies between the Muchuhar Glacier to the west, and the Shispare Glacier to the east.

name: Sherpi Kangri
name_ur: شیرپی کانگری
short_description: Mountain peak in the Karakoram range
description: Sherpi Kangri is a mountain peak in the Karakoram Range. It lies six km south of Ghent Kangri and ten km northwest of Saltoro Kangri.

name: Koyo Zom
name_ur: کویو زوم
short_description: Highest mountain of the Hindu Raj Mountains
description: Koyo Zom is the highest peak in Pakistan's Hindu Raj mountain range at 6,872 metres (22,546 ft). The Hindu Raj mountain range sits between the Hindu Kush in the west and the Karakoram in the east.

name: Hadero Lake Protected Wetland Reserve
name_ur: ہدیرو جھیل جنگلی حیات کی پناہ گاہ ٹھٹھہ
short_description: Pristine brackish wetland sanctuary designated as a national park for flamingos, pelicans, and wintering waders.
description: A tranquil haven for ornithologists and nature photographers, Hadero Lake hosts up to 50,000 migratory waterfowl each winter feeding on aquatic crustacea along its quiet reed-fringed shores.

name: Keti Bandar Indus Delta Coastal Outpost
name_ur: کیٹی بندر انڈس ڈیلٹا ساحلی بستی ٹھٹھہ
short_description: Pakistan's southernmost settlement on the active Indus River delta where freshwater branches spill into the Arabian Sea.
description: Surrounded by dense tidal mangrove channels and mudflats, Keti Bandar has survived being rebuilt three times due to coastal sea erosion, providing boat access into the remote mangrove islands.

name: Sujawal Indus Riverfront & Bridge
name_ur: سجاول دریائے سندھ کا کنارہ و تاریخی پل
short_description: Wide sweeping riverfront on the Indus River connecting Thatta and Sujawal, famous for fresh Palla fish catch.
description: A bustling delta river crossing where traditional Sindhi boatmen cast circular fishing nets from wooden boats into the muddy waters of the mighty Indus, accompanied by scenic riverside tea dhabas.

name: Biale Kangri
name_ur: بیالے کانگری
short_description: Notable nature site located in Shigar District.
description: Mountain in Pakistan

name: Great Trango Tower
name_ur: گریٹ ٹرانگو ٹاور
short_description: Mountain
description: Mountain
image_credit: Maria Ly from San Francisco, USA

name: Skil Brum
name_ur: سکل برم
short_description: Notable nature site located in Shigar District.
description: Skil Brum, or Skilbrum, is a mountain in the Karakoram range in Gilgit–Baltistan, Pakistan, approximately 9 km (5 mi) west-southwest of K2. It lies on the western side of the Godwin-Austen Glacier, roughly opposite Broad Peak.

name: Rupa Mari Archaeological Ruins (Badin)
name_ur: روپا ماڑی قدیم آثار و کھنڈرات بدین
short_description: Ancient 14th-century capital city ruins of the Soomra dynasty, immortalized in the epic love romance of Dodo Chanesar.
description: Excavations reveal extensive brick defense foundations, medieval ceramics, and burial tumuli where heroic Soomra warriors fought to defend Sindh against the invading Delhi Sultanate armies.

name: Kadhan Wetland Wildlife Reserves
name_ur: کڈھن قدرتی جھیلیں و جنگلی حیات بدین
short_description: Interconnected freshwater and brackish natural lakes hosting thousands of migratory ducks, coots, and ibises.
description: Spread across southern Badin district near the Rann of Kutch border, these untouched coastal wetlands support rare fishing cat populations, freshwater turtles, and thriving wetland fisheries.

name: Badin Irrigation Canals & Rice Fields
name_ur: بدین نہری نظام و دھان کے لہلہاتے کھیت
short_description: Lush green paddy fields and extensive irrigation canal networks that earn Badin the title of Sindh's Sugar Bowl.
description: Fed by the Kotri Barrage canal commands, Badin features emerald landscapes of Basmati rice paddies, towering sugarcane crops, and historic brick water regulators spanning the canal distributors.

name: Dargah Luari Sharif (Khwaja Muhammad Zaman)
name_ur: درگاہ لواری شریف (خواجہ محمد زمان) بدین
short_description: Revered 18th-century Naqshbandi Sufi shrine of Khwaja Muhammad Zaman attracting thousands of spiritual seekers.
description: Surrounded by tranquil palm groves, Luari Sharif is a preeminent spiritual center of Sindh renowned for preserving classical Persian mystic manuscripts, communal recitation of dhikr, and an annual Urs.

name: Koh-i-Sultan
name_ur: کوہ سلطان
short_description: Notable nature site located in Chagai District.
description: Koh-i-Sultan is a volcano in Balochistan, Pakistan. It is part of the tectonic belt formed by the collision of the Eurasian Plate and Arabian Plate: specifically, a segment influenced by the subduction of the Arabian plate beneath the Asian plate and forming a volcanic arc which includes the Bazman and Taftan volcanoes in Iran. The volcano consists of three main cones, with heavily eroded craters running west-northwest and surrounded by a number of subsidiary volcanic centres. Its summit is 2,334 metres (7,657 ft) high, and the crater associated with the Miri cone has a smaller crater inside.

name: Broad Peak
name_ur: بروڈ پیک
short_description: 12th highest mountain in the world
description: Broad Peak is the 12th highest mountain in the world at 8,051 metres (26,414 ft) elevation above sea level. It is one of the eight-thousanders, and is located in the Karakoram range spanning Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, and Xinjiang, China. The first ascent of this mountain was in June 1957, accomplished by Fritz Wintersteller, Marcus Schmuck, Kurt Diemberger, and Hermann Buhl as part of an Austrian expedition.

name: Nicholson Monument
name_ur: نکلسن کی ابلیسک
short_description: Monument in Margalla Pass, Punjab, Pakistan
description: Nicholson's Obelisk, also known as Nicholson's Memorial, is an obelisk located in Rawalpindi District, Punjab, Pakistan, which was erected in 1868 in the honour of Brigadier-General John Nicholson. It is situated at the Margalla Pass of the Margalla Hills close to the twin cities of Rawalpindi–Islamabad, en route to the historical town of Taxila.

name: Clock Tower Faisalabad
name_ur: گھنٹہ گھر
short_description: Clock tower in Faisalabad, Punjab, Pakistan
description: The Faisalabad Clock Tower, formerly known as the Lyallpur Clock Tower, is a clock tower in Faisalabad, Punjab, Pakistan. Built in 1905, it is one of the city's oldest monuments still standing in its original state.

name: Army Museum Lahore
name_ur: آرمی میوزیم لاہور
short_description: Museum in Lahore Cant
description: Museum in Lahore Cant

name: National Museum of Pakistan
name_ur: قومی عجائب گھر پاکستان
short_description: Art museum and historic site in Karachi, Pakistan
description: The National Museum of Pakistan is a public museum located in Karachi, Pakistan.

name: Manora Fort
name_ur: منوڑا قلعہ، کراچی
short_description: Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan
description: Manora Fort is a fort that was built to protect the harbour of Karachi. Originally erected as a mud fortress by the Talpur Mirs in 1797, the fort was captured by the British in 1839 - after which they seized control of Karachi and lower Sindh.

name: Seer Creek Indus Mangrove Delta
name_ur: سیر کریک انڈس مینگروو ڈیلٹا بدین
short_description: Remote tidal mangrove creek at the outer mouth of the Indus River touching the Arabian Sea salt flats.
description: An extreme coastal wilderness reachable by traditional dhows, supporting healthy stands of Avicennia marina mangroves, saltwater mud crabs, and pods of humpback dolphins breaching in the tidal channels.

name: Pacca Qila Ramparts & Mirs Harem
name_ur: پکا قلعہ فصیل و حرمِ میران حیدرآباد
short_description: 1768 monumental burnt-brick fortress built by Ghulam Shah Kalhoro on the limestone ridge of historic Nerun Kot.
description: Rising over 50 feet above Hyderabad, Pacca Qila features massive circular bastions, fortified gateways, the surviving Mirs' Harem palace with carved teakwood ceilings, and historical armory quarters.

name: Kacha Qila (Mud Fort)
name_ur: کچا قلعہ حیدرآباد
short_description: Historic defensive earthen and sun-dried mud brick fortress constructed to shelter camp followers and soldiers.
description: Built simultaneously with Pacca Qila to house the military garrisons and weapon forges, its thick mud-rammed walls and arched gates demonstrate medieval passive thermal defense architecture.

name: Haramosh
name_ur: ہراموش چوٹی
short_description: Mountain
description: Haramosh Peak, also known as Haramosh or Peak 58, is a Karakoram range mountain located in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. The 7,409-metre Haramosh Peak is situated roughly 65 kilometres (40 mi) to the east of Gilgit, within the south-central part of the Rakaposhi-Haramosh Mountains, which is a subrange of the Karakoram range. This mountain rises steeply above the north bank of the Indus River, just upstream from its confluence with the Gilgit River.

name: Makra Peak
name_ur: مکڑا چوٹی
short_description: Mountain
description: The Makra Peak is a mountain peak in the Himalayas Range, located on the border between the Kaghan Valley of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the Pakistani-administered Azad Kashmir. It is 3,885 metres (12,746 ft) high and almost 200 kilometres (120 mi) from Islamabad on the Naran Road. The trek to the peak starts from the Kaghan Valley, located in Hazara region of the northern Pakistan. From Kiwai, a single 7-kilometre-long road runs uphill to Shogran, a tourist resort with numerous hotels; the track continues to climb up to Siri Lake and ends at Payee. From here it is a trek of four hours to the top of the Makra.

name: Kallar kahar Museum
name_ur: کلر کہار میوزیم
short_description: Museum in Kallar Kahar
description: Museum in Kallar Kahar

name: Chauburji
name_ur: چو برجی
short_description: Mughal era monument in Lahore
description: Chauburji is a Mughal era monument in the city of Lahore, capital of the Pakistani province of Punjab. The monument was built in 1646 C.E. during the reign of the emperor Shah Jahan. It previously acted as a gateway to a large garden.

name: Valmiki Temple
name_ur: والمیکی مندر
short_description: Hindu temple in Punjab, Pakistan
description: Valmiki Temple, also called Nila Gumbad Valmiki temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Hindu sage Valmiki located in the Bhim Street in the Neela Gumbad area of Anarkali Bazar in Lahore, Pakistan. The temple is managed and maintained by the Pakistan Hindu Council and Evacuee Trust Property Board. In the contemporary era, the Krishna Temple and the Valmiki Temple are the only two functional Hindu temples in Lahore. The temple is located in New Anarkali.

name: Tombs of the Kalhora Rulers (Ghulam Shah Kalhoro)
name_ur: مقابر کلہوڑا حکمران (میاں غلام شاہ کلہوڑا) حیدرآباد
short_description: 1772 grand square mausoleum of Hyderabad's founder adorned with exquisite glazed kashi tiles and floral frescoes.
description: Constructed atop a fortified platform, this majestic tomb features vibrant azure kashi tiles, an arched domed arcade, and the carved marble cenotaph of Mian Ghulam Shah Kalhoro, the founder of modern Hyderabad.

name: Women Craft Cooperative
name_ur: ویمن کرافٹ کوآپریٹو گلمت
short_description: Museum in Gulmit
description: Museum in Gulmit

name: Tombs of the Talpur Mirs (Qubbas)
name_ur: مقابر تالپور میران (قبے) حیدرآباد
short_description: 19th-century royal necropolis of the Talpur rulers featuring carved marble cenotaphs and Persian blue domes.
description: Holding the remains of Mir Karam Ali Khan, Mir Murad Ali, and other rulers of Sindh, these mausoleums feature painted floral interiors, mirrored plasterwork, and carved wooden doors of rare craftsmanship.

name: Sindh Museum Qasimabad
name_ur: سندھ میوزیم قاسم آباد حیدرآباد
short_description: Provincial cultural museum in Qasimabad showcasing Indus Valley artifacts, folk musical instruments, and crafts.
description: Featuring life-sized dioramas of Thar desert nomads, Hala pottery workshops, Ajrak block carvers, and rare archaeological relics spanning 5,000 years of civilization along the Indus River basin.

name: Kamran's Baradari (Ravi River Island)
name_ur: کامران کی بارہ دری (دریائے راوی)
short_description: Oldest surviving Mughal structure in Lahore, a 1540 CE riverside pleasure pavilion on the Ravi.
description: Built in 1540 by Kamran Mirza, son of first Mughal Emperor Babur and brother of Humayun, this 12-door arched summer pavilion stands as an island retreat in the River Ravi.

name: Khanpur Cave
name_ur: خانپور غار
short_description: Notable nature site located in Khanpur.
description: Archaeological site in Pakistan

name: Rani Gat Buddhists Ruins
name_ur: رانی گٹ بودھوں کھنڈرات
short_description: Buddhist ruins
description: Ranigat is a 2500-year-old Buddhist archaeological site belonging to the Gandahara civilization located in the Buner District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Ranigat is a good example of the Buddhist past of the area. The site is located on top of a hill, accessible by climbing the stairs constructed by the Japanese. The main attractions include the Stupas, a big rock erected by the ancient people at some distance that they probably used to worship. The city or town was beautifully designed, and stones from the local mountains have been extensively used. Ranigat is easily accessible through the M1 and N35. It is about 20 km (12 mi) away from Swabi and 100 km (62 mi) from Peshawar and Islamabad.

name: Attock Fort
name_ur: قلعہ اٹک بنارس
short_description: Fort in Punjab, Pakistan
description: Attock Fort is a 16th-century fortress in Punjab, Pakistan. It was built at Attock Khurd during the reign of Akbar from 1581 to 1583 under the supervision of Khawaja Shamsuddin to protect the passage of the Indus River.

name: Rani Bagh Zoological & Botanical Gardens
name_ur: رانی باغ چڑیا گھر و نباتاتی باغ حیدرآباد
short_description: 1861 historic botanical park named after Queen Victoria spanning 53 shaded green acres with a lake and zoo.
description: Originally established as an agro-horticultural garden during British rule, Rani Bagh features historic mahogany and banyan trees, an open-air theater named after Abbas College, and family amusement lawns.

name: Resham Gali Historic Bridal Silk Bazaar
name_ur: ریشم گلی تاریخی برائیڈل بازار حیدرآباد
short_description: Legendary covered bazaar in Hyderabad famed for traditional glass bangles, pure silk embroidery, and wedding trousseaus.
description: A mesmerizing narrow pedestrian lane sparkling with thousands of multicolored glass bangles (choorian), gold gota work, Sindhi hand-stitched quilts (rilli), and bridal jewelry ateliers.

name: Shahi Bazaar Historic 2-km Covered Spine
name_ur: شاہی بازار تاریخی دو کلومیٹر لمبا بازار حیدرآباد
short_description: One of Asia's longest continuous historic bazaars stretching two kilometers from Pacca Qila to Market Tower.
description: Laid out by Ghulam Shah Kalhoro in the 18th century, this shaded labyrinth offers silverware, embroidered Sindhi topis, block-printed Ajraks, leather mojari shoes, and street food stalls.

name: Bombay Bakery (Cantonment Heritage)
name_ur: بمبئی بیکری تاریخی کینٹ حیدرآباد
short_description: Historic 1911 Parsi-Swiss confectionery in the Cantonment famed worldwide for its signature Coffee and Chocolate Cakes.
description: Operating from an atmospheric red-brick bungalow since 1911, this legendary bakery enforces strict batch limits for its rich coffee macaroons, chocolate fudge, and caramel cakes that sell out within minutes daily.

name: Malika Parbat
name_ur: ملکہ پربت
short_description: Mountain in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
description: Malika Parbat is the highest peak in the Kaghan Valley as well as the Hazara region of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, with an elevation of 5,290 metres (17,360 ft). It lies about 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) south of Lake Saiful Muluk, near Ansoo Lake.

name: Gurdwara Chowa Sahib
name_ur: گردوارہ چوآ صاحب
short_description: Gurdwara in Punjab, Pakistan
description: Gurdwara Chowa Sahib is a gurdwara located at the northern edge of the Rohtas Fort, near Jhelum, Punjab, Pakistan. Situated near the fort's Talaqi Gate, the gurdwara commemorates the site where Guru Nanak is popularly believed to have created a water-spring during one of his journeys known as udasi.

name: Kashmiri Gate
name_ur: کشمیری دروازہ
short_description: One of the historic gates of the Walled City of Lahore, Pakistan
description: Kashmiri Gate, Lahore is one of the thirteen gates of Walled City of Lahore in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan. The gate gets its name as it faces in the direction of Kashmir.

name: Krishna Temple
name_ur: کرشن مندر، لاہور
short_description: Notable religious site located in Walled City.
description: The Krishna Mandir is a Hindu temple (mandir) dedicated to the Hindu deity Krishna located in Ravi Road, opposite of Timber Market in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan. In 2006, the temple became a centre of controversy due to media reports on its demolition which later turned out incorrect. In the contemporary era, it is one of two functional Hindu temples in Lahore, the other being Valmiki Mandir.

name: Navalrai Clock Tower (Market Tower)
name_ur: نول رائے کلاک ٹاور (مارکیٹ ٹاور) حیدرآباد
short_description: 1914 historic Indo-Saracenic limestone clock tower and wholesale fish and fruit marketplace in central Hyderabad.
description: Designed in classical colonial stone architecture and named after civic benefactor Navalrai, this towering clock face has regulated Hyderabad's daily commercial rhythms for over a century.

name: Kotri Barrage Promenade & Palla Fish
name_ur: کوٹری بیراج پرومیناڈ و تازہ پلہ مچھلی
short_description: 1955 Indus River barrage on the National Highway famous for sunset river views and authentic river Palla fish.
description: Also known as Ghulam Muhammad Barrage, its 44 sluice gates irrigate 2.8 million acres of Sindh. The bridge promenade is lined with dhabas serving the prized migratory Hilsa (Palla) fish grilled with traditional red chilies.

name: Al-Manzar Indus River Viewpoint (Jamshoro)
name_ur: المنظر دریائے سندھ ویو پوائنٹ جامشورو
short_description: Scenic riverbank cliff viewpoint looking across the mighty Indus waters between Kotri and Jamshoro.
description: A beloved cultural gathering spot where poets, university students, and families relax on charpoys drinking hot doodh-patti chai while watching fishermen steer wooden boats across the wide river expanse.

name: Mukhi House Cultural Museum
name_ur: مکھی ہاؤس کلچرل میوزیم حیدرآباد
short_description: 1920 grand Italianate mansion of the wealthy Hindu Mukhi family restored as a Sindh cultural heritage museum.
description: Featuring carved teakwood staircases, imported Italian marble tiles, stained glass windows, and period furniture showcasing the aristocratic lifestyle of pre-partition Hyderabad's merchant elite.

short_description: Hindu temple in Peshawar, Pakistan
description: Goraknath Temple is a Hindu temple located in the Gorkhatri area of Peshawar in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The temple is dedicated to Gorakhnath. The temple was built in 1851. The temple has been declared as a heritage site.

name: Nammal Lake
name_ur: نمل جھیل
short_description: Lake in Punjab, Pakistan
description: Namal Lake is a man-made lake located near Rikhi, a village on one corner of the Namal valley in Mianwali District, Punjab, Pakistan. It was formed following the construction of Namal Dam in 1913. Namal Dam is situated some 32 km (20 mi) from Mianwali city.

name: Ranikot Fort (The Great Wall of Sindh)
name_ur: قلعہ رانی کوٹ (دی گریٹ وال آف سندھ) سان گیٹ
short_description: World's largest fort spanning 32 kilometers of fortified stone defense walls meandering across the Kirthar hills.
description: Often called the Great Wall of Sindh, Ranikot's monumental stone ramparts, crenellated parapets, and Sann Gate guard a rugged natural canyon containing inner fortified citadels of legendary antiquity.

name: Meeri Fort (Ranikot Inner Citadel)
name_ur: میری قلعہ (رانی کوٹ اندرونی قلعہ)
short_description: Fortified royal inner redoubt at the heart of Ranikot commanding panoramic views of the entire valley basin.
description: Serving as the royal residential palace and command post inside Ranikot, Meeri Fort features stone battlements, internal water reservoirs, and elevated sniper bastions designed for impregnable mountain defense.

name: Amri Prehistoric Indus Settlement Mounds
name_ur: آمری قبل از تاریخ آثار و قدیم ٹیلے جامشورو
short_description: Crucial 3600 BCE pre-Harappan archaeological site giving its name to the famous ancient Amri pottery culture.
description: Excavations by French archaeologist Jean-Marie Casal proved that advanced urban communities flourished here along the Indus River long before the rise of Mohenjo-daro, producing distinctive geometric painted ceramics.

name: Shrine of Hazrat Lal Shahbaz Qalandar (Sehwan)
name_ur: مزارِ اقدس حضرت لعل شہباز قلندر سیہون شریف
short_description: 13th-century golden-domed spiritual shrine of the patron Sufi saint of Sindh, revered by millions across South Asia.
description: Syed Usman Marwandi, known as Lal Shahbaz Qalandar, preached unconditional divine love and human equality. His magnificent shrine features a massive gilded dome, mirror-work halls, and centuries-old golden doors.

description: The Princess of Hope is a natural rock formation in the Hingol National Park of Lasbela in Balochistan, Pakistan. It is of the type known as a hoodoo or "fairy chimney" and which could fancifully be construed as resembling a crowned and skirted female figure looking toward the horizon. It is situated approximately 190 km (120 mi) from Pakistan's financial hub, Karachi, and approximately 717 km (446 mi) from the provincial capital, Quetta.

description: Moti Masjid, one of the "Pearl Mosques", is a 17th-century religious building located inside the Lahore Fort, Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan. It is a small, white marble structure built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan and modified by the architects of Shah Jahan, and is among his prominent extensions to the Lahore Fort Complex. The mosque is located on the western side of Lahore Fort, closer to Alamgiri Gate, the main entrance.

description: Tarbela lake is a reservoir formed by the Tarbela Dam, located 3 km south of Haripur, in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province in Pakistan. It is one of the biggest lakes of Pakistan.

short_description: Gurdwara in Sialkot, Punjab, Pakistan
description: Gurdawara Bair Sahib, also called Baba Beri or Baba Bair, or Gurdwara Babe Di Ber, is situated in Sialkot, Pakistan.

name: Oonchi Mosque
name_ur: اونچی مسجد
short_description: Mosque in Lahore, Pakistan
description: The Oonchi Mosque, or Uchi Mosque is a Mughal-era mosque located along the Hakiman Bazaar, near the Bhati Gate which leads into the Walled City of Lahore, in Pakistan. The mosque may date from the reign of the Mughal Emperor Akbar.

name: Shrine of Bodlo Bahar (Sehwan)
name_ur: درگاہ بودلہ بہار سیہون شریف
short_description: Historic shrine of Qalandar's devoted disciple Sikandar Bodlo Bahar, surrounded by red flags and natural spring channels.
description: Associated with deep mystic legends of selfless devotion, this shrine is visited by pilgrims who march with red banners and play earthen drums before paying homage at the main Qalandar sanctum.

name: Manchhar Lake Boathouse Fishing Community
name_ur: منچھر جھیل کشتیوں کے گھر و روایتی ماہی گیر جامشورو
short_description: South Asia's largest shallow freshwater lake home to the indigenous Mirbahar boat-dwelling water tribe.
description: Covering over 260 square kilometers against the Kirthar foothills, Manchhar features wooden houseboats (boathouses) where fisherfolk cook, sleep, and live on the water, harvesting lotus roots and waterfowl.

name: Batura Glacier
name_ur: بتورا گلیشیر
short_description: Notable nature site located in Hunza District.
description: Batura Glacier, 57 km (35 mi) long, is one of the largest and longest glaciers outside of the polar regions. It lies in the upper Hunza (Gojal) region of Hunza District, in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. It is just north of the massifs of Batura, at 7,795 metres (25,574 ft), and Passu, at 7,500 metres (24,600 ft). The glacier flows west to east. The lower portions can be described as a grey sea of rocks and gravelly moraine, bordered by a few summer villages and pastures with herds of sheep, goats, cows and yaks and where roses and juniper trees are common.

name: Mahundand Lake

short_description: Lake in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
description: The Swat River is a perennial river in the northern region of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan. The source of river is in the high glacial valleys of the Hindu Kush mountains, from where it then flows into the Kalam Valley before forming the spine of the wider Swat Valley.

name: Lake Manchar
name_ur: منچھر جھیل
short_description: Lake in Sindh, Pakistan
description: Lake Manchar, also spelled Manchhar, is the largest natural freshwater lake in Pakistan, and one of the largest in South Asia. It is located west of the Indus River, in Jamshoro and Dadu districts of Sindh, 18 kilometres (11 mi) away from Sehwan. Lake Manchar collects water from numerous small streams in the Kirthar Mountains, and then empties into the Indus River. The lake's surface area fluctuates with the seasons, from as little as 36 km2, to as much as 500 km2 during monsoon rains.

name: Manchhar Lake Lotus & Pelican Sanctuary
name_ur: منچھر جھیل کنول باغات و پیلیکن پرندے
short_description: Extensive wild aquatic lotus flower fields providing breeding habitat for Siberian pelicans and herons.
description: During winter mornings, the calm waters of Manchhar are covered in blooming pink lotus flowers and thousands of migratory flamingos and pelicans diving for lake fish, creating a dreamlike natural spectacle.
