description: Chogo Lungma Glacier is a glacier in the Karakorum mountain ranges in Shigar District of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. It was the first of all the big Karakorum glaciers to be discovered, in 1835.

name: Kirthar National Park
name_ur: کیرتھر قومی پارک
short_description: National park in Sindh, Pakistan
description: Kirthar National Park is a national park located in the Kirthar Mountains range in Dadu and Jamshoro districts of Sindh, Pakistan. Lying north to Karachi, the park was established in 1974 and encompasses over 3,087 km2 (1,192 sq mi), making it the third largest national park in Pakistan. Wildlife in the park comprises leopard, striped hyena, Indian wolf, honey badger, urial, chinkara gazelle and rare Sindh ibex. Blackbuck are kept in enclosures for a reintroduction project.

name: Keenjhar Lake
name_ur: کینجھر جھیل
short_description: Lake in Sindh, Pakistan
description: Keenjhar Lake, commonly called Karli Lake, is located in Thatta District of the Sindh province in Pakistan. It is situated about 36 kilometres (22 mi) from the city of Thatta. It is an important source of drinking water for Thatta District and Karachi city. Through the construction of a bund on the eastern side, it is said that the lake was formed by the union of two lakes: Sonehri and Keenjhar.

name: Gorakh Hill Midnight Ridge Camping Site
name_ur: گورکھ ہل مڈنائٹ رج کیمپنگ گراؤنڈ دادو
short_description: Popular high-altitude tent camping ground along the rugged limestone ridges of Gorakh.
description: Equipped for adventure seekers, visitors pitch tents under freezing night winds, enjoy live charcoal barbecue around campfires, and wake up to dramatic sunrises rising over the Kirthar mountain range.

name: Nai Gaj Valley & Fresh River Gorge
name_ur: نئی گاج وادی و قدرتی پہاڑی گھاٹی دادو
short_description: A torrential mountain stream from Balochistan cutting through towering Kirthar limestone gorges into Dadu.
description: Renowned for its crystal-clear natural pools, ancient petroglyph rock carvings, and lush date palms clinging to vertical cliff walls, serving as the site of the strategic Nai Gaj Dam water reservoir.

name: Dadu Historic Shahi Bazaar & Grain Hub
name_ur: دادو تاریخی شاہی بازار و غلہ منڈی
short_description: Central agricultural trading market and traditional Sindhi handicraft center of northern Dadu district.
description: Known for its bustling trade in cotton, wheat, and handcrafted camel-leather footwear, the bazaar provides the commercial lifeblood for farming communities between Sehwan and Larkana.

name: Hala Glazed Kashi Tile Craft Workshops
name_ur: ہالہ کاشی ٹائلز دستکاری کارخانے مٹیاری
short_description: World-famous artisanal studios where master craftsmen create blue-and-white hand-painted glazed tiles for Sufi shrines.
description: Carrying forward a 500-year-old terracotta and ceramic tradition, Hala's Kashigars paint cobalt and turquoise floral motifs onto kiln-fired clay plaques that grace the domes and facades of South Asia's holiest monuments.

name: Hispar Glacier
name_ur: ہسپر گلیشر
short_description: Notable nature site located in Nagar District.
description: Hispar Glacier is a 49-km (30-mile) long glacier situated in the Karakoram Mountains of Gilgit–Baltistan, Pakistan. It converges with the Biafo Glacier, which extends for 67 kilometers, at the Hispar La (Pass), reaching an altitude of 5,128 meters. This confluence creates the world's longest glacial system outside of the polar regions.

name: Rann of Kutch Wildlife Sanctuary
name_ur: رن کچھ جنگلی حیات پناہ گاہ
short_description: Ramsar site in Sindh, Pakistan
description: The Rann of Kutch Wildlife Sanctuary is the largest Ramsar site in Sindh, covering 566,375 ha, and is located in the Rann of Kutch in Badin District, Sindh, Pakistan. In 1980, declared as a wildlife sanctuary by the Government of Sindh, the Rann of Kutch covers the most Ramsar site area as compared to that of any other of the ten Ramsar sites in Sindh province of Pakistan.

name: Saiful Maluk National Park
name_ur: سیف الملوک نیشنل پارک
short_description: National park of Pakistan
description: Saiful Muluk National Park is situated in the Kaghan Valley within the Mansehra District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The park was officially declared in 2003, and is centred upon the alpine Saiful Muluk Lake.

name: Jaulian
name_ur: جولین
short_description: Notable historical site located in Khanpur.
description: Jaulian is a ruined Buddhist monastery dating from the 2nd century CE, located in Taxila, in Pakistan.

name: Hala Jandi Lacquered Wood Furniture Bazaar
name_ur: ہالہ جندی لکڑی کا روایتی فرنیچر بازار مٹیاری
short_description: Centuries-old bazaar of hand-lathed woodcraft known as Jandi, creating vibrant yellow and red lacquer work.
description: Crafted from local babool and shisham timber, master woodturners apply layers of natural colored lacquer, engraving delicate geometric motifs into traditional baby cots (peengho), footstools, and decorative spoons.

name: Tambura Sufi Music Courtyard (Bhit Shah)
name_ur: تنبورہ صوفیانہ راگ کورٹ یارڈ بھٹ شاہ
short_description: The sacred veranda where Faqirs have continuously sung Shah Jo Risalo on the stringed Tambura for over 250 years.
description: Initiated by Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai himself with his invented string instrument the Danburo, hereditary faqir troupes sing the 30 musical Sur (modes) in continuous unbroken relays day and night.

name: Shrine of Makhdoom Nooh (Old Hala)
name_ur: درگاہ مخدوم نوح رح پرانا ہالہ مٹیاری
short_description: 16th-century spiritual sanctuary of the Sarwari Suhrawardi Sufi master, featuring towering minarets and kashi facades.
description: Makhdoom Nooh translated the Holy Quran into Persian in the 16th century. His grand mausoleum in Old Hala is a major pilgrimage center renowned for its spiritual serenity and historic blue tile architecture.

name: Cholistan Wildlife Sanctuary
name_ur: صحرائے چولستان جنگلی حیات کی پناہ گاہ
short_description: Desert in Punjab, Pakistan
description: The Cholistan Desert, also known locally by its Punjabi name Rohi, is a desert in the Bahawalpur Division of Punjab, Pakistan. It forms part of the greater Thar Desert, which also extends into Sindh and Rajasthan. It is one of two large deserts in Punjab, the other being the Thal Desert. The name is derived from the Turkic word chol, meaning "sands," and istan, a Persian suffix meaning "land of."

short_description: One of South Asia's largest pilgrimage temples dedicated to Baba Ramdev Pir, drawing a million devotees annually.
description: Built in the early 19th century around a sacred footprint stone, this expansive temple complex hosts one of the largest Hindu gatherings in Pakistan, where pilgrims carry vibrant flags on foot across Sindh.

name: Mirwah World-Famous Mango Orchards
name_ur: میرواہ عالمی شہرت یافتہ آم کے باغات ٹنڈو الہ یار
short_description: Pakistan's premier Sindhrri mango capital holding sprawling sweet fruit estates along the Mirwah Canal.
description: Renowned internationally for producing the gold-standard 'Sindhri', 'Chunsa', and 'Anwar Ratol' mangoes, Tando Allahyar's climate yields sweet, aromatic fruit exported to gourmet markets worldwide.

name: Baradari of Kamran Mirza
name_ur: کامران کی بارہ دری
short_description: Baradari of Kamran Mirza is a summer pavilion (baradari) in Lahore, Pakistan.
description: Baradari of Kamran Mirza is a summer pavilion (baradari) in Lahore, Pakistan. It was built in 1540 by Kamran Mirza, a son of first Mughal emperor Babur, and a brother of the second Mughal emperor Humayun. The building is believed to be the oldest existing Mughal structure in Lahore, and is the only garden in Lahore's Shahdara Bagh area that was not converted into a funerary monument.

description: Bijnot Fort is a ruined fortress located in Bahawalpur District of Punjab, Pakistan, 23 kilometres west of the Pakistan-India border in Cholistan Desert.

name: Fort Derawar
name_ur: حصن ديراور
short_description: Large square fortress in Punjab, Pakistan
description: Derawar Fort is a fortress located in the Cholistan Desert of Punjab, Pakistan, specifically within the Yazman Tehsil of the Bahawalpur District. Approximately 20 km south of the city of Ahmedpur East, the forty bastions of Derawar are visible from many miles in the Cholistan. The walls have a perimeter of 1500 metres and stand up to thirty metres high.

name: Mosque of Mariyam Zamani Begum
name_ur: مریم الزمانی بیگم شاہی مسجد
short_description: Random Mosque in the Mughal Empire
description: Begum Shahi Mosque, officially the Mosque of Mariyam Zamani Begum, is a 17th-century mosque situated in the interior walled city of Lahore in Punjab, Pakistan. It was commissioned by Mughal empress Mariam-uz-Zamani, the chief consort of Akbar. The mosque was built between 1611 and 1614 during the reign of Jahangir.

name: Nasarpur Historic Glazed Pottery Kilns
name_ur: نصر پور تاریخی مٹی کے برتن و کاشی کے بھٹے
short_description: Ancient 10th-century pottery center celebrated for hand-molded clay urns, water pitchers, and blue tiles.
description: A sister city to Hala in ceramic excellence, Nasarpur's master potters use alluvial Indus mud to mold ultra-thin water pitchers (matkas), decorative vases, and enameled plates in wood-fired kilns.

name: Shrine & Temple of Odero Lal (Jhulelal)
name_ur: درگاہ و مندر اوڈیرو لال (جھولے لال) مٹیاری
short_description: Sacred shared syncretic sanctuary where Hindus worship Jhulelal (deity of the Indus) and Muslims venerate Sheikh Tahir.
description: A shining beacon of Sindh's syncretic interfaith heritage, this grand domed complex holds both an eternal flame (jyoti) and a Muslim prayer hall, celebrating the divine water saint who protected the people of Sindh.

name: Kot Diji Pre-Harappan Archaeological Excavations
name_ur: کوٹ ڈیجی قبل از ہڑپہ آثارِ قدیمہ خیرپور
short_description: 3300 BCE archaeological citadel proving the pre-Harappan urban roots of the Indus Valley Civilization.
description: Excavated by Dr. F.A. Khan, this site revealed a fortified citadel, defensive stone rubble walls, and the famous 'Kot Diji style' painted pottery featuring horned deities that preceded Mohenjo-daro.

name: General Post Office (GPO Mall Road)
name_ur: جنرل پوسٹ آفس (جی پی او) مال روڈ لاہور
short_description: 1887 Victorian Gothic red-brick postal palace with twin domed towers anchoring central Mall Road.
description: Designed by Sir Ganga Ram and opened for Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee, the GPO remains Pakistan's largest operational mail hub, renowned for its clocks, pointed arches, and polished brass counters.

name: Supreme Court of Pakistan (Lahore Branch)
name_ur: سپریم کورٹ آف پاکستان لاہور رجسٹری

description: Surrounded by manicured green lawns, this historic courthouse has witnessed monumental legal trials that shaped Pakistan's judicial and constitutional history.

name: Lahore Zoo & 150-Year-Old Botanical Gardens
name_ur: لاہور چڑیا گھر و ڈیڑھ سو سال پرانا نباتاتی باغ
short_description: 1872 historic zoological park on Mall Road spanning 25 acres, one of the oldest operational zoos in the world.
description: Established in 1872, it houses over a thousand animals beneath ancient banyan and mahogany canopies, featuring lion houses, elephant pavilions, and children's avian aviaries.

name: Lahore Canal Road Linear Green Promenade
name_ur: لاہور کینال روڈ سرسبز لکیری پرومیناڈ
short_description: Scenic 82-kilometer tree-lined waterway cutting through the heart of Lahore with seasonal floating floral floats.
description: Originally constructed during the Mughal era and expanded under British irrigation works, the shaded canal is the lifeblood of Lahore's springtime Jashn-e-Baharan flower carnivals.

name: Diwan-e-Aam (Hall of Public Audience Lahore Fort)
name_ur: دیوانِ عام شاہی قلعہ لاہور
short_description: 1628 monumental 40-pillar red sandstone imperial court hall built by Emperor Shah Jahan.
description: Featuring deep vaulted red sandstone arcades and an elevated marble Jharoka throne, this historic durbar hall was where Mughal Emperors presided over daily state petitions and royal proclamations.

short_description: Archaeological site of an ancient Buddhist monastery in Pakistan
description: Takht-i-Bahi, is an Indo-Parthian archaeological site of an ancient Buddhist monastery in Mardan, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The site is considered among the most important relics of Buddhism in all of what was once Gandhara.

name: Mohra Morado
name_ur: موہرا مرادو
short_description: Notable historical site located in Taxila.
description: Mohra Muradu is the place of an ancient Buddhist stupa and monastery near the ruins of Taxila, in the Punjab province of Pakistan. The ancient monastery is located in a valley and has views of the surrounding mountains. The monks could meditate in all stillness at this place but were near enough to the city of Sirsukh to go for begging as it is only around 1.5 km away. The city is said to have been built the 2nd century CE and renovated in the 5th century.

name: Canhun Jo Daro ((Sheffield of India)
name_ur: چنھودڑو
short_description: Notable historical site located in Sakrand.
description: Chanhu-daro, a shorter form of Chanhun-jo-daro which in Sindhi means "the mound of Chanhun", is an archaeological site belonging to the Indus Valley civilization. The site is located 130 kilometers (81 mi) south of Mohenjo-daro, now in Sindh, Pakistan. The settlement was inhabited between 4000 and 1700 BCE, and is considered to have been a centre for manufacturing carnelian beads. This site is a group of three low mounds that excavations has shown were parts of a single settlement, approximately 7 hectares in size.

name: Faiz Mahal (The Royal Talpur Palace)
name_ur: فیض محل شاہی تالپور محل خیرپور میرس
short_description: 1798 majestic classical pink-and-white palace of the Talpur Mirs set within manicured royal formal gardens.
description: Serving as the sovereign sovereign seat of the princely State of Khairpur, Faiz Mahal features magnificent carved plaster arcades, stained-glass reception halls, and original royal durbar thrones.

name: Therhi Historic Wholesale Date Market
name_ur: ٹھیڑی تاریخی کھجور ہول سیل منڈی خیرپور
short_description: South Asia's busiest wholesale trading hub for sun-dried dried dates (chhohara) and Aseel dates.
description: Every summer, thousands of truckloads of golden processed dates from across Sindh and Balochistan converge on Therhi to be packed, graded, and exported to international markets worldwide.

name: Raja Bazaar Historic Labyrinth (Rawalpindi)
name_ur: راجہ بازار تاریخی پرپیچ بازار راولپنڈی
short_description: Centuries-old historic trade labyrinth packed with brass markets, spice merchants, and unstitched fabrics.
description: The commercial nerve center of Potohar, Raja Bazaar spans historic pre-partition brick buildings, narrow winding lanes, and specialized sectors like Sarafa, Namak Mandi, and Sabzi Mandi.

short_description: Massive 2,300-acre public recreation park in Rawalpindi featuring serene lakes, golf courses, and an open-air theater.
description: Established in the 1960s, Ayub Park offers paddle boating, Japanese zen gardens, military hardware museums, and shaded picnic woods for families across the twin cities.

name: Flashman's Heritage Hotel (The Mall Rawalpindi)
name_ur: فلیش مینز تاریخی ہوٹل مال روڈ راولپنڈی
short_description: 1888 colonial bungalow resort on The Mall that accommodated British viceroys and commanders.
description: Spread across expansive shaded courtyards, Flashman's preserves 19th-century teak fireplaces, high-ceilinged verandahs, and heritage suites that witnessed the birth of the Pakistan Army GHQ.

name: Multan Arts Council & Cultural Auditorium
name_ur: ملتان آرٹس کونسل و آڈیٹوریم
short_description: Premier cultural and performing arts theater complex of South Punjab near the Multan Cantonment.
description: Featuring acoustic theater auditoriums, open-air amphitheatres, and contemporary art galleries, the council hosts the annual National Sufi Festival, Saraiki literature conferences, and artisan exhibitions.

short_description: Pakistani writer (1873–1956)
description: Zafar Ali Khan was a Pakistani writer, poet, translator and a journalist who used his work against the British rule. He was also one of the Majlis-e-Ahrar-e-Islam's founding members.

name: Laar Museum & Molvi Haji Ahmed Mallah Library Badin
name_ur: لار میوزیم و لائبریری بدین
short_description: History museum in Sindh, Pakistan
description: The Laar Museum and Molvi Haji Ahmed Mallah Library is a historic building located on the main Karachi road opposite the deputy commissioner's office in Badin, Sindh, Pakistan.

name_ur: مسکین جہان خان کھوسو میوزیم نگرپارکر
short_description: Museum in Nagarparkar
description: Museum in Nagarparkar, Tharparkar District, Sindh.

name: Liaquat Bagh
name_ur: لیاقت قومی باغ
short_description: At Jamshoro, Sindh, Pakistan
description: Liaqat National Bagh, formerly known as Company Bagh, usually just referred to as Liaqat Bagh, is a park on Murree Road in the city of Rawalpindi, Punjab, Pakistan. It is close to 'Arya Mohalla' and Government Gordon College, which are two well-known residential and commercial areas of Rawalpindi.

name: Aqsa Mosque
name_ur: مسجد اقصی
short_description: Mosque in Rabwah, Pakistan
description: The Aqsa Mosque in Rabwah is the main and largest mosque of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community in Pakistan. Its foundation stone was laid down in 1966. The mosque was inaugurated on 31 March 1972 by the head of the worldwide community, Mirza Nasir Ahmad. The building can accommodate up to 20,000 worshippers.

name: Iqbal Park
name_ur: اقبال پارک
short_description: Urban park in Lahore, Pakistan
description: Greater Iqbal Park, formerly Iqbal Park and Minto Park, is an urban park, spread over an area of 329 acres, located on the outskirts of the Walled City in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan.

name: Makli Hill Necropolis
name_ur: شہرِ خموشاں مکلی
short_description: Necropolis in Sindh, Pakistan
description: Makli Necropolis is one of the largest funerary sites in the world, spread over an area of 10 kilometres near the city of Thatta, in the Pakistani province of Sindh. The site houses approximately 500,000 to 1 million tombs built over the course of a 400-year period. Makli Necropolis features several large funerary monuments belonging to royalty, various Sufi saints, and esteemed scholars. The site was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1981 as an "outstanding testament" to Sindhi civilization between the 14th and 18th centuries.

name: Gambat Historic Sufi Shrines & Medical Center
name_ur: گمبٹ تاریخی صوفی درگاہیں و میڈیکل سینٹر خیرپور
short_description: Renowned medical care citadel and historic Sufi crossroads near the Rohri Canal in Khairpur.
description: Home to the world-renowned Gambat Institute of Medical Sciences (GIMS) providing free organ transplants, surrounded by ancient date groves and peaceful Sufi shrines.

name: Ranipur Historic Shrines & Seminaries
name_ur: رانی پور تاریخی درگاہیں و دینی مدارس خیرپور
short_description: Renowned spiritual sanctuary on the National Highway holding centuries-old Dargahs and Islamic schools.
description: Famous for Dargah Bodlo Bahar and revered Chishti and Qadiri saints, Ranipur is a regular pilgrimage stop for spiritual travelers heading toward the shrine of Sachal Sarmast.

name: Hingorja Historical Merchant Havelis
name_ur: ہنگورجہ تاریخی تاجر حویلیاں خیرپور
short_description: Centuries-old aristocratic town holding 19th-century carved brick havelis and traditional schools.
description: Historically home to wealthy bureaucrats and scholars of the Talpur court, Hingorja features multi-storey brick residences with carved wooden doors and peaceful shaded alleys.

name: Sobhodero Historic Talpur Brick Fort
name_ur: سوبھو دیرو تاریخی تالپور اینٹوں کا قلعہ خیرپور
short_description: 18th-century defensive military fort built by Talpur Mirs to protect western canal territories.
description: Featuring thick burnt-brick ramparts, circular bastions, and high arched gates, Sobhodero stands as an imposing reminder of the princely State of Khairpur's military architecture.

name: Setharja Historic Railway Town & Bazaar
name_ur: سیٹھارجہ تاریخی ریلوے اسٹیشن و بازار خیرپور
short_description: Vibrant market town on the main railway line trading dates, wheat, and handcrafted pottery.
description: A bustling local transit stop connecting surrounding agricultural villages, Setharja is known for traditional sweet shops, tea hotels, and historic colonial station platforms.

name: Godwin Austen Glacier
name_ur: گاڈون آسٹن گلیشیر
short_description: Notable nature site located in Shigar District.
description: The Godwin-Austen Glacier is a glacier in the Karakoram range and is close to K2, the second highest mountain peak in the world, situated in Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan. Its confluence with the Baltoro Glacier is called Concordia and is a popular trekking destination as it provides views of four of the five eight-thousanders in the region.

name: Race Course Park
name_ur: جیلانی پارک
short_description: Park in Lahore, Pakistan
description: Jilani Park is located in the city of Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan. It is situated on the Jail Road in front of the Services Hospital. It is known for its floral exhibitions and artificial waterfall and also for holding various annual festivals. Annual horse racing competitions are held in this park. There is also a famous restaurant inside the park called 'Polo Lounge'. It is named after Ghulam Jilani Khan.

name: Panja Sahib
name_ur: گردوارہ پنجہ صاحب
short_description: Notable religious site located in ‎Hasan Abdal.
description: Gurdwara Panja Sahib is a gurdwara located in Hasan Abdal, Punjab, Pakistan. It is one of the most important sites for the Sikhs, as the handprint of Guru Nanak—the founder of Sikhism—is believed to be imprinted on a boulder at the gurdwara. It is managed by the Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee under the federal government of Pakistan.

name: Khairpur Date Palm Oases & Processing Orchards
name_ur: خیرپور کھجور کے وسیع نخلستان و باغات
short_description: Pakistan's premier date farming heartland holding millions of lush date palms producing Aseel dates.
description: Spread across thousands of irrigated acres, Khairpur transforms into a golden spectacle during summer harvest, when millions of dates are sun-dried on vast mats to create sweet 'Chhohara' and premium fresh fruit.

name: Askari Park
name_ur: عسكری پارک
short_description: Amusement park in Karachi, Pakistan
description: Kashmir Park (formerly KMC Park / Askari Amusement Park) is an amusement park located in Karachi, Pakistan.

name: Shrine of Hazrat Sachal Sarmast (Daraza Sharif)
name_ur: درگاہ حضرت سچل سرمست رح درازا شریف خیرپور
short_description: 18th-century shrine of the ecstatic Sufi poet known as the 'Attar of Sindh', celebrated for universal humanism.
description: Abdul Wahab Farooqi, known as Sachal Sarmast ('Truthful Intoxicated One'), composed ecstatic mystic poetry in seven languages. His vibrant blue-and-turquoise tiled mausoleum draws lovers of truth from across the globe.

name: Lansdowne Bridge Historic Steel Railway Span
name_ur: لینس ڈاؤن برج تاریخی فولادی ریلوے پل سکھر
short_description: 1889 marvel of Victorian cantilever engineering spanning the Indus River between Sukkur and Rohri.
description: When completed in 1889, it was the longest cantilever railway span in the world. Built without central river piers, its dramatic steel arched trusses remain a triumphant landmark of civil engineering.

name: Ayub Arch Bridge (Indus Rail Bridge)
name_ur: ایوب آرچ برج (ریلوے پل) سکھر
short_description: 1962 monumental steel railway arch bridge rising 207 feet above the Indus River beside Lansdowne Bridge.
description: Designed by world-renowned bridge engineer David B. Steinman, this graceful steel railway arch took over heavy train traffic from the aging Lansdowne Bridge, framing scenic river panoramas.

name: Bagh e Karachi
name_ur: باغ کراچی
short_description: Public Park in Karachi, Pakistan
description: Bagh-e-Karachi is a public park in Gulshan-e-Iqbal, Karachi.

name: Shandur Lake
name_ur: شندور جھیل
short_description: Lake in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan
description: Shandur Lake, also known as Hundrup Lake, is a high-altitude lake located in Shandur-Hundrup National Park, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. It is located in between the Shandur Pass and Shandur Polo Ground, and is a primary source of origin for Gilgit River. It is the 5th largest lake in northern Pakistan by surface area.

name: Lake View Park
name_ur: لیک ویو پارک، اسلام آباد
short_description: Park in Islamabad, Pakistan
description: Lake View Park is a wildlife park, amusement park and adventure park located near Malpur village at the edge of Rawal lake in Islamabad, Pakistan. It runs under the administration of Capital Development Authority. It is considered as a major hub for festivals and events, particularly during spring and winter. Flower exhibitions, bird shows, and national holiday celebrations have drawn tourists to the facility.

name: Safari Park
name_ur: سفاری باغ
short_description: Notable park site located in Gulshan e Iqbal Block 10.
description: Karachi Safari Park, opened in 1970, is a public-funded, 'family-only' safari park covering an area of 0.60 square kilometres, located in Gulshan-e-Iqbal, Karachi, Sindh, Pakistan. It has a zoo, with viewing facilities like a chairlift and safari tracks, as well as two natural lakes.

name: PIA Planetarium
name_ur: پی آئی اے پلینٹیریم کراچی
short_description: Museum in Gulshan-e-Iqbal
description: Museum in Gulshan-e-Iqbal

name: Sadhu Bela Island Hindu Temple (Menghraj Mandir)
name_ur: سادھو بیلا جزیرہ ہندو مندر سکھر
short_description: 1823 sacred island temple on the Indus River featuring white marble carvings, courtyards, and riverside ghats.
description: Founded by Baba Bankhandi Maharaj on an island in the Indus River, Sadhu Bela is one of the most revered Hindu pilgrimage sanctuaries in Pakistan, adorned with marble reliefs depicting mythological epics.

name: Lab-e-Mehran Indus Riverside Promenade
name_ur: لبِ مہران دریائے سندھ واک وے و پارک سکھر
short_description: Scenic landscaped municipal park on the banks of the Indus River offering shaded boat rides and family tea lawns.
description: A cherished leisure promenade for Sukkur families, Lab-e-Mehran features riverside stone walks, boat docks for trips around Sadhu Bela island, and evening tea stalls watching illuminated bridges.

name: Satyan-jo-Asthan (Tomb of the Seven Sisters)
name_ur: ستین جو آستان (سات سہیلیوں کا آستانہ) روہڑی
short_description: Historic 17th-century clifftop shrine on the Indus River shrouded in legends of seven pious maidens.
description: Perched on a yellow limestone cliff overlooking the river, this necropolis features richly decorated tile cenotaphs, shady carved stone pavilions, and scenic vistas of Lansdowne Bridge spanning the gorge.

name: Rohri Historic Carved Wooden Balcony Havelis
name_ur: روہڑی تاریخی حویلیاں و لکڑی کے جھروکے
short_description: Labyrinthine medieval streets of Rohri holding 18th-century multi-storey brick havelis with teakwood jharokas.
description: Rising steeply on limestone hills, Rohri's old quarters preserve magnificent multi-storey merchant homes featuring intricately hand-carved Burmese teak windows, overhanging balconies, and winding cobbled alleys.

name: Liligo Glacier
name_ur: لِیلِیگو گلیشیر
short_description: Glacier in Pakistan
description: Glacier in Pakistan

name: Sheosar Lake
name_ur: شیوسر جھیل
short_description: Lake in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan
description: Sheosar Lake is an alpine lake situated at the western end of Deosai National Park, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. Located at an elevation of 4,250 metres (13,940 ft), the lake is regarded as one of the highest altitude lakes in the world.

name: Hazuri Bagh
name_ur: حضوری باغ
short_description: Garden in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan
description: Hazuri Bagh is a garden in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan, bounded by the Lahore Fort to the east, Badshahi Mosque to the west, the Samadhi of Ranjit Singh to the north, and the Roshnai Gate to the south. The garden was built during the reign of Ranjit Singh, in the style of Mughal gardens. In the centre of the garden stands the Hazuri Bagh Baradari, built by Ranjit Singh in 1818 to celebrate his capture of the Koh-i-Noor diamond from Shuja Shah Durrani in 1813. The Serai Alamgiri caravanserai formerly stood where Hazuri Bagh is now located.

name: Jinnah Gardens
name_ur: باغ جناح
short_description: Historical park in the city of Lahore, Pakistan
description: Bagh-e-Jinnah, formerly known as Lawrence Gardens, is a historical park in the city of Lahore, Pakistan. The large green space contains a botanical garden, Masjid Dar-ul-Islam, and Quaid-e-Azam Library.

name: Aror (Alor) Rock Formations & Historic Ruins
name_ur: اروڑی کی چٹانیں و محمد بن قاسم مسجد کے کھنڈرات سکھر
short_description: Ancient Hindu capital of Sindh captured by Muhammad bin Qasim in 711 CE, set amid dramatic limestone cliffs.
description: Featuring towering natural limestone pillars, pre-historic chert quarries, and the stone foundations of Sindh's earliest congregational mosques overlooking the ancient abandoned dry riverbed of the Indus.

name: Garhi Khuda Bakhsh Bhutto Family Mausoleum
name_ur: گڑھی خدا بخش بھٹو خاندان کا تاریخی مزار لاڑکانہ
short_description: Monumental white marble domed mausoleum holding the tombs of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Benazir Bhutto.
description: Inspired by Mughal and Islamic architecture, this imposing white edifice features soaring arches, carved calligraphic facades, and vast prayer plazas drawing millions of political pilgrims annually.

name: Shikarpur Covered Bazaar (Dhak Bazaar)
name_ur: شکارپور ڈھک بازار (چھت والا تاریخی بازار)
short_description: Legendary historic timber-roofed covered bazaar established in the 17th century as a trans-Eurasian trade hub.
description: Constructed with a continuous wooden ceiling to block out the fierce summer sun, this narrow bazaar once financed caravan trade to Bukhara, Samarkand, and Kandahar through Shikarpur's legendary Hundi banking system.

name: Shikarpur World-Famous Achar & Pickle Bazaar
name_ur: شکارپور عالمی شہرت یافتہ اچار مارکیٹ
short_description: Pakistan's pickle capital celebrated for mustard oil pickles of mango, garlic, mixed vegetable, and stuffed chilies.
description: Famous across South Asia for over a century, Shikarpuri achar combines raw green mangoes, whole garlic cloves, carrots, and secret spiced blends aged in clay jars to create the subcontinent's most piquant condiment.

name: Gawalmandi Food Street (Historic)
name_ur: گوالمنڈی فوڈ اسٹریٹ تاریخی لاہور
short_description: Pakistan's original street food hub famous for spiced fried fish, hareesa, and lassi.
description: Established by families who migrated from Amritsar in 1947, Gawalmandi pioneered Pakistan's nighttime food culture with its century-old wooden balconies and sizzling karahis.

name: Bab-e-Khyber (Gateway to Khyber)
name_ur: بابِ خیبر جمرود
short_description: Monumental stone gateway marking the historic entrance to the Khyber Pass on Grand Trunk Road.
description: Constructed in 1964 adjacent to the 1836 Sikh fort of Jamrud, Bab-e-Khyber is a national symbol commemorating the Silk Road gateway between South and Central Asia.

name: Noor Mahal
name_ur: نور محل
short_description: Palace in Bahawalpur, Punjab, Pakistan
description: The Noor Mahal is a historic royal palace located in Bahawalpur, Punjab, Pakistan. It was constructed in the 1870s by the princely state of Bahawalpur, and served as the residence and workplace of the Nawab. It is currently owned by the Ministry of Defense (MoD) under the management of the Army Secretariat.

name: Abbasi Mosque
name_ur: عباسی مسجد، بہاولپور
short_description: Mosque in Punjab, Pakistan
description: The Abbasi Mosque, or Derawar Mosque, and locally known as Jamia Masjid‑e‑Abbasi, is a mosque located close to Derawar Fort in Yazman Tehsil, in the Cholistan Desert in Bahawalpur District, in the Punjab province of Pakistan. The mosque can accommodate 10,000 worshippers.

name: Tomb of Allama Iqbal
name_ur: مقبرہ علامہ اقبال
short_description: Mausoleum in Lahore, Pakistan
description: The Tomb of Allama Iqbal or Mazar-e-Iqbal is the final resting place of Muhammad Iqbal, the national poet of Pakistan. Designed in the Mughal architectural style, the mausoleum is located next to the walls of the iconic Mughal-era Badshahi Mosque, within the Hazuri Bagh in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan.

name: Shikarpur Historic Falooda & Kulfi Corners
name_ur: شکارپور روایتی فالودہ و قلفی مارکیٹ
short_description: Famous dessert shops serving hand-churned frozen cream Kulfi topped with hand-pressed vermicelli and kewra syrup.
description: Generations-old sweetmasters churn pure buffalo milk over ice and rock salt in wooden casks, serving thick slices of decadent saffron kulfi layered with cooling sev noodles that provide the ultimate summer refreshment.

name: Shikarpur Heritage Merchant Havelis
name_ur: شکارپور تاریخی تاجر حویلیاں و جھروکے
short_description: Opulent 19th-century mansions featuring carved teakwood jharokas, imported Italian floor tiles, and cast iron grilles.
description: Testament to Shikarpur's golden era when its merchants controlled finance houses from London to St. Petersburg, these grand multi-storey mansions boast intricate wooden facades and ornate European ironwork.

name: Umerkot Fort & Emperor Akbar Birthplace
name_ur: عمرکوٹ قلعہ و جائے پیدائش شہنشاہ اکبر
short_description: Historic medieval desert fortress where Mughal Emperor Akbar the Great was born in 1542 during Humayun's exile.
description: Featuring towering mud and brick ramparts, an ancient cannon battery on an elevated bastion, and an imperial memorial pavilion marking the exact birthplace of Emperor Akbar set within the desert citadel.

name: Gadhi Bhit Giant Sand Dune Viewpoint (Mithi)
name_ur: گڈھی بھٹ ریت کا دیوہیکل ٹیلا و ویو پوائنٹ مٹھی تھرپارکر
short_description: The highest natural sand dune in Mithi offering breathtaking 360-degree sunset panoramas across the Thar Desert.
description: Overlooking the peaceful desert capital of Mithi where peacocks roam freely and Hindu-Muslim harmony thrives, visitors climb stone steps to the summit pavilion for cool evening breezes and sweeping dune views.

name: Sant Nenuram Ashram & Langar (Mithi)
name_ur: سنت نینورام آشرم و لنگر مٹھی تھرپارکر
short_description: Historic philanthropic ashram serving free hot vegetarian meals to thousands of travelers and birds daily.
description: A testament to Thar's profound culture of humanitarian service, this serene ashram feeds hundreds of wild peacocks at dawn, maintains shaded guest chambers, and serves continuous hot lentils, roti, and sweets.

name: Khaplu Palace
name_ur: تھوقسی کھر
short_description: Historical fort and palace, now hotel in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan
description: Khaplu Palace, locally known as Yabgo Khar, is an old fort and palace located in Khaplu, a city in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. The palace, considered an architectural heritage site and a significant tourist attraction, was built in the mid-19th century to replace an earlier-dated fort located nearby. It served as a royal residence for the Raja of Khaplu.

name: Ansoo Lake
name_ur: آنسو جھیل
short_description: Notable nature site located in Batakundi.
description: Ansoo Lake,, translated as Teardrop Lake, is situated in the Kaghan Valley of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. As its name suggests, it is a tear-shaped body of water located in Pakistan's Mansehra District.

name: Zaman Park
name_ur: زمان پارک
short_description: Notable park site located in Civil Lines.
description: Zaman Park is a neighborhood in the city of Lahore, Pakistan.

name: Gori Jain Temple (52-Dome Medieval Shrine)
name_ur: گوری جین مندر (52 گنبد والا تاریخی مندر) نگرپارکر
short_description: 1375 CE medieval Jain temple in Thar featuring 52 domed cupolas and ancient Jain fresco paintings on the ceiling.
description: Constructed from local marble and sandstone, Gori Temple is renowned across South Asia for its intricate domed ceilings adorned with 14th-century Jain religious frescoes depicting Tirthankaras and royal processions.

name: Bhodesar Mosque & White Marble Pillars
name_ur: بھوڈیسر مسجد و سفید سنگِ مرمر کے ستون نگرپارکر
short_description: 1505 historic white marble mosque built by Sultan Mahmud Begada of Gujarat at the base of the Karoonjhar hills.
description: Built in 1505 from sparkling white marble salvaged from regional temples, this compact mosque features arched bays, intricately carved pillars, and an adjacent stone water reservoir overlooking the granite cliffs.

name: Sardharo Natural Spring & Shiva Temple
name_ur: سردھارو قدرتی چشمہ و شیو مندر نگرپارکر
short_description: Perennial natural freshwater mountain spring emerging from granite boulders at Karoonjhar, sacred to Lord Shiva.
description: Nestled in a dramatic rocky canyon of the Karoonjhar hills, Sardharo is a major pilgrimage center where devotees bathe in sacred spring waters and perform funeral rites amidst wild peacocks and granite pools.

name: Savoia Glacier
name_ur: ساوُویا گلیشیر
short_description: Glacier in Pakistan
description: Glacier in Pakistan

name: Kasbo Village Desert Oasis & Peacock Sanctuary
name_ur: کاسبو گاؤں نخلستان و موروں کا مسکن نگرپارکر
short_description: Idyllic agricultural desert village bordered by Indian frontier fences where hundreds of wild peacocks roam freely.
description: Known for its sweet underground water aquifers that nourish lush green onion and vegetable patches in the heart of the desert, Kasbo offers magical encounters with wild peacocks calling from neem trees at sunset.

name: Rainbow Lake
name_ur: رینبو جھیل
short_description: Lake in Azad Kashmir, Pakistan
description: Lake in Azad Kashmir, Pakistan

name: Churrio Jabal Durga Mata Hilltop Temple
name_ur: چوڑیوجبل درگا ماتا مندر نگرپارکر
short_description: Spectacular granite hill right on the border crowned by a historic temple dedicated to Hindu Goddess Durga.
description: Named 'Churrio' for the sound of glass bangles, this isolated granite outcrop is mined for premium stone. Pilgrims climb hundreds of steps to the temple sanctum for breathtaking views spanning both Pakistan and India.

name: Shakar Pariyan
name_ur: شکرپریاں
short_description: Park in Islamabad, Pakistan
description: Shakarparian is a hill and a national park located near the Zero Point Interchange in Islamabad, Pakistan. Pakistan Monument and Pakistan Monument Museum are also located in Shakarparian.
image_credit: Ahmed Sajjad Zaidi from Islamabad, Pakistan

name: Shahi Hammam
name_ur: شاہی حمام
short_description: Building in Lahore, Punjab Pakistan
description: The Shahi Hammam, also known as the Wazir Khan Hammam, is a hammam which was built in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan, in 1635 C.E. during the reign of Emperor Shah Jahan. It was built by chief physician to the Mughal Court, Ilam-ud-din Ansari, who was widely known as Wazir Khan. The baths were built to serve as a waqf, or endowment, for the maintenance of the Wazir Khan Mosque.

name: Delhi Gate
name_ur: دہلی گیٹ
short_description: One of the historic gates of the Walled City of Lahore, Pakistan
description: Delhi Gate is one of the six remaining historic gates of the Walled City of Lahore in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan. Delhi Gate and the adjacent Shahi Hammam were restored in 2015 by the Aga Khan Cultural Service Pakistan.

name: Gurdwara Janam Asthan Guru Ram Das
name_ur: گوردوارہ جنم آسھن گرو رام داس
short_description: Gurdwara in Lahore, Pakistan
description: The Janam Asthan Guru Ram Das, also known as Gurdwara Janamasthan Patshahi Chauthi, is a gurdwara in Lahore, Pakistan. The gurdwara was built atop the site traditionally believed to be the location of the birthplace and childhood home of Guru Ram Das, the 4th Sikh guru.
image_credit: The Walled City of Lahore Authority

name: Mansura Ancient Arab Capital Archaeological Ruins
name_ur: منصورہ قدیم عرب دارالحکومت کے آثار سانگھڑ
short_description: Ruins of the legendary 8th-century capital of the Umayyad and Abbasid Caliphates in Sindh, near Shahdadpur.
description: Founded around 730 CE after the conquest of Muhammad bin Qasim, Mansura was a sprawling metropolis of brick mansions, copper coins, and one of the earliest congregational mosques built in South Asia.

name: Chotiari Reservoir & Wetland Wildlife Complex
name_ur: چوٹیاری ریزروائر و قدرتی آبی جھیلیں سانگھڑ
short_description: Vast 18,000-hectare artificial and natural wetland complex bordering the Thar Desert, home to marsh crocodiles.
description: Created by linking natural depressions with the Nara Canal, Chotiari is a critical ecosystem sheltering one of Pakistan's largest populations of indigenous Mugger Crocodiles, hog deer, and wintering waterbirds.

name: Makhi Forest Historic Hur Resistance Sanctuary
name_ur: ماکھی جنگل و حر مجاہدین کی تاریخی پناہ گاہ سانگھڑ
short_description: Dense historic riverine forest and marshland that served as the impregnable base for the anti-colonial Hur uprising.
description: Led by the heroic Pir Sibghatullah Shah Rashdi (Suriyeh Badshah), the Hur fighters fought guerrilla campaigns against the British Empire from deep within the impenetrable thickets of Makhi Forest in the 1940s.

name: Nawabshah Central Jamia Mosque & Clock Tower
name_ur: نواب شاہ مرکزی جامع مسجد و کلاک ٹاور شہید بینظیر آباد
short_description: Sprawling congregational mosque in the center of Nawabshah featuring soaring white minarets and arcaded courtyards.
description: The religious centerpiece of Shaheed Benazirabad district, this grand mosque hosts thousands of worshippers for Friday congregations and Eid prayers, anchoring the city's bustling market square.

name: Old Anarkali Food Street
name_ur: پرانی انارکلی فوڈ اسٹریٹ لاہور
short_description: Bustling pedestrian food haven on Mall Road renowned for karahi, mutton tikka, and falooda.
description: Adjacent to the legendary tomb of Anarkali, this vibrant street comes alive every evening with the scent of charcoal-grilled kebabs, rich butter karahis, and fresh sweet kulfi.

name: Lal Suhanra National Park
name_ur: لال سہانرا قومی پارک
short_description: National park in Punjab, Pakistan
description: Lal Suhanra National Park is a national park in Bahawalpur district of Punjab province in Pakistan. It is one of Pakistan's largest nationals parks, and is a UNESCO declared Biosphere Reserve. Its landscape includes desert, forest and wetland ecosystems.

name: Bhir Mound
name_ur: بھڑ ماونڈ
short_description: Archaeological Site in Taxila, Pakistan
description: The Bhir Mound is an archaeological site in Taxila in the Punjab province of Pakistan. It contains some of the oldest ruins of Ancient Taxila, dated to sometime around the period 800–525 BC as its earliest layers bear "grooved" Red Burnished Ware, the Bhir Mound, along with several other nearby excavations, form part of the Ruins of Taxila – inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.

name: Dharmarajika Stupa
name_ur: دھرم راجک اسٹوپا
short_description: Archaeological site in Punjab, Pakistan
description: The Dharmarajika Stupa, also referred to as the Great Stupa of Taxila, is a Buddhist stupa near Taxila, Pakistan. It was built over the relics of the Buddha by Ashoka, the Emperor of Magadha, in the 3rd century BCE. The stupa, along with the large monastic complex that later developed around it, forms part of the Ruins of Taxila - which were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.

name: Karachi Port Trust (KPT) Head Office
name_ur: کراچی پورٹ ٹرسٹ (کے پی ٹی) ہیڈ آفس
short_description: 1916 Renaissance-style yellow sandstone palace on Eduljee Dinshaw Road with an imposing Roman dome.
description: Designed by George Wittet, this palatial curved edifice features Gizri limestone colonnades, teakwood interior furnishings, and ceremonial boardrooms that guided Karachi's maritime trade for over a century.

name: Katrak Terrace & Parsi Heritage Square
name_ur: کاٹرک ٹیرس و پارسی ورثہ چوک صدر کراچی
short_description: Stately 1920s Parsi residential apartment palace in Saddar with intricate cast iron wrap-around balconies.
description: A landmark of colonial Karachi's cosmopolitan urbanism, Katrak Terrace exhibits elegant colonnaded street facades, wooden shuttered French windows, and period street lighting.

name: Mules Mansion (Keamari Harbour Gateway)
name_ur: میولز مینشن کیماڑی ہاربر گیٹ وے کراچی
short_description: 1917 Renaissance palace at Keamari waterfront named after Sir Charles Mules, first KPT Chairman.
description: Built to greet seafaring passengers arriving at Keamari docks from across the British Empire, Mules Mansion features curved stone arcades, nautical motifs, and corner towers overlooking the ships.

name: Cypress Tomb
name_ur: سرو والا مقبرہ
short_description: Notable park site located in Begampura.
description: Cypress Tomb, also known as Saruwala Maqbara, is an early 18th century tomb located in Begumpura, Lahore, Pakistan.

name: Naulakha Pavilion
name_ur: نولکھا پویلین
short_description: World Heritage Site in Pakistan
description: The Naulakha Pavilion is a white marble personal chamber with a curvilinear roof, located beside the Sheesh Mahal courtyard, in the northern section of the Lahore Fort in Lahore, Pakistan. The monument is one of the 21 monuments situated within the Lahore Fort, with its western façade providing a panoramic view of the old city of Lahore.

name: Alamgiri Gate
name_ur: عالمگیری دروازہ
short_description: Fortified main entrance to Lahore Fort, Pakistan
description: Alamgiri Gate is an entrance of Walled City of Lahore in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan. It was built by Mughal emperor Aurangzeb Alamgir in 1673, when he constructed the Badshahi Mosque. It is the only remaining original entranceway to the mosque and is a main entrance to Lahore Fort. Alamgiri Gate "exemplifies the final flourish of imperial Mughal gateway architecture".

name: Shah Burj Gate
name_ur: شاہ برج دروازہ
short_description: Historic site in Walled City
description: Historic site in Walled City

name: Bhatti Gate
name_ur: بھاٹی دروازه
short_description: One of the historic gates of the Walled City of Lahore, Pakistan
description: Bhati Gate is one of the thirteen historic gates of the Walled City of Lahore in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan. Bhati Gate also serves as a union council located in the Ravi Zone.

name: Chitta Gate
name_ur: چٹا گیٹ
short_description: One of the historic gates of the Walled City of Lahore, Pakistan
description: The Chitta Gate is a gateway located in the Walled City of Lahore in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan, dating back to 1650. The gate was once Lahore's original "Delhi Gate," and the city's main entry point.
image_credit: The Walled City of Lahore Authority

name: Khadda Market Historic Lyari Commercial Spine
name_ur: کھڈا مارکیٹ تاریخی لیاری تجارتی بازار کراچی
short_description: Centuries-old market quarter in Lyari celebrated for fresh sea fish, traditional halwa, and sports gear.
description: One of the earliest settled commercial areas of Karachi, Khadda Market is filled with vibrant community tea stalls, boxing clubs, and bustling fishmongers handling morning hauls from Keamari.

name: Clifton Block 4 Heritage Art District
name_ur: کلفٹن بلاک 4 ہیرٹیج آرٹ ڈسٹرکٹ کراچی
short_description: Charming tree-lined heritage enclave in Old Clifton hosting premier contemporary art galleries and bistros.
description: Home to Mohatta Palace, Koel, Canvas, and Chawkandi galleries, this residential quarter serves as the artistic salon of Pakistan, where curators, diplomats, and painters gather for evening openings.

name: Dhoraji Gola Ganda & Street Dessert Hub
name_ur: دھوراجی گولا گنڈا و اسٹریٹ ڈیزرٹ اسٹریٹ کراچی
short_description: Karachi's celebrated dessert street famous for towering shaved ice Gola Gandas loaded with condensed milk and syrups.
description: A summertime family pilgrimage spot where vendors craft elaborate ice snow cones drenched in rose, blueberry, and chocolate syrups, topped with crushed pineapple, tutty-fruity, and condensed milk.

name: Biarchedi Glacier
name_ur: بیارچڑی گلیشیر
short_description: Glacier in Pakistan
description: The Biarchedi Glacier is located on the northeast of Biarchedi Peak in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. It flows north into the Baltoro Glacier.

name: Baltoro Glacier
name_ur: بالتورو گلیشیر
short_description: Notable nature site located in Shigar District.
description: The Baltoro Glacier is a glacier located in the Shigar District of the Gilgit-Baltistan, a region in Pakistan-administered Kashmir.

name: Bibi Pak Daman
name_ur: بی بی پاک دامن
short_description: Notable historical site located in Civil Lines.
description: Bibi Pak Daman is a shrine dedicated to Ruqayya bint Ali in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan. It is a major pilgrimage site for Shia Muslims. According to Imam Ali Raza Haram Research Centre Iran, the shrine contain the tomb of Ruqayya bint Ali, a daughter of Ali ibn Abi Talib, sister of Abbas ibn Ali and wife of Muslim ibn Aqil. Apart from her, the mausoleum contains the graves of five other ladies, which are said to be Muslim ibn Aqil's sister and daughters. It traditionally claimed that they came to Lahore after the Battle of Karbala in 680.

name: Shrine of Mian Mir
name_ur: درگاہ میاں میر
short_description: Shrine in Lahore, Pakistan
description: The Shrine of Mian Mir is a 17th-century shrine located in Lahore, Pakistan, that is dedicated to the Sufi mystic Mian Mir. The shrine is one of the most celebrated in Lahore, and has historically been revered by both Muslims and Sikhs.

name: Shab Bhar
name_ur: مسجد شب بھر
short_description: Mosque in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan
description: The Shab Bhar Mosque is a colonial era mosque in the Shah Alami neighbourhood of Lahore, Pakistan. The mosque is said to have been built overnight, following a dispute between local Hindus and Muslims in 1917.

name: Wazir Mansion

short_description: Museum in Lyari
description: Museum in Lyari

name_ur: کیماڑی ہاربر بوٹ بیسن و کریبنگ جیٹی کراچی
short_description: Bustling coastal boat basin where colorful wooden launches depart for Manora Island and night crabbing cruises.
description: The gateway to Karachi's maritime waterways, Keamari offers thrilling sea voyages on diesel launches where boat crews cook freshly caught crabs and prawns in fiery masala on charcoal stoves onboard.

name: Creek Marina Promenade (DHA Phase 8)
name_ur: کریک مرینا پرومیناڈ ڈی ایچ اے فیز 8 کراچی
short_description: Ultra-modern waterfront boardwalk along the tidal creek overlooking private yachts and coastal mangroves.
description: Offering refreshing marine breezes, pristine landscaped paths, and upscale coffee kiosks, Creek Marina provides a serene contemporary counterpoint to Karachi's bustling urban core.

name: Memon Masjid (M.A. Jinnah Road)
name_ur: میمن مسجد ایم اے جناح روڈ کراچی
short_description: Historic congregational mosque on Bunder Road accommodating 10,000 worshippers under grand sandstone domes.
description: Constructed in classical Mughal style from Gizri yellow sandstone, Memon Masjid is an architectural landmark of Old Karachi, famous for its majestic minarets, marble ablution pools, and Eid gatherings.

name: Fatima Jinnah Park
name_ur: فاطمہ جناح پارک
short_description: Public recreational park in Islamabad, Pakistan
description: Fatima Jinnah Park, also known as Capital Park or F-9 Park, is a public recreational park that spans the whole of Sector F-9 of Islamabad, Pakistan. It is named after Mādar-e Millat Fatima Jinnah, the younger sister of the founder of Pakistan Muhammad Ali Jinnah. The park is administered by the Environment Wing of Capital Development Authority (CDA).

name: Rawat Fort
name_ur: قلعہ روات
short_description: 16th century fort in Rawalpindi, Pakistan
description: 16th century fort in Rawalpindi, Pakistan

name: Bahawalpur Zoo
name_ur: بہاولپور چڑیا گھر
short_description: Zoo in Bahawalpur, Pakistan
description: Bahawalpur Zoo, established in 1942, is a 10-hectare (25-acre) zoological garden in Bahawalpur, Punjab, Pakistan. It is managed by the Government of Pakistan.

name: Grand Jamia Mosque
name_ur: گرینڈ جامع مسجد
short_description: Notable religious site located in Chung.
description: Grand Jamia Mosque Lahore is a mosque located in Bahria Town, Lahore, Pakistan. With a capacity of 70,000 worshippers, it is the third largest mosque in Pakistan and the fourteenth largest mosque in the world.

name: Gurdwara Sri Darbar Sahib
name_ur: گردوارہ سری دربار صاحب
short_description: Sikh gurdwara in Kartarpur, Pakistan
description: Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur, also called Kartarpur Sahib, is a gurdwara in Kartarpur, Punjab, Pakistan. Kartarpur, a small town beside the Ravi River in the Shakargarh Tehsil of Narowal District, stands on the historic site where Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, settled and assembled the Sikh community after his missionary travels. Nanak lived there for 18 years until his death in 1539. It is one of the holiest sites in Sikhism.

name: Army Museum
name_ur: پاکستان آرمی میوزیم راولپنڈی
short_description: Museum in Rawalpindi
description: Museum in Rawalpindi

name: New Challi Historic Financial & Cotton Quarter
name_ur: نیو چالی تاریخی کاٹن ایکسچینج و فنانشل کوارٹر کراچی
short_description: Pakistan's historic commodity finance and cotton brokering district lined with 1930s colonial banking arcades.
description: Adjacent to I.I. Chundrigar Road, New Challi is packed with cotton merchants, tea clearing houses, and heritage stone chambers that laid the financial foundations of newly independent Pakistan.

name: Delhi Rabri House (Burns Road)
name_ur: دہلی ربڑی ہاؤس برنز روڈ کراچی
short_description: Legendary dessert house serving rich, layered sweet clotted cream Rabri in traditional terracotta bowls since 1948.
description: Slowly simmering fresh whole milk in massive iron cauldrons for eight hours, Delhi Rabri House creates thick, caramelized cream sheets flavored with green cardamom and crushed pistachios.

name: Ayubia National Park
name_ur: ایوبیہ قومی پارک
short_description: National park in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
description:
Ayubia National Park, also known as Ayubia, is a protected area of 3,312 hectares (33 km2) located in Abbottabad District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan. It was declared a national park in 1984. Ayubia was named after Muhammad Ayub Khan (1958–1969), second President of Pakistan. The area supports temperate coniferous forest and temperate broadleaf and mixed forest ecoregion habitats, with an average elevation of 2,400 metres (8,000 ft) above sea level.
Ayubia National Park is surrounded by seven major villages and three small towns of Thandiani, Nathiagali and Khanspur. The park has been developed as a resort complex from a combination of four mini resorts of Khaira Gali, Changla Gali, Khanspur and Ghora Dhaka in Galyat. Currently, it is managed by the Wildlife and Parks Department of Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

name: Shrine Complex of Shah Shams Sabzwari
name_ur: مزار شاہ شمس سبزواری
short_description: Tomb in Multan, Pakistan
description: Tomb in Multan, Pakistan

name: Well of Raja Dina Nath
name_ur: کنواں دینا ناتھ
short_description: Building in Lahore, India
description: The Well of Dina Nath was intended to be a water well in the Wazir Khan Chowk in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan. The well's construction in the 19th century by a Sikh nobleman sparked controversy, given its location in the immediate vicinity of the Wazir Khan Mosque.

name: Gurdwara Dera Sahib
name_ur: گوردوارہ ڈیرا صاحب
short_description: Sikh Gurudwara in Lahore
description: Gurdwara Dera Sahib, also known as Gurdwara Dera Sahib Patshahi Panjvin, is a gurdwara in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan, which commemorates the spot where the 5th guru of Sikhism, Guru Arjan Dev, was martyred in 1606.

name: Lohari Gate
name_ur: لوہاری دروازہ
short_description: One of the historic gates of the Walled City of Lahore, Pakistan
description: The Lahori Gate, also known as Lohari Gate, is one of the 13 gates located within the Walled City of Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan.

name: Karachi Press Club & Democratic Square
name_ur: کراچی پریس کلب و جمہوری چوک
short_description: Historic 1890s stone bungalow in Saddar serving as the legendary vanguard of press freedom and civil rights.
description: Known as Pakistan's 'Hyde Park', the pavement outside the Karachi Press Club has hosted peaceful protests, labor rights demonstrations, and political debates for over six decades.

name: Sindh High Court Colonial Palace of Justice
name_ur: سندھ ہائی کورٹ تاریخی عدالتِ عالیہ کراچی
short_description: 1929 Neo-Renaissance sandstone judicial palace in Civil Lines designed by consulting architect Walter Fletcher.
description: Built from golden Gizri limestone, this majestic courthouse features imposing Corinthian columns, a central cupola dome, and grand teakwood courtrooms steeped in landmark constitutional trials.

name: Karachi City Railway Station (McLeod Road)
name_ur: کراچی سٹی ریلوے اسٹیشن (میکلوڈ روڈ)
short_description: Pakistan's oldest operational railway terminal opened in 1861 connecting the port to Kotri.
description: The starting point of the Scinde Railway in 1861, this heritage sandstone station features historic iron canopy platforms, British semaphore signals, and early locomotive heritage.

name: Izmis Lake
name_ur: ازمس جھیل
short_description: Lake in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
description: Izmis Lake is a lake in Swat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, located to the south-west of Utror valley at a high altitude above the treeline. The name Izmis means "caves" in Kohistani, and as the lake is surrounded by several natural caves, the people have named the lake after these caves. A small jeep-able link road from Utror leads part of the way to the lake, ending in a valley called Loypanrghalay. The lake can be accessed from here after trekking for almost 3–6 hours.

name: Omar Hayat Mahal
name_ur: عمر حیات محل
short_description: Haveli mansion in Chiniot, Pakistan
description: Omar Hayat Mahal, also spelt Umer Hayat Mahal, and alternatively known as Gulzar Manzil, is an early 20th-century wooden haveli mansion in Chiniot, Pakistan.

name: Shrine of Shah Aqeeq Bukhari
name_ur: شاہ عقیق بابا
short_description: Sufi saint
description: Syed Asghar Ali Shah Bukhari, also known as Shah Yaqeeq Baba and Roohani Surgeon, was a Muslim saint from Sindh. Shah Yaqeeq's ‘urs is held in the town of Shah Yaqeeq near Thatta. His Suhrawardi shrine there is regarded as a place of miraculous healing from various ailments.

name: Arts Council of Pakistan Karachi
name_ur: آرٹس کونسل آف پاکستان کراچی
short_description: Organization in Karachi, Pakistan
description: The Arts Council of Pakistan, Karachi, abbreviated as ACPKHI, is a non-profit organisation in Karachi, Pakistan, dedicated to the promotion of performing and fine arts. Its activities include theatre productions, dance and music academies, literary conferences, talent competitions, and other cultural events. The council's programmes are intended to be accessible to a broad range of audiences and of diverse segments of society.

name: Burns Garden (National Museum Grounds)
name_ur: برنز گارڈن و نیشنل میوزیم گراؤنڈز کراچی
short_description: Peaceful 25-acre colonial park in Old Town surrounding the National Museum of Pakistan.
description: Named after 19th-century traveler and diplomat Dr. James Burnes, this park features mature mahogany and neem groves, shaded walking paths, and historic stone pavilions.

name: Victoria Clock Tower Jacobabad
name_ur: وکٹوریہ کلاک ٹاور جیکب آباد
short_description: 1887 Victorian Gothic limestone clock tower erected to commemorate Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee.
description: Designed by Col. S.S. Jacob, this elegant stone tower stands prominently in the center of Jacobabad, rising above shaded avenues that General John Jacob engineered in the 1850s.

name: Lakshmi Chowk (Nisbat Road Food)
name_ur: لکشمی چوک فوڈ بازار لاہور
short_description: Historic cinematic crossroads famous for Nishat Cafe, tawa chicken, and karahi.
description: Once the epicenter of pre-partition Lollywood cinema palaces, Lakshmi Chowk is equally legendary for Butt Karahi, spicy tawa chicken, and round-the-clock Lahori street dining.

name: General John Jacob Residency & Memorial
name_ur: جنرل جان جیکب ریزیڈنسی و یادگار جیکب آباد
short_description: 1847 fortified colonial residency of the founder of Jacobabad, housing antique military relics and maps.
description: Surrounded by deep cool verandas designed to survive extreme summer temperatures exceeding 50 degrees Celsius, this historic residency preserves the tomb and personal quarters of the administrator of Upper Sindh.

name: Jacobabad Historic Shahi Bazaar
name_ur: جیکب آباد تاریخی شاہی بازار و غلہ منڈی
short_description: Major transit wholesale market connecting northern Sindh, Balochistan, and southern Punjab.
description: Bustling with traders dealing in aromatic rice, Balochi carpets, and dry fruits, this historic bazaar reflects Jacobabad's role as the commercial gateway to the Bolan Pass.

name: Guddu Barrage Indus Dolphin Sanctuary
name_ur: گڈو بیراج انڈس ڈولفن پناہ گاہ کشمور
short_description: 1962 monumental Indus River barrage sheltering the endangered blind Indus River Dolphin (Bhulan).
description: Spanning 64 sluice bays across the mighty Indus River, Guddu Barrage is a critical sanctuary where travelers can spot the rare blind Indus dolphin surfacing for air in the swirling river currents.

name: Kandhkot Historic Grain & Timber Mandi
name_ur: کندھ کوٹ تاریخی غلہ و لکڑی منڈی کشمور
short_description: Centuries-old agricultural hub on the right bank of the Indus famed for bumper wheat and rice auctions.
description: Serving as the market crossroads between the Kirthar foothills and the Indus plains, Kandhkot trades vast volumes of grain, livestock, and hand-woven tribal carpets.

name: Dargah Bharchundi Sharif (Ghotki)
name_ur: درگاہ بھرچونڈی شریف گھوٹکی
short_description: Historic Sufi shrine and Islamic seminary of Hazrat Pir Abdul Rehman, renowned for spiritual welfare.
description: A cornerstone of spiritual life in northern Sindh, Bharchundi Sharif draws thousands of devotees for its commitment to Islamic scholarship, peaceful dispute mediation, and religious gatherings.

name: Mathelo Fort Ancient Archaeological Citadel
name_ur: ماتھیلو قلعہ قدیم آثار و کھنڈرات میرپور ماتھیلو
short_description: Pre-Islamic high fortified mound dating back to the Rai Dynasty of Sindh mentioned in the Chachnama.
description: Rising steeply above surrounding agricultural plains, this ancient mound holds layers of pottery, burnt brick battlements, and folklore from the earliest recorded dynasties of Sindh.

name: Salehpat Desert Safari Gateway (Nara Desert)
name_ur: صالح پٹ صحرائی سفاری گیٹ وے (نارا صحرا) سکھر
short_description: Strategic gateway town where the irrigated Indus plains meet the golden wilderness of the Nara Desert.
description: The launching point for desert 4x4 expeditions into the historic Rohri flint hills and Nara Canal wetlands, Salehpat offers rugged desert vistas and star-filled night skies.

name: Arain Road Historic Fruit & Guava Orchards
name_ur: ارائیں روڈ تاریخی فروٹ و امرود باغات سکھر
short_description: Lush agricultural green belt on the northern outskirts of Sukkur famed for sweet seedless guavas.
description: Fed by canals from the Sukkur Barrage, Arain Road produces Sindh's finest winter guavas and pomegranates, providing cool shady walking orchards just minutes from the city center.

name: Pano Aqil Military Cantonment Oasis
name_ur: پنو عاقل ملٹری چھاؤنی نخلستان سکھر
short_description: One of Pakistan's premier modern military cantonments nestled within a lush green forest oasis.
description: A marvel of environmental afforestation, Pano Aqil transformed arid scrubland into a meticulously planned township of hundreds of thousands of planted neem trees, parks, and parade grounds.

name: Mirpur Mathelo Industrial Green Oasis
name_ur: میرپور ماتھیلو صنعتی نخلستان و باغات گھوٹکی
short_description: Ultra-modern agro-chemical industrial township renowned for extensive landscaped rose parks and lakes.
description: Home to Pakistan's largest urea chemical plants (FFC), this planned industrial enclave features world-class employee housing colonies, schools, and lush botanical gardens in northern Sindh.

name: Daharki Inter-Faith Peace & Sufi Enclave
name_ur: ڈہرکی بین المذاہب امن و صوفی آستانہ گھوٹکی
short_description: Spiritual crossroads town in eastern Ghotki where Hindu ashrams and Sufi hospices foster communal harmony.
description: A testament to the enduring pluralism of rural Sindh, Daharki brings together diverse communities for inter-faith feasts, free medical aid, and shared spiritual celebrations.

name: Ubauro Frontier Canal Head & Regulators
name_ur: اوباڑو سرحدی نہری ہیڈ و ریگولیٹرز گھوٹکی
short_description: Strategic irrigation crossing point near the Punjab boundary distributing water to northern agricultural tracts.
description: Flanked by towering deodar trees and historic British water gauges, Ubauro commands views of sweeping cotton and wheat fields right at the tri-provincial frontier.

name: Reti Historic Colonial Railway Junction
name_ur: ریتی تاریخی نوآبادیاتی ریلوے جنکشن گھوٹکی
short_description: Historic red-brick frontier railway station that served as an early military and troop marshaling depot.
description: Preserving massive iron overhead pedestrian bridges, manual signal boxes, and historic water towers, Reti is a classic surviving relic of late 19th-century railway architecture.

name: Khanpur Mahar Historic Shrines & Mango Groves
name_ur: خانپور مہر تاریخی درگاہیں و آم کے باغات گھوٹکی
short_description: Tribal ancestral center of the Mahar clan holding historic Sufi shrines and vast mango plantations.
description: Surrounded by rich agricultural fields, Khanpur Mahar is famous for tribal hospitality, historic wrestling arenas, and communal mediation gatherings.

name: Adilpur Historic Date & Grain Market
name_ur: عادل پور تاریخی کھجور و غلہ منڈی گھوٹکی
short_description: Ancient market town renowned for early-season fresh date varieties and organic raw cane brown sugar (gur).
description: Lined with traditional wood-fired sugarcane boiling pans (karhaos), Adilpur fills with sweet aromas during winter cane crushing, drawing buyers from Sukkur and Multan.

name: Sultan Kot Historic Caravanserai & Bazaar
name_ur: سلطان کوٹ تاریخی کاروان سرائے و بازار شکارپور
short_description: Historic staging post on the ancient caravan highway between Shikarpur and Jacobabad.
description: Preserving old brick shops, traditional blacksmith ateliers, and tea houses, Sultan Kot still serves rural farming communities trading wheat, rice, and handmade metal farming tools.

name: Khanpur Historic Canal Headworks & Falls
name_ur: خانپور تاریخی نہری ہیڈ ورکس و واٹر فال شکارپور
short_description: Scenic brick water regulator on the Shikarpur canal command providing family bathing spots.
description: Shaded by dense shisham and acacia trees, the foaming water chutes of Khanpur regulator provide a cool summer refuge where locals swim and enjoy sweet seasonal watermelons.

name: Madeji Historic Railway Town & Rice Mills
name_ur: مادیجی تاریخی ریلوے ٹاؤن و چاول فیکٹریز شکارپور
short_description: Southern railhead market of Shikarpur district holding major rice husking and storage plants.
description: Connecting the rice plains of Larkana to the wholesale ports of Karachi, Madeji is a bustling commercial center filled with grain brokers and local street food stalls.

name: Dokri Rice Research Institute & Orchards
name_ur: ڈوکری رائس ریسرچ انسٹیٹیوٹ و باغات لاڑکانہ
short_description: Premier national agricultural research institute that developed world-renowned high-yield Basmati rice.
description: Spanning expansive experimental paddy fields near Mohenjo-daro, Dokri conducts cutting-edge agronomic trials, training agriculturalists and safeguarding indigenous Indus rice genetics.

name: Bakrani Historic Guava & Citrus Belt
name_ur: باقرانی تاریخی امرود و لیموں باغات لاڑکانہ
short_description: Legendary horticultural garden township producing Larkana's famous seedless pink-flesh guavas.
description: Fed by fresh canal distributaries from the Dadu canal, Bakrani's sweet fruit orchards yield hundreds of tons of sweet, fragrant guavas packed in wicker baskets daily.

name: Ratodero Historic Sweets & Mawa Bazaar
name_ur: رتو ڈیرو روایتی ماوا و مٹھائی بازار لاڑکانہ
short_description: Famous culinary town in northern Larkana celebrated across Pakistan for rich buffalo milk Mawa sweets.
description: Generations of sweetmasters boil pure buffalo milk in giant copper vats until it thickens into rich, golden caramelized fudge (Mawa), served fresh to travelers day and night.

name: Mirokhan Grain & Paddy Auction Mandi
name_ur: میرو خان غلہ و دھان نیلامی منڈی قمبر
short_description: Vibrant agricultural market town in Qambar-Shahdadkot district surrounded by endless rice fields.
description: A bustling commerce center connecting rural farming villages to major road corridors, Mirokhan auctions vast quantities of premium rice, mustard seeds, and winter lentils.

name: Nasirabad Rice Mills & Canal Basin
name_ur: نصیر آباد چاول فیکٹریز و کینال بیسن قمبر
short_description: Key processing capital of superior non-basmati rice on the Rice Canal in western Larkana basin.
description: Located in the heart of Sindh's flood-irrigated rice bowl, Nasirabad is famous for its towering grain processing plants, traditional bazaars, and scenic canal regulators.

name: Warah Historic Desert Fringe Town
name_ur: وارہ تاریخی صحرائی سرحدی قصبہ قمبر
short_description: Ancient market outpost where the irrigated green fields of Qambar end and the arid Kirthar desert begins.
description: Preserving traditional mud-brick havelis, camel rest houses, and handicraft markets, Warah represents the resilient frontier culture of western Sindh.

name: Thul Historic Grain & Rice Complex
name_ur: ٹھل تاریخی غلہ و چاول کمپلیکس جیکب آباد
short_description: Premier grain auction market of Jacobabad district commanding vast rice and wheat command areas.
description: Intersected by the Begari canal network, Thul is a vibrant trading town bustling with wholesale grain brokers, tractor dealerships, and traditional Sindhi sweet stalls.

name: Garhi Khairo Ancient Canal Crossing
name_ur: گڑھی خیرو تاریخی نہری کراسنگ جیکب آباد
short_description: Historic frontier town on the boundary of Sindh and Balochistan known for canal headworks.
description: Guarding the irrigation routes feeding the Shahdadkot plains, Garhi Khairo features traditional brick residences, bustling weekly bazaars, and peaceful date palm orchards.

name: Shahi Guzargah (Royal Trail Lahore)
name_ur: شاہی گزرگاہ (رائل ٹریل) لاہور
short_description: Historic Mughal procession route connecting Delhi Gate to Lahore Fort via Wazir Khan Mosque.
description: The Shahi Guzargah was the imperial ceremonial street used by Mughal emperors arriving from Delhi. Carefully restored by the Walled City Authority, it features historic baths, spice bazaars, and frescoed havelis.

name: Tomb of Empress Nur Jahan
name_ur: مقبرہ ملکہ نور جہاں شاہدرہ لاہور
short_description: 1645 CE marble-faced mausoleum of the powerful Mughal Empress Nur Jahan in Shahdara.
description: Designed by the empress herself, this red-brick and marble tomb features floral frescoes and honeycombed ceilings. Her epitaph famously reads: 'On our grave, let neither lamp nor rose bloom.'

name: Tomb of Asif Khan (Shahdara)
name_ur: مقبرہ آصف خان شاہدرہ لاہور
short_description: 1645 CE monumental octagonal tomb of Emperor Shah Jahan's prime minister, crowned with a high bulbous dome.
description: Adjoining the tomb of Jahangir, this vast octagonal monument was encrusted with fine marble and Persian tile mosaics before its stone was appropriated during Sikh rule.

name: Shrine of Madho Lal Hussain (Mela Chiraghan)
name_ur: مزار شاہ حسین و مادھو لال (میلہ چراغاں)
short_description: 16th-century Sufi poet shrine near Shalimar Gardens, famous for the annual Festival of Lights (Mela Chiraghan).
description: Dedicated to Punjabi Sufi poet Shah Hussain and his devoted Hindu companion Madho, this shrine hosts the vibrant Mela Chiraghan where thousands light candles and bonfire flames in ecstatic devotion.

name: Multan Fort & Qasim Bagh Damdama
name_ur: قلعہ ملتان و قاسم باغ دمدمہ
short_description: Ancient 2,500-year-old citadel mound rising over Multan with panoramic views from the Damdama.
description: Perched on a high alluvial mound, Multan Fort was besieged by Alexander the Great in 326 BCE and later by the British in 1849. It houses the magnificent shrines of Rukn-e-Alam and Zakariya.

name: Shrine of Shah Ali Akbar (Little Rukn-e-Alam)
name_ur: مزار شاہ علی اکبر (چھوٹا رکنِ عالم) ملتان
short_description: 1585 CE architectural miniature of Shah Rukn-e-Alam with dazzling blue Multani faience tiles.
description: Built in the Suri period, this octagonal brick mausoleum in Suraj Miani replicates the iconic architecture of Shah Rukn-e-Alam with intricate glazed cobalt blue tilework.

name: Multan Clock Tower (Ghanta Ghar)
name_ur: گھنٹہ گھر ملتان
short_description: 1884 Victorian Indo-Saracenic clock tower in central Multan, now housing the Multan Museum.
description: Constructed during British rule in 1884 to celebrate Queen Victoria's reign, this brick and sandstone municipal palace features high clock dials and regional archaeological galleries.

name: Hussain Agahi Bazaar Multan
name_ur: حسین آگاہی بازار ملتان
short_description: Ancient bazaar famous for authentic Multani Sohan Halwa, blue pottery, and camel-skin lamps.
description: The vibrant heartbeat of old Multan shopping. Sweetmakers stir boiling copper vats of Hafiz Sohan Halwa as craft stalls display handcrafted cobalt Kashikari plates and embroidered khussas.

name: Darbar Mahal
name_ur: دربار محل بہاولپور
short_description: 1905 CE red-brick royal court palace of the Nawabs of Bahawalpur in Indo-Saracenic style.
description: Commissioned by Nawab Bahawal Khan V, Darbar Mahal features 80 rooms, exquisite marble balconies, Mughal domes, and sprawling lawns used for state durbars and royal receptions.

name: Gulzar Mahal
name_ur: گلزار محل بہاولپور
short_description: Stately 1906 royal palace in Bahawalpur blending Italian neoclassical and Mughal architecture.
description: Built for the royal queens of Bahawalpur, Gulzar Mahal was the first palace in the princely state equipped with electric lighting and imported chandeliers.

name: Central Library Bahawalpur
name_ur: سینٹرل لائبریری بہاولپور
short_description: 1924 Victorian Gothic public library housing over 100,000 rare manuscripts and books.
description: One of the premier research libraries in Pakistan, founded by the Nawabs of Bahawalpur. Its distinctive clock tower and arched reading halls preserve centuries of rare Islamic texts.

name: Mojgarh Fort (Cholistan Desert)
name_ur: قلعہ موج گڑھ صحرائے چولستان
short_description: 1743 CE ruined desert fortress in Cholistan built from burnt brick with an ornamental mosque.
description: Part of the legendary chain of desert citadels guarding the ancient Hakra River valley, Mojgarh features high battlements and the ruined blue-tiled tomb of its founder, Maruf Khan Kehrani.

name: Khewra Salt Mine Tourist Resort
name_ur: کھیوڑا نمک کی کان سیاحتی مقام
short_description: World's second-largest salt mine, operating since 320 BCE with carved underground salt mosques and illuminated tunnels.
description: Discovered by Alexander the Great's army in 320 BCE, Khewra features 17 levels of subterranean salt caverns. Visitors ride a vintage electric train into illuminated halls with a salt-brick replica of Minar-e-Pakistan and Badshahi Mosque.

name: Malot Temple & Fort (Salt Range)
name_ur: ملوٹ مندر و قلعہ سالٹ رینج
short_description: 10th-century Kashmiri-Greek style sandstone temple perched on a dramatic cliff in the Salt Range.
description: Built by the Hindu Shahi kings in the 900s, Malot combines Greek Doric fluted columns with Kashmiri temple spires on a sheer precipice commanding sweeping views over the Jhelum plains.

name: Nandana Fort (Al-Biruni Earth Measurement Site)
name_ur: قلعہ نندنہ (البیرونی سائنسی مقام)
short_description: Ancient hill fort where polymath Al-Biruni calculated the Earth's circumference in 1023 CE.
description: Guarding a vital pass through the Salt Range, Nandana was captured by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1014. Here, Persian scholar Al-Biruni used trigonometric calculations from the hill summit to compute Earth's radius with 99% accuracy.

name: Tilla Jogian Monastic Sanctuary
name_ur: ٹلہ جوگیاں تاریخی خانقاہ سالٹ رینج
short_description: 3,000-year-old mountain monastery at 3,200 feet, sacred heart of the Kanphata Yogi order and Waris Shah's Heer.
description: The highest peak in the eastern Salt Range, Tilla Jogian was founded around the 1st century BCE as the supreme monastery of Guru Gorakhnath's jogis. Waris Shah immortalized it as the sanctuary where Ranjha took yogic vows.

name: Haveli Sujan Singh
name_ur: حویلی سوجان سنگھ راولپنڈی
short_description: Opulent 1893 multi-storey timber and brick Sikh haveli in Bhabra Bazaar.
description: Built by wealthy timber magnate Rai Bahadur Sujan Singh, this magnificent mansion features iron staircases, painted ceilings, and carved teak jharokas illustrating pre-partition Rawalpindi's grandeur.

name: Shrine of Baba Bulleh Shah
name_ur: مزار حضرت بابا بلھے شاہ قصور
short_description: Venerated 18th-century shrine of Punjab's immortal Sufi poet of defiance and divine love in Kasur.
description: Bulleh Shah (1680–1757) challenged social hierarchy and religious orthodoxy through ecstatic Punjabi Kafi poetry. His shrine in Kasur is a sanctuary for music, qawwali, and free food.

name: Shahi Hammam (Royal Bathhouse Lahore)
name_ur: شاہی حمام اندرون لاہور
short_description: 1635 Mughal royal bathhouse near Delhi Gate featuring restored frescoes, cold plunge pools, and hypocaust heating.
description: Constructed in 1635 by court physician Ilam-ud-Din Ansari (Wazir Khan), this UNESCO-recognized bathhouse preserves the only surviving Turkish-style steam bath of the Mughal era in South Asia.

name: Chauburji Monument & Mughal Gardens
name_ur: چوبرجی تاریخی یادگار و مغل باغات لاہور
short_description: 1646 monumental four-minaret Mughal gateway adorned with vibrant glazed mosaic tiles on Multan Road.
description: Built as the ornamental gateway to an expansive lost pleasure garden for Princess Zeb-un-Nissa, Chauburji features blue-and-yellow glazed ceramic mosaic calligraphy and elegant corner minarets.

name: Kamran's Baradari (Ravi River Island)
name_ur: کامران کی بارہ دری دریائے راوی لاہور
short_description: 1540 historic 12-door pleasure pavilion on an island in the Ravi River, Lahore's oldest Mughal structure.
description: Constructed by Prince Kamran Mirza, son of Emperor Babur, this garden retreat features arched stone loggias, fountain pools, and scenic riverboat access from the Ravi banks.

name: Dai Anga Mosque (Railway Station)
name_ur: دائی انگہ مسجد ریلوے اسٹیشن لاہور
short_description: 1635 grand Mughal mosque near Lahore Railway Station adorned with rich Persian glazed tile mosaics.
description: Built by Zeb-un-Nisa, the wet-nurse of Emperor Shah Jahan, this compact brick mosque features ribbed bulbous domes, tall corner minarets, and museum-grade floral tilework.

name: Mariam Zamani Begum Mosque (Begum Shahi Mosque)
name_ur: مریم زمانی بیگم مسجد (بیگم شاہی مسجد) لاہور
